title: Business Issues in Biotechnology Enterprises
school: College of Medicine and Public Health
syllabus_overview:
This topic within the MBA (Biotechnology) programme encourages participants to not only challenge the paradigms with which business development and commercialization are envisaged to interact with research in biotechnology and the life sciences, but to also gain a firm grasp of why and how to integrate the complexities of planning and operations from both research and business viewpoints. This topic will give students a comprehensive understanding of the commercialisation and business development skills required to manage a modern innovation-intensive enterprise. Specific aims and objectives are to: Develop a strong understanding of Intellectual Property (IP) management for a biotechnology enterprise Gain professional skills in Licencing, Drafting contracts and making deals in the Life Sciences sector Learn how to manage technology commercialization and Research and Development portfolios Gain skills in strategic financing and valuations Develop professional communication and leadership skills

This topic will cover the underlying business principles and methodologies and strategic insight for successful management of the commercial Biotechnology and Life Sciences sector. It will provide the strategic directions and business development issues in the biotechnology industry with an emphasis on commercialization of new products.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply the key components of strategic financing for the different stages of company and product development
Undertake valuations of biotechnology products or services
Manage technology transfer and product development portfolios
Negotiate deals and licence technologies in an innovation-intensive industry
Demonstrate teamwork and leadership attributes
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBA-Master of Business Administration 1a Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Integrated Research Experience
school: College of Medicine and Public Health
syllabus_overview:
This topic provides students with an authentic, immersive research experience, enabling them to apply and refine core scientific skills in a collaborative, inquiry driven environment. Through the design and execution of a team-based research project, students will strengthen their abilities in experimental design, data analysis, scientific communication, and project management. The experience is designed to foster critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork, and practical research competencies essential for future careers in biotechnology, biomedical sciences and related interdisciplinary fields.

This topic equips students with the practical, analytical and professional skills required for success essential for success in biotechnology research and development. Working in collaborative teams, students will design and carry out a substantial research project that addresses a real-world scientific or industry-relevant question. Through this process, they will individually gain hands-on experience in experimental design, data collection and analysis, and the interpretation and communication of results.
learning_outcomes: Defend scientific findings through effective communication utilizing both written and oral formats to appropriate academic and professional audiences
Apply advanced laboratory and data management skills, maintaining rigorous documentation and ethical standards

Demonstrate professional teamwork capabilities by contributing effectively to collaborative research, applying communication and interpersonal strategies, and reflecting on team processes to enhance future practice
Critically evaluate scientific literature to inform the design of experiments and the interpretation of complex data, drawing evidence-based conclusions
Independently analyse scientific problems and apply advanced methodologies to develop, implement, and evaluate research solutions within defined timelines
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBTL-Master of Biotechnology 2 36 units of topics Must satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Biotechnology Research Project (13.5/27 units)
school: College of Medicine and Public Health
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students the opportunity to spend two semesters working on a research project in a specialised area of biotechnology. This develops graduate skills by demonstrating ability to work in a research environment to solve complex problems for the economic and social benefit of society Provide experience in experimental design, critical analysis of scientific data management, advanced technical skills, and use of state-of the art equipment Provide students the opportunity to write a graduate thesis and present oral presentations at a professional level The skills and experience gained in the topic should enable the Masters graduates to function in an interdisciplinary, global, research intensive biotechnology industry.

This topic comprises a major research project in which the student is required to engage in individually supervised research, presenting results in the form of a postgraduate level thesis and seminar presentations. It is expected that this work will be conducted in the research laboratories in the College of Medicine and Public Health, Flinders University, or in conjunction with other suitable laboratories for which relevant and adequate facilities and immediate supervision exists, either in academia, research institutes or industry. All areas of contemporary biotechnology are open, with the research including any bioscience activity which is either fundamental in nature, or more applied, and having distinct economic or social objectives.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to carry out experimental design, critical analysis of scientific data, project management, advanced technical skills, and use of state-of the art equipment
Prepare a postgraduate level thesis and deliver professional oral presentations
Demonstrate the ability to work in a research environment in an independent manner

title: Pre-Masters Business
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to cultivate student’s understanding of the learning environment at Flinders University and the expectations of tertiary education in Australia. Throughout this topic, students will engage in hands on learning to develop academic English and be introduced to foundation concepts in preparation for progressing to a Business Masters course. During the topic, students will interact with international students and be presented with opportunities to join other students in social events, through university student associations, gaining an appreciation for Australian culture and way of life.

The Pre-Masters Program is a 7 week intensive course for international students to develop key business knowledge, language and academic skills in the context of an Australian university as a foundation for Flinders Business Masters programs.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate foundation knowledge in core business topics including accounting, economics, management and marketing
Appraise Australian culture and environment
Determine the learning requirements of tertiary education in the context of an Australian University
Illustrate the academic and English language skills required to succeed in a Business Masters course
Develop connections with international and local students
prerequisites: Admission into PMPBUSNFP-Pre-Masters Program - Business - Flinders City Campus

title: Recording Business Transactions
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the technical aspects of recording and reporting accounting information in the context of a sole trader. It introduces the accounting cycle, the rules of debit and credit, double-entry accrual-based accounting and the need for adjusting and closing entries. The topic also includes how to account for the transactions of a retail business, cash management and control, receivables, inventory systems and the preparation of straightforward financial statements.

This topic is designed to introduce the nature of accounting, its main functions, and its role in the decision-making process of business entities. It aims to provide a solid grounding in accounting fundamentals.
learning_outcomes: Appraise information for retailing transactions, inventory systems and bank reconciliations
Determine the role and purpose of financial accounting and financial statements
Analyse and record business transactions using double entry accounting for a sole trader
Construct financial statements

school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce the objectives of financial reporting and the definitions and recognition criteria of the elements of financial statements. It accounts for more complex transactions and forms of business organisations, including partnerships, non-current assets, liabilities as well as the preparation and presentation of financial reports.

Exploring Accounting Processes is designed to develop knowledge of the nature of accounting, its main functions, and its role in the decision-making process of business entities. It considers the application of accounting standards and practical issues in financial reporting.
learning_outcomes: Construct a range of financial statements
Assess the application of a range of accounting principles to specified cases and transactions
Analyse and record business transactions for a partnership

title: Finance and Accounting for Leaders
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to provide students with an understanding of financial information that drives business planning and strategy for internal and external stakeholders. The topic will enable students to critically apply broad theoretical and technical accounting and finance knowledge and skills. The topic emphasises the use of technology to analyse data through financial statement preparation, interpretation and analysis, and budgeting, cost analysis and working capital management.

This topic introduces students to the fundamental concepts of finance and accounting for business leaders. It examines the analysis of business transactions, as well as the evaluation and interpretation of financial statements provided to external users. The topic also introduces several financial and accounting functions useful for internal management and planning.
learning_outcomes: Apply contemporary technologies to analyse and interpret accounting and finance data
Analyse and apply business practices and decisions using ethical and regulatory perspective
Apply systems thinking for effectively evaluating and communicating data to external stakeholders through reporting of the financial position, financial performance and cash flows of an entity

title: Interpreting and Visualising Business Data
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with knowledge and skills to analyse and interpret business data to make evidence-based decisions for the organisation.

This topic will enable you to develop the understanding needed to collect, analyse and interpret data to inform business decision-making for real-world business problems. The topic assesses sources of business data, methods of summarising data and ways in which the data can be analysed and communicated to make evidence-based decisions. The topic introduces essential concepts, tools and methods of analysis and statistics. The focus is on concepts, reasoning, interpretation, and thinking that build upon formulae and theory. The topic covers both descriptive statistics and inferential statistics.
learning_outcomes: Implement a structured approach to collecting business data to generate meaningful insights to inform ethical decision-making in business
Apply data analysis and visualisation technologies to effectively communicate the results of data analyses and analytical models
Analyse and interpret data using descriptive and inferential statistical tools and technologies to support sustainable, socially impactful business planning and strategy
incompatibilities: 1 of BUSN1018, BUSN1209, STAT1121, STAT1122, STAT1412, STAT8721

title: Managing in Modern Organisations
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to principles, practices and issues relevant to the management of organisations. Since this is a core topic for several degrees, activities and assessments are designed to enable students to develop important skills relevant to academic study and employment, such as applying technologies, and developing critical and analytical skills.

This topic introduces students to the knowledge and skills required to manage organisations and the people within them. It provides an overview of management in organisations and helps develop communication and organisational skills required for professional practice. In addition, we will consider human factors for decision making, emerging technologies, and social impact.
learning_outcomes: Contribute to effective performance of groups and teams
Use appropriate management terminology in spoken and written communication
Explain fundamental management principles and related theory as they apply to actual business scenarios
Discuss the role of technology and IT systems in management and organisations
Analyse management practices and decisions using ethical and sustainability practices to create social impact

title: Analysing Data in Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to determine the fundamental techniques of accessing and collecting data, analysing the data and communicating the results. It includes data collection, formatting and descriptive measures, measuring probability and distributions as well as drawing conclusions about populations and hypothesis testing.

This topic introduces the role of data and statistical analysis in business for decision making. It applies appropriate quantitative methods to collect and analyse data and to interpret and communicate the results of the analysis.
learning_outcomes: Examine appropriate quantitative methods to collect and analyse data
Interpret and communicate the results of data analysis
Evaluate the role of data and statistical analysis in business for decision making
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BACCT-Bachelor of Accounting 1a Admission into BAF-Bachelor of Accounting and Finance 1b Admission into BACOL-Bachelor of Accounting 1c Admission into BCOMACOL-Bachelor of Commerce (Accounting) 1d Admission into BACCTFP-Bachelor of Accounting - Flinders City Campus 1e Admission into BAFFP-Bachelor of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus 1f Admission into CACCR-Bachelor of Accounting/Bachelor of Criminology - Flinders City Campus 1g Admission into CACCRH-Bachelor of Accounting/Bachelor of Criminology (Honours) - Flinders City Campus 1h Admission into CACIR-Bachelor of Accounting/Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science - Flinders City Campus 1i Admission into CLAWAC-Bachelor of Laws/Bachelor of Accounting - Flinders City Campus 1j Admission into CLAWHAC-Bachelor of Laws (Honours)/Bachelor of Accounting - Flinders City Campus 1k Admission into BCOMM-Bachelor of Commerce 1l Admission into CCOIR-Bachelor of Commerce / Bachelor of International Relations and Political Science 1m Admission into CLAWCO-Bachelor of Laws/Bachelor of Commerce Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g or 1h or 1i or 1j or 1k or 1l or 1m))

title: Financial Markets
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce financial markets, emphasising the pivotal role of financial intermediaries. It also seeks to develop skills in analysing market dynamics, distinguishing instruments in financial markets, applying basic mathematical tools for financial analysis, and navigating global financial landscapes.

The topic provides students with an introduction to financial markets including debt (bond) markets, equity (share) markets, foreign exchange markets and derivatives markets. On completing the topic, students should be able to explain the role that markets play in the economy, the role of participants in the various markets and the use of the financial instruments for financing and risk management purposes.
learning_outcomes: Apply fundamental mathematical tools to address financial situations
Elaborate on the role of derivative securities in the context of risk management
Investigate the main features of financial markets and the role of financial intermediaries within them
Differentiate between debt and equity markets, along with the instruments employed in each
Examine foreign exchange markets and perform calculations related to exchange rates

title: Organisational Behaviour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to introduce students to core theories of organisational behaviour and critically evaluate the evolving roles and functions of managers, along with effective team dynamics, leadership styles and organisational structures in a diverse and tech-driven landscape.

This topic examines critical organisational behaviour issues and theories, including perception, leadership, personality, communication, learning, job design, culture and motivation, with a focus on how technology and social factors influence these aspects. The topic will explore how groups and teams form and develop in a technology-rich environment and equip you with strategies for managing conflict and leading successful change initiatives in a socially conscious way.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the evolving roles and responsibilities of managers in a diverse, technology-driven and socially conscious business environment
Apply effective motivation and conflict management strategies in a diverse work environment to enhance work performance
Critically evaluate the influence of individual and group behaviour within organisations
Examine ethical considerations and social responsibility in organisational decision-making
Apply strategies for leading effective teams and change initiatives in a technology-rich work environment, while considering the social impact of those changes

title: Assessing Economic Environments
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to consider the applications of microeconomic and macroeconomic principles. The basics of consumer behaviour, elasticity and market efficiency and the short-run and long-run output decisions of a business are considered. It compares competitive and monopolistic market outcomes from both a business and societal perspective. It considers national output and expenditure, inflation, unemployment the role of fiscal and monetary policies.

This topic is designed to introduce how economies operate. It considers the interaction and choices of individuals, businesses, and governments. It introduces key microeconomic and macroeconomic principles that help inform how decisions are made in the business environment.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of economics on decision making by individuals, businesses and government and different types of market structures
Analyse the effect of economic policies on individuals and businesses
Determine the fundamental principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics
Assess economic systems and the regulatory and political environment in which businesses operate

title: Marketing Principles in the Digital Era
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic will enable you to understand the fundamental concepts and theories of marketing and their application in the modern technology-driven business environment. This topic covers a range of relevant marketing concepts and their applications from commercial marketing and branding to the application of marketing for well-being, social and environmental impact. This topic specifically focuses on digital technologies and digital consumers.

This topic will enable you to understand the fundamental concepts and theories of marketing and their application in the modern technology-driven business environment. This topic covers a range of relevant marketing concepts and their applications from commercial marketing and branding to the application of marketing for well-being, social and environmental impact. This topic specifically focuses on digital technologies and the new digital consumers.
learning_outcomes: Explain and critically evaluate the use of key components of the marketing mix in marketing decision making
Apply marketing concepts to real-world business cases in different commercial and non-for-profit contexts and situations
Conduct marketing analysis using the relevant tools and technologies
Discuss the role of marketing in organisations’ strategic planning in the digital and technology-driven business landscape

title: Harnessing the Power of Fintech
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide a deeper insight into the concept of fintech, specifically to increase understanding of how the application of digital technology is disrupting the financial services industry. It explores the fintech sector and various business models and applications in Australia.

This topic is designed to enable students to understand the importance of financial technology (fintech) in the dynamic business environment. The topic provides students with contemporary knowledge in digital technology, such as blockchain technology and AI, and its applications in the financial services industry.
learning_outcomes: Explore the landscape of the fintech sector
Distinguish the different types of fintech business models in Australia
Appraise the emergence of new technologies in accounting
Evaluate the role of banks and financial services in the fintech ecosystem
Assess the application of blockchain technology and AI

title: Coding for Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a practical application of coding and computational thinking skills in solving complex business problems. It considers various issues in analysing arrays of data.

This topic is designed to equip students with digital skills that will be useful in business and accounting professions. The topic provides students with knowledge in digital technology, including the concept of Big Data and the role of machine learning and AI.
learning_outcomes: Determine the importance of digital skills in business and accounting professions
Distinguish the various types of data in business
Weigh up the importance of ethics in analysing data
Explore the applications of computer and technology in business using coding and computational thinking skills

title: Transforming Business Towards Net Zero
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to discuss the importance of the principles of good governance and corporate social responsibility practices, at both organisation and international levels. It introduces various net zero strategies. It considers non-financial data and information in the reporting framework.

This topic is designed to enable students to understand the role of business managers in making decisions that will have impact to the society and global environment. The topic considers the key concepts of corporate governance, CSR, and sustainability reporting.
learning_outcomes: Explore the concept of corporate governance
Analyse an entity’s role in social impact- sustainable development and corporate social responsibility practices
Interpret sustainability reporting including integrated reporting
Evaluate the globalisation of financial reporting

title: Sports Management and Leadership
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
In this topic students will have the opportunity to acquire management and leadership skills for sport clubs and communities. They will explore aspects of effective club management and leadership in a range of contexts including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledge and perspectives.

This topic explores management and leadership principles and related theory in the sports context, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait leadership. The topic explores the relationship of management and leadership principles and theory with application to authentic business scenarios in the club context. It also explores the importance of teamwork and collaboration in achieving organisational goals.
learning_outcomes: Relate management and leadership principles and theory to authentic business scenarios in the club context
Apply interpersonal and interprofessional communication skills for club and community contexts
Demonstrate teamwork and collaboration in achieving organisational goals
Explain management and leadership principles and related theory, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait leadership
Demonstrate awareness of the legal, ethical, and professional issues associated with diversity and inclusion management in the club context
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPSM-Diploma in Sports Management 1a Admission into DIPSBFP-Diploma in Sport Business - Flinders City Campus 1b Admission into DIPSA-Diploma in Sports Management Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b))

title: Exploring and Reporting Sport Business Data
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
In this topic students will have the opportunity to acquire skills in generating, analysing and reporting on data related to sports business. Working individually and in groups, students will apply their skills to authentic reports and analyses from a sporting club context.

This topic covers how to interpret, summarise and report data in the sports context, including how to design and present reports for the club.
learning_outcomes: Work collaboratively and communicate ideas clearly in group/team settings
Describe data in the sports context
Interpret and communicate the results of data analysis
Analyse sport business data
Design reports for the club
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPSM-Diploma in Sports Management 1a Admission into DIPSBFP-Diploma in Sport Business - Flinders City Campus 1b Admission into DIPSA-Diploma in Sports Management Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b))

title: Introduction to Sport Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
In this topic students will have the opportunity to learn about marketing and how it is enacted in a sporting club and community context. Working individually and in groups, students will explore and develop marketing scenarios based on real world examples.

This topic covers the key marketing concepts and how they are applied within club and community contexts. It also explores marketing theory and the factors that influence marketing decisions.
learning_outcomes: Discuss factors that influence marketing decisions
Describe marketing theories and practices
Recognise the importance of marketing concepts in the overall marketing planning and strategy formulation
Discuss the key marketing concepts and how they are applied within club and community contexts
Explore marketing issues including marketing mix, consumer behaviour, branding and use of marketing tools
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPSM-Diploma in Sports Management 1a Admission into DIPSBFP-Diploma in Sport Business - Flinders City Campus Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Applying Business Law
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce, and familiarise, students with the areas of Australian law that are relevant to business Develop students' understanding and appreciation of the Australian system of commercial law that has been developed and enforced by the Parliaments and the Courts Enable students to recognise legal problems and their implications when they arise in commercial and business practice and settings; and Provide students with the knowledge and tools to be able to seek legal advice or to make appropriate referrals to legal professionals, when and where required

The topic is concerned with providing students with an introduction to basic aspects of Australian law relevant to business including: The Australian Legal System; Agency and Business Structures; Law of Contract; Law of Property; Law of Torts and Trade Practices (Consumer Protection and Restrictive Trade Practices.
learning_outcomes: Identify sources of law and important features of the Australian legal system
Differentiate various elements and features of a contract
Explain legal concepts relevant to a business structure (such as partnership or company)
Discuss some of the commercial legal responsibilities and risks of doing business
Analyse factual scenarios involving commercially relevant legal issues

title: Mastering Financial Literacy
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a foundational understanding of core financial concepts and practices. It is designed to build financial literacy and decision-making skills by introducing students to the tools, strategies, and knowledge required to manage financial resources effectively in diverse settings.

This topic introduces students to the foundational principles of finance and their practical application in both personal and professional contexts. It explores key financial concepts, decision-making frameworks, and tools used to manage financial resources effectively. Students will engage with topics such as financial planning, resource allocation, investment fundamentals, and the role of financial systems in supporting individual and organisational goals. Through applied learning and real-world scenarios, students will develop the confidence and capability to make informed financial decisions that support both short-term needs and long-term financial wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Interpret key financial concepts, including the time value of money and basic valuation techniques
Evaluate a range of financial strategies and products in relation to financial goals and risk preferences
Analyse the role of financial systems in shaping financial outcomes and behaviours
Apply financial tools and data to analyse planning and decision-making in personal, business, or broader economic contexts

syllabus_overview:
In this topic students will have the opportunity to apply their skills and knowledge in sport management in a club context. They will be based in the club environment, actively contributing to club activity and business, with the opportunity to demonstrate their teamwork and communication skills in this context.

This practicum topic enables the practical application of the skills developed in the club context.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective, professional and ethical engagement and teamwork in a diverse, workplace setting
Demonstrate effective spoken and written communication skills in a work context
Develop goals to enhance personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practice in a club or community setting
Demonstrate ability to apply a broad range of digital, technical and professional skills in a club or community context
Explore, analyse and document potential solutions for business issues

title: The Business of Growing Wine Grapes
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with insights into the seasonal nature of wine grape production and some different wine grape varieties and the influence and importance of wine varieties and regions. They will gain an appreciation of the basic physiological processes of vine and fruit growth, various risks linked to grape production (including the influence of climate changes, pests etc,) and how to manage these in order to successfully and sustainably manage a wine grape growing business.

This topic provides students with important underpinning knowledge of grape production in the Australian wine industry, including an understanding of the variations in scale and concentration across the sector. The topic is focused on the production of fruit fit for the intended winemaking purpose and management of risk. Students will learn about key threats such as pests and diseases that can endanger business outcomes and will become familiar with strategies and vineyard operations used to address those risks. The topic will address the issue of biosecurity and will introduce organic and biodynamic production systems consistent with the need for sustainability and environmental stewardship in a changing climate.
learning_outcomes: Create a basic vineyard budget
Categorise the key Australian winegrowing regions and the key wine grape varieties within them
Identify and analyse agricultural risks that impact on winegrowing businesses and plan ways to mitigate them
Develop a basic vineyard management plan

title: Wines of the World
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of the fundamentals of how the world's viti- and viniculture operates. In it students will explore selected wine regions, learn important terms and abbreviations, grape varieties; wine styles and production specificities and gain insight into wine styles and production specificities.

This topic introduces and explains the fundamentals of the world's viti- and vinicultural situation, i.e. statistics regarding planted area, produced volumes per country (wine, table grapes, raisins, grape juice), wine styles and traditions in production and aging. It also provides a brief historical overview of the most important wine regions of the world, quality regulations and quality criteria, protected areas of origin and vineyard classification systems. It also introduces students to industry-specific vocabulary used in labelling and describing important wines of the world including terms that describe residual sugar levels, indicate quality and/or aging as well as specific technologies (e.g. "sur lie" or "roble" or "pasito").
learning_outcomes: Describe wine styles from selected wine regions of the world that are considered as key players; including the characteristics and tastes of the wines
Distinguish wine regions regarding their role as global players in the wine business or niche product producers in terms of quantity, quality and international market importance
Explain characteristics of selected and important wine regions of Europe, Australia, Oceania, the Americas, Africa and Asia
Describe wine styles, grape varieties and the 'terroir' of selected wine areas

Explain (denominations) and geographical locations of the world's important wine areas, including similarities and differences within specific regions, their wine styles, grape varieties, production methods and traditions

title: Finance and Accounting for Leaders PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of the importance of financial information in business practice. The topic includes introductory financial accounting, introductory management accounting, financial statement interpretation and analysis, and budgeting.

This topic introduces students to the fundamental concepts of financial and management accounting. It examines the elements of the financial statements provided to external users and the information provided in, and interpretation of, those statements. Several management accounting functions, important to internal users, are also introduced.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret information contained in the financial statements
Demonstrate basic knowledge of techniques used for internal management processes, including budgeting, cost analysis and working capital management
Demonstrate a basic understanding of the measurement and reporting of the financial position, financial performance and cash flows of an entity and how this information is reported to external users
Use word processors, spreadsheets and presentation software

title: Introduction to Sports Law
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide an introduction to the principles of law that are relevant to sports, and to explore application of these principles, as well as to discuss those laws relevant to sports.

This topic will provide students with an introduction to sources of legislation in a sporting context. Students will explore the principles of law in relation to sporting organisations, teams and products including contracts, competition law, sporting tribunals and policies related to discrimination and misconduct in sports.
learning_outcomes: Describe the legal issues that arise in the sports context
Discuss state, national and international law in relation to sports
Explore the mechanisms for the legal regulation of sport including such issues as sport-related governance, dispute settlement, the commercial regulation of sport, and the anti-doping in sport regime
Describe how to use legal principles a sports environment

title: Economics for Business PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to understand the business applications of microeconomic concepts. The basics of consumer behaviour and the short-run and long-run output decisions of a business will be examined. Students will learn how to make comparisons between competitive and monopolistic market outcomes from both a business and societal perspective.

This topic is concerned with the study of markets and the behaviour of consumers and firms in both competitive and monopolistic markets. An understanding is developed of market demand and supply forces and the interaction of both in determining market outcomes. Insight is given into the behaviour of major decision-makers in the market place. These include: consumers (demand), producers or firms (supply) operating in competitive and monopolistic markets, and the role of government (e.g. taxes and subsidies) and the impact of government intervention on economic welfare.
learning_outcomes: Reflect the relationship between business costs and short-run and long-run output decisions, with reference to the returns to a variable output, returns to scale, and the minimum efficient scale of production
Identify the relationship between the business cycle and inflation and unemployment
Explain elasticity and the relationship with the market demand curve
Explain the concept of scarcity; opportunity cost; demand and supply; economic profit; profit maximisation; short-run and long-run; economies and diseconomies of scale; and price discrimination
Use diagrammatic models and tools, to indicate your understanding of the short-run and long-run adjustments of competitive markets
Explain the need for equity considerations and the efficiency impact of government taxes, subsidies, price floors and price ceilings
Illustrate how fiscal and monetary policy are used over the business cycle

title: Managing in Modern Organisations PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to principles, practices and issues relevant to the management of organisations. Since this is a core topic for several degrees, activities and assessments are designed to enable students to develop generic skills relevant to academic study and employment.

This topic introduces students to the knowledge and skills required to manage people and organisations in the global economy. It provides an overview of management in organisations and helps develop communication and organisational skills required in the professional workplace.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and use the basic language of management
Demonstrate reflection and incorporation of feedback from peers and educators for learning
Explain basic management principles and related theory
Describe ways to address knowledge gaps associated with the academic and organisational work for research and learning
Relate basic management principles and theory to actual business scenarios
Work collaboratively and communicate ideas clearly in group/team settings
Demonstrate appropriate effective communication strategies for diverse audiences to ensure cultural safety

title: Recording Business Transactions PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the technical aspects of recording and reporting accounting information in the context of a sole trader. It introduces the accounting cycle, the rules of debit and credit, double-entry accrual-based accounting and the need for adjusting and closing entries. The topic also includes how to account for the transactions of a retail business, cash management and control, receivables, inventory systems and the preparation of straightforward financial statements.

This topic is designed to introduce the nature of accounting, its main functions, and its role in the decision-making process of business entities. It aims to provide a solid grounding in accounting fundamentals.
learning_outcomes: Use word processors, spreadsheets and presentation software
Analyse and record business transactions using double entry accounting for a sole trader
Appraise information for retailing transactions, inventory systems and bank reconciliations
Determine the role and purpose of financial accounting and financial statements
Construct financial statements

title: Marketing Principles in the Digital Era PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic is structured such that the basic concepts and principles of marketing management are introduced, providing students a foundation/framework within which to work. Students will be required to apply these concepts in their assignment. Students will compare the theories they learn in the class with marketing practices in the real world situations. To improve student team skills, group assessment has been included.

This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the concepts and tools used in marketing management. Concepts such as: market segmentation, consumer behaviour, marketing mix (product, place, price and promotion), branding and marketing are discussed. These fundamental concepts provide a foundation/framework within which to work. The topic concludes by discussing issues such as internet marketing, marketing strategy and planning. In addition, this topic aims to develop students' team skills.
learning_outcomes: Apply marketing concepts to real-world business cases in different commercial and non-for-profit contexts and situations
Explain and critically evaluate the use of key components of the marketing mix in marketing decision making
Conduct marketing analysis using the relevant tools and technologies
Discuss the role of marketing in organisations’ strategic planning in the digital and technology-driven business landscape

It accounts for more complex transactions and forms of business organisations, including partnerships, non-current assets, liabilities as well as the preparation and presentation of financial reports.

Exploring Accounting Processes is designed to develop knowledge of the nature of accounting, its main functions, and its role in the decision-making process of business entities. It considers the application of accounting standards and practical issues in financial reporting.

Construct a range of financial statements
Analyse and record business transactions for a partnership

title: Interpreting and Visualising Business Data PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the opportunity to develop knowledge and skills in quantitative methods useful in business.

The topic provides an introduction on how to use computational and decision-making techniques useful to business students in such fields as accounting, management, finance and economics. Subjects covered include data and statistics, probability, sampling, hypothesis testing and how business managers can access and process information to make sound business decisions. The topic reviews sources of business information, methods of summarizing information and ways in which the information can be processed to make good business decisions.
learning_outcomes: Describe methods of collecting business data
Explain and apply basic probability and distribution concepts and carry out statistical estimation and testing
Describe and apply quantitative analytical techniques used in business and economics
Summarise data and present them graphically
Carry out linear regression and interpret output

title: Financial Markets PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to explain: The role that markets play in the economy How people buy and sell (trade) financial securities (such as stocks and bonds), commodities (such as precious metals or agricultural goods), and other items of value at low transaction costs and at prices that reflect the global market

The topic provides students with an introduction to financial markets including debt (bond) markets, equity (share) markets, foreign exchange markets and derivatives markets. On completing the topic, students should be able to explain the role that markets play in the economy, the role of participants in the various markets and the use of the financial instruments for financing and risk management purposes.
learning_outcomes: Describe the different financing instruments that are available for both private sector and government sector financing requirements, and develop an appreciation of the appropriate forms of financing for different purposes
Describe the main features of financial markets
Describe ethical principles and the laws and codes of ethics applicable to financial markets
Describe the functions and operations of foreign exchange markets and perform calculations with respect to exchange rates
Explain the role that financial intermediaries play in financial markets; including the role played by banks and non-bank financial institutions
Explain the role of derivative securities in risk management
Explain the different approaches to forecasting share price movements
Distinguish between debt and equity financing
Discuss the various forms of equity finance and the regulatory controls on equity capital markets

school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to discuss the importance of the principles of good governance and corporate social responsibility practices, at both organisation and international levels. It introduces various net zero strategies. It considers non-financial data and information in the reporting framework.

This topic is designed to enable students to understand the role of business managers in making decisions that will have impact to the society and global environment. The topic considers the key concepts of corporate governance, CSR, and sustainability reporting.

Analyse an entity’s role in social impact- sustainable development and corporate social responsibility practices
Evaluate the globalisation of financial reporting

Subjects relevant to business and the accounting profession are covered, including Agency and Business Structures and the key features of Contract Law. It covers the concept of the company as a separate legal entity, directors’ duties and the rights of shareholders.

This introductory topic covers areas such as the national legal system and sources of Business and Corporations Law relevant to the accounting profession. Students will be exposed to critical analysis of legal issues for individuals, business, and accounting professionals.

Apply knowledge of legal principles and regulation to solve problems in a business context

title: Commercial Outcomes In Sport
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of the fundamentals of financial information, strategic planning, management and the legal framework as it applies to businesses operating in modern competitive environments.

This topic introduces students to the fundamental concepts of finance, accounting and strategic management. It examines purpose of financial information, as well as the evaluation and interpretation of financial statements. It considers essential concepts in strategic management in a sporting club context.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate financial statements and assess the financial performance and position of an organisation and its significance in strategic decision making
Apply strategic management principles to the sports industry
Explain the legal and regulatory frameworks affecting financial operations and reporting in the sports industry
Determine the role and purpose of financial information and the key elements of financial statements

school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide the foundational knowledge required to formulate and evaluate company investment and financing policies. It covers the role and objectives of financial management, risk and return concepts, capital budgeting, sources of financing, the cost of capital, operating and financial leverage, financial structure decisions and dividend policies.

This is an introductory topic to financial management principles and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of finance management. Students will learn about analytical techniques that assist decision makers finance business and make investment and distribution decisions.

Analyse capital budgeting decisions incorporating risk management
Assess the sources of finance available to an organisation and how it structures its finances
Determine the role of finance in an organisation and the financial environment in which it operates

school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
In this topic students will have the opportunity to learn about marketing and how it is enacted in a sporting club and community context. Students will have the opportunity to acquire knowledge of sport engagement in a fan, community and club context.

This topic covers key marketing concepts and how they are applied within club and community contexts. It also explores the key aspects of fan and community engagement and development in the sports context, including participation, diversity, inclusion and respect.
learning_outcomes: Describe the meaning and benefits of community participation for individuals
Discuss factors that influence marketing decisions
Identify and evaluate inclusive strategies for effectively engaging diverse communities in sport
Analyse strategies to enhance fan engagement through marketing and fan experience initiatives

title: Developing Entrepreneurs and Small Businesses
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an entrepreneurial orientation and skills to identify and explore opportunities when creating a business or acting as intrapreneurs within existing organisations through a problem-solving approach. Creativity, innovation, and design thinking are key concepts of this entrepreneurial process, providing students with new, agile, and dynamic methods to test and validate a new venture or initiative, including emerging technologies that facilitate diverse aspects of business development.

This topic will enable you to comprehend the entrepreneurship journey and process of creating a business or major initiatives within a business, from the initial idea to growth strategies. You will examine the relevance of entrepreneurs and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to regional and socioeconomic contexts. This topic focuses on applying an entrepreneurial mindset to new venture creation and initiatives for growth, including consideration of the value proposition, market research, business model planning, and strategy. You will explore a range of entrepreneurial contexts and purposes including social impact, indigenous businesses, sustainability, the role of technology, start-ups, franchising, corporate venture and intrapreneurship, and the legal, financial and resource factors effecting decision-making.
learning_outcomes: Integrate use of existing and emerging technologies in planning processes and conception of new ventures or initiatives
Discuss the challenges of entrepreneurial practice in various geographical and socio-economic settings
Analyse business practices and value creation in relation to ethics, sustainability, social impact, and economic impact
Critically apply theoretical and entrepreneurial approaches to prepare a feasibility and implementation plan for a new venture or major growth initiative

It is designed to build financial literacy and decision-making skills by introducing students to the tools, strategies, and knowledge required to manage financial resources effectively in diverse settings.

This topic introduces students to the foundational principles of finance and their practical application in both personal and professional contexts. It explores key financial concepts, decision-making frameworks, and tools used to manage financial resources effectively. Students will engage with topics such as financial planning, resource allocation, investment fundamentals, and the role of financial systems in supporting individual and organisational goals. Through applied learning and real-world scenarios, students will develop the confidence and capability to make informed financial decisions that support both short-term needs and long-term financial wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Interpret key financial concepts, including the time value of money and basic valuation techniques
Apply financial tools and data to analyse planning and decision-making in personal, business, or broader economic contexts
Evaluate a range of financial strategies and products in relation to financial goals and risk preferences
Analyse the role of financial systems in shaping financial outcomes and behaviours
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPBU-Diploma in Business 1a Admission into DIPBUE-Diploma in Business - Extended 1b Admission into DIPBUEFP Diploma in Business 1c Admission into DIPBUFP Diploma in Business Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c)

title: Coding for Business PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a practical application of coding and computational thinking skills in solving complex business problems. It considers various issues in analysing arrays of data.

This topic is designed to equip students with digital skills that will be useful in business and accounting professions. The topic provides students with knowledge in digital technology, including the concept of Big Data and the role of machine learning and AI.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish the various types of data in business
Determine the importance of digital skills in business and accounting professions
Weigh up the importance of ethics in analysing data
Explore the applications of computer and technology in business using coding and computational thinking skills
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPBU-Diploma in Business 1a Admission into DIPBUE-Diploma in Business - Extended 1b Admission into DIPBUFP-Diploma in Business - Flinders City Campus 1c Admission into DIPBUEFP-Diploma in Business - Flinders City Campus - Extended Must satisfy: (1 or 1a or 1b or 1c )

title: Applying Business Law PW
school: Flinders University Academy
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce, and familiarise, students with the areas of Australian law that are relevant to business Develop students' understanding and appreciation of the Australian system of commercial law that has been developed and enforced by the Parliaments and the Courts Enable students to recognise legal problems and their implications when they arise in commercial and business practice and settings; and Provide students with the knowledge and tools to be able to seek legal advice or to make appropriate referrals to legal professionals, when and where required

This topic is concerned with providing students with an introduction to basic aspects of Australian law relevant to business including: The Australian Legal System; Agency and Business Structures; Law of Contract; Law of Property; Law of Torts and Trade Practices (Consumer Protection and Restrictive Trade Practices).
learning_outcomes: Identify sources of law and important features of the Australian legal system
Discuss some of the commercial legal responsibilities and risks of doing business
Explain legal concepts relevant to a business structure (such as partnership or company)
Differentiate various elements and features of a contract
Analyse factual scenarios involving commercially relevant legal issues
prerequisites: 1 Admission into DIPBU-Diploma in Business 1a Admission into DIPBUE-Diploma in Business - Extended 1b Admission into DIPBUEFP Diploma in Business 1c Admission into DIPBUFP Diploma in Business Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c)

title: International Business Context
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to provide students with an understanding of many aspects of engaging in international business in an increasingly challenging global market.

This topic will enable you to assess opportunities in the global market while considering the risks of overseas business expansion. It will equip you with a decision-making tool for designing a global business model. You will gain knowledge of when, why, and how businesses expand into the international market. The topic introduces students to the rapidly evolving international business environment, including populist movements, nationalist and protectionist policies, and their implications for international business. It examines disruptive innovation, climate change, and ethical issues driving increasing pressure on international businesses and aims to assist students in assessing and thinking critically about these issues and how businesses can organise for sustainability and success in an ever-changing international business environment.
learning_outcomes: Design an effective method for internationalising your business overseas

Analyse different internal and external influences that a business must consider when expanding beyond the domestic market into foreign markets through exporting, foreign direct investment, or other collaborative ventures
Evaluate an organisation’s internal resources to successfully navigate the risks in the global market
Evaluate the risks and opportunities presented by a semi-globalised environment
Assess the social, environmental, and ethical considerations of international business to effectively manage global operations

title: Management of Financial Institutions
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
Financial institutions are participating in an increasingly globalised environment and are subject to international regulation. The study of the management of financial institutions means that students are developing skills which will help them connect across international boundaries in the workplace should they choose to work in the international banking arena or for other financial institutions which are engaged in cross-border activities

This topic explores the role and management of financial institutions within a dynamic and increasingly globalised financial system. Students will examine the functions and types of financial institutions, the key risks they face, and the regulatory frameworks that govern their operations. Emphasis is placed on the tools and techniques used to manage financial risk, as well as the challenges and opportunities presented by global financial integration.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the importance of financial institutions in the global economy
Apply relevant techniques to measure and manage those risks
Discuss contemporary issues affecting financial institutions and their stakeholders
Identify the main types of risk confronted by financial institutions
Evaluate the main regulations and operations of financial institutions within regulatory frameworks
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN2008, BUSN1210 1a BUSN1030 Must satisfy: (1 or 1a)

title: Consumer Behaviour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic focuses on the influences of consumer behaviour, a core component of marketing. The topic introduces you to consumer behaviour and how this knowledge relates to the marketing of products and services.

This topic focuses on one of the core components of marketing: consumer behaviour. You will understand how individuals behave as consumers and the influences of consumer behaviour in connection to the marketing of products and services in both the private and public sectors. Drawing on psychological and sociological perspectives, this topic covers the consumer as an individual; the consumer in social and cultural settings; the role of consumer behaviour in marketing; and the marketing decision-making process. This prepares you to manage and respond to create an improved consumer experience.
learning_outcomes: Assess consumer behaviour issues to make recommendations for an improved customer experience
Explain the consumer behaviour decision-making elements that influence how consumers react to internal and external elements in the buying, using and discarding decision process
Use key consumer behaviour conceptual tools to guide decisions on effective strategies for successful management of the consumer and service delivery
Evaluate situational influences to anticipate customer responses and reactions to a given consumption situation
prerequisites: 36 units of topics

title: The Australian Economy
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim is for students to understand the structure of the Australian economy and its performance in meeting various goals. Students should be able to analyse, evaluate and communicate important economic policy issues, such as government intervention, taxation, immigration, protection, wage regulations, foreign investment and the financial system.

The topic will review the structure of the Australian economy and its performance in meeting various goals. Economic policy issues will be discussed including important policy issues that are currently being debated. Issues explored will include government intervention, taxation, immigration, protection, wage regulations, foreign investment and the financial system.
learning_outcomes: Analyse, evaluate and communicate arguments framed in an economic perspective, and be able to respond with your own view, framed in an appropriate manner
Explain key terms and concepts commonly used in economics, including their definition and meaning, and the limitations in their use
Explain the significant economic policy issues and debates in various aspects of the economy, including who the key stakeholders are and the perspectives they bring to the issues
Locate and use appropriately, key economic data, both past and current, gathered by relevant agencies
Describe important historical trends in performance of the economy in key areas

title: Sustainable Resource Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to critical concepts and practices relevant to sustainable resource management, including sustainability, resilience, social impact, and corporate social responsibility. It also aims to build students’ critical analysis, planning and communication skills for sustainability management.

In this topic, students will examine critical concepts in sustainable resource management, including sustainability, resilience, social impact, and corporate social responsibility. Importantly, students will examine how these concepts are applied in real world practice. This topic emphasizes critical analysis of real-world sustainability issues and challenges, application of topic concepts to real world practice, discussion, and case studies relating to business sustainability.
learning_outcomes: Apply critical concepts relevant to sustainable resource management to analysis of real-world practice
Critically analyse the relationships between resource management, sustainability, resilience, social impact, and corporate social responsibility concepts
Assess a company’s sustainability and resilience-building practices
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1013, BUSN1020 1a ^ BUSN2054 Must Satisfy: (1 or 1a) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: International Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to provide students with a solid understanding of international financial systems and the financial decisions of multinational firms, focusing on global markets, exchange rates, and capital flows.

This topic provides students with the knowledge and analytical skills to understand international financial systems and the decisions of multinational firms. It examines global markets, exchange rates, and the structure of international capital flows, offering insights into how financial strategies operate in an interconnected world.
learning_outcomes: Apply forecasting techniques and derivative-based strategies to manage foreign exchange exposure
Analyse the operation of international banking and global capital markets and their significance in international finance
Evaluate the role of multinational firms and globalisation in shaping international financial decisions
Assess the structure and functioning of international financial systems and their influence on global markets
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1210

title: Uncovering Global Market Insights
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to market research in a variety of contexts, as a means of assessing consumer markets nationally and internationally and providing a communication channel between consumers and decision makers. It will develop a template for transforming problems into research objectives, designing, and implementing a research plan and communicating the results effectively. The topic will also address, at an applied level, a range of issues in the design and practice of a range of research methodologies. The topic will also equip students with the practical skills to conduct market research to develop and further enhance strategic decisions.

This topic will provide an applied introduction to the theory and practice of market research, and its use as a decision making tool for a range of stakeholders. It will enable students to transform problems into research objectives, design and implement a research plan, and interpret and communicate market research insights. The topic covers research design and practice with respect to quantitative and qualitative methodologies, and considers emerging approaches to understanding consumers and communities.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the effectiveness of different types of research methodologies, including qualitative and quantitative approaches
Question the role of traditional market research approaches and compare these to emerging methods of developing insight into diverse, global audiences
Evaluate the role of market research in providing insight for relevant stakeholders
Design a market research project that will achieve relevant research objectives and transform information into insight for decision-making
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1009, BUSN1018, BUSN1209, HLPE1005, SOCI2025, POLI2026, PSYC1106

title: Training and Development
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to equip you with the knowledge and skills to design, implement, and evaluate impactful training & development programs in a rapidly changing technological landscape. You'll learn to consider the human factor and the social impact of training towards organisational sustainability, ensuring effective skill development for a future-ready workforce.

This topic dives into the constantly evolving world of training and development, equipping you to design and implement effective training & development programs in the digital age. We'll explore how technology transforms learning, analyse the human factors that influence training effectiveness, and consider the social impact of developing a skilled and adaptable workforce. You'll gain insights into strategic training needs assessments, learning theories, and best practices for program design and evaluation. The topic also examines traditional and technology-based training methods, explores employee development and career management strategies, and delves into fostering a diverse and inclusive learning environment.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate various learning theories and apply them to design engaging and effective training and development programs that leverage technology
Conduct strategic training needs assessments that consider the evolving digital landscape and human and social factors impacting learning within organisations
Develop strategies to ensure successful transfer of learning to the evolving workplace requirements and the achievement of organisation’s business objectives
Explore the future of training in relation to innovative technologies and approaches to employee development, fostering diversity and inclusivity in the learning process
Design comprehensive training evaluation methods to measure the impact of programs on individuals and the organisation’s social responsibility goals
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1021, BUSN1012, BUSN2038, BUSN2009, BUSN1203

title: Business Forecasting
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the knowledge, practical skills, and ethical awareness required to analyse business data and develop forecasts for business decision-making. Specifically, the topic aims to: Build practical skills in statistical analysis, modelling, and forecasting across diverse business scenarios. Develop the ability to translate analytical findings into clear, evidence-based recommendations. Foster critical awareness of bias, ethical considerations, and the responsible use of data in business decision-making.

This topic builds students' skills in analysing and forecasting business data. It will discuss how to make analysis and forecasts in circumstances where there is little information available and situations where considerable data are available. Major business data sources are reviewed and methods of processing data to generate good forecasts are discussed. Students will develop practical skills through hands-on activities in exploratory data analysis, statistical inference, regression analysis, time series analysis, and judgmental forecasting. Students will also learn to identify potential bias in modelling and analytics, consider relevant regulatory and ethical principles, and use analytical evidence responsibly to support ethical, evidence-based business decision-making.
learning_outcomes: Develop statistical models and forecasts for a range of business scenarios
Justify business recommendations using evidence from statistical tests and forecast results
Analyse business data using appropriate statistical and analytical techniques
Evaluate the impact of bias and ethical issues on forecasting outcomes and business decision-making
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1009, BUSN1018, BUSN1209

title: Branding and Advertising
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an: Understanding of the Integrated Marketing Communications concept and the environment marketers operate in when designing marketing communications strategies Appreciation of the processes used to create an effective communications strategy and the tools used in marketing communications Understanding of the effectiveness of different traditional and modern marketing communication tools and practices Knowledge of consumer behaviour, branding and other relevant factors that are strongly linked with marketing communications

This topic introduces students to the process of developing and managing effective marketing communications. Using the Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) concept, students will gain an understanding of consumer behaviour, communication theory and the various media used in advertising and promotion. They will also learn how to plan, develop and implement advertising and promotional campaigns.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the ethical issues associated with marketing communications
Examine the role of integrated marketing communications (IMC) in the marketing process
Apply consumer behaviour and branding theories to marketing communications contexts
Illustrate the use of marketing communications tools across broadcast, digital, support media, direct marketing, sales promotion, public relations, and personal selling
Analyse the factors that influence consumer response to marketing communication activities
prerequisites: ^ 1 of BUSN2015, BUSN2025, BUSN1022, BUSN1206 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Costing for Managers
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to analyse various costing systems and appropriate quantitative techniques to calculate and communicate cost information to support management decision making. It will introduce the analysis of cost behaviour and drivers, job costing and other costing information for business planning and control. It will help assess the actual performance of various parts of a business organisation against its budgeted performance.

This topic introduces the role and purpose of management accounting. It evaluates the role of strategy in the planning, control, and decision-making functions of an organisation and assesses how cost information is analysed within an organisation to measure performance and inform decision makers.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role and purpose of management accounting
Determine the role of strategy in the planning, control, and decision-making functions of an organisation
Appraise the actual performance of various parts of a business organisation against its budgeted performance
Analyse various costing systems and appropriate quantitative techniques to calculate and communicate cost information to support management decision making
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1001, BUSN1202

title: Human Resource Planning, Recruitment and Selection
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills required to advise on and participate in recruitment and selection activities in a range of organisational contexts. It seeks to foster an appreciation for the human element in recruitment decisions, the social implications of recruitment strategies, and the potential of technology to enhance the efficiency and fairness of selection processes. Students will be prepared to navigate and contribute to recruitment and selection in a way that values human potential, addresses social considerations, and leverages technological advancements for organisational benefits.

This topic includes job analysis; channels and methods of recruitment; shortlisting and selection processes; and reliability and validity of selection processes. It delves into the interaction among human decision-making, social interactions within organisations, and the continuous advancement of technological tools and platforms, providing a thorough understanding of contemporary recruitment and selection methods.
learning_outcomes: Use reflective questioning and research to support analysis
Describe the nature and strategic importance of human resource planning, recruitment and selection to the achievement of an organisation's business objectives
Critically analyse the application of concepts and processes in practice, including the role of technology
Discuss the importance of committing to equity and equal opportunities
prerequisites: 1 BUSN1021 1a BUSN2038 1b BUSN2009 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b))

title: Applying Accounting Standards
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce the theoretical principles and the regulatory environment that applies to financial reporting, including the conceptual framework and the accounting standard setting process. It considers the application of accounting standards in the areas of provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets, impairment of assets, leases, intangible assets, revenue recognition, financial instruments, and foreign exchange transactions.

This topic considers the regulatory environment that applies to financial reporting, including the conceptual framework and the accounting standard setting process. The theoretical principles underlying accounting practice are considered as well as the application of accounting standards involving measurement, professional judgement and more practical issues in financial reporting.
learning_outcomes: Assess the application of a range of International Financial Reporting Standards to the preparation of financial statements
Determine the regulatory environment that applies to financial reporting including the conceptual framework and the accounting standard setting process
Appraise the theoretical principles underlying accounting practice
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1002, BUSN1208

title: Human Resource Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with foundational knowledge and professional skills in the roles, processes and activities that make up human resource management practice in organisations. The topic also aims to provide students with an understanding of the impact of global trends and challenges, such as artificial intelligence, digital technologies, and sustainability, on work and HRM.

This topic introduces students to the theory and practice of Human Resource Management (HRM), with a focus on the strategic perspective on HRM. It provides an overview of the HR roles, processes and activities that underpin the practice of HRM. Global trends, and challenges, impacting on work and HRM, are also explored. These include artificial intelligence and other digital technologies and sustainability.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate the role that HRM plays in building and sustaining competitive advantage in organisations
Develop skills in collaboration in the practice of HRM
Critically evaluate the theory and practice of HRM in organisations
Analyse and evaluate the HR implications of global trends impacting on work and people in workplaces, and propose strategic responses that are equitable, inclusive, meaningful, and productive
Apply foundational knowledge and technical skills in HRM to analyse real-world business cases within various organizational settings

title: Exploring the Fundamentals of Corporate Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to build students’ understanding of corporate financial decision-making and the tools used to support these decisions.
