It seeks to develop analytical and practical skills for evaluating investment opportunities, financing options, and business performance, while fostering an appreciation of the role of finance in enhancing organisational value.

This topic provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles and practices of corporate finance. It explores the corporate finance decision-making processes that underpin value creation in businesses, including investment appraisal, financing choices, and working capital management. Students will develop a foundational understanding of risk and return analysis, cost of capital, capital budgeting, and the implications of dividend and capital structure policies. Additional focus is placed on interpreting financial statements, valuing bonds and shares, and understanding mergers and acquisitions (M&A). Through applied techniques and analytical frameworks, students will build the skills required to evaluate and make informed financial decisions in a business context.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate capital budgeting and investment decisions
Analyse financing decisions related to capital structure, leverage, and dividend policy, and their impact on firm value
Assess the role of short-term financial management, including working capital and liquidity strategies, in supporting business operations
Interpret financial statements to assess organisational performance and cash flow health
Apply valuation models to determine the value and assess the risk of financial instruments such as bonds and shares

title: International Business Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop students’ understanding of the human factors influencing business performance in a complex international business environment is the aim of this topic.

The emphasis of this topic is on the varying decisions made by executives based on their individual characteristics, and their subsequent impact on business performance. The content includes aspects of strategic leadership, negotiation, and motivation for firms engaged in international business. The focus is on management approaches to diversity in an organisation to effectively manage business in a global market comprising complex cultural, political, economic, competitive, and other contextual factors.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast leadership, negotiation, and motivations across cultures
Evaluate industry and business context to effectively recruit executives for successful business operations
Analyse and evaluate corporate governance of a business operating in a global market
Design an effective method for managing diverse teams within organisations
Analyse the impact of top executives on business performance

title: Evaluating Macroeconomic Trends
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to identify and analyse the key factors that influence policymakers and contribute to decisions on economic growth or recovery. It also seeks to explain how behaviour and decision-making affect financial markets at both national and global levels. Students will use standard macroeconomic models to analyse the likely consequences of economic shocks and policy changes, developing the skills to interpret and evaluate macroeconomic outcomes in real-world contexts.

This topic builds on introductory macroeconomic principles to analyse the causes of, and policy responses to, the major macroeconomic challenges confronting policymakers. These include unemployment, inflation, public debt, terms of trade shocks, current account deficits, foreign debt, and economic growth. The topic also examines how these issues affect financial markets through their influence on government spending, taxation, public debt, interest rates, exchange rates, and capital flows. Students will develop the analytical skills to understand and evaluate macroeconomic policy decisions in both domestic and global contexts.
learning_outcomes: Determine appropriate policy responses for a range of economic conditions
Apply macroeconomic models to assess the effects of policy changes and non-intervention
Analyse the major macroeconomic objectives and their relationship to the business cycle
Evaluate the implications of fiscal policy for government budgets, interest rates, and public debt
Interpret the implementation and transmission mechanisms of monetary policy
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Accounting for Corporations
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to assess the impact of specific regulatory requirements and accepted accounting principles on more complex corporate accounting transactions. It covers accounting for transactions with equity participants, tax effect accounting, business combinations, the preparation of consolidated financial statements.

This topic considers the application of accounting standards involving measurement, professional judgement and more practical issues in financial reporting that apply in the context of a corporation.
learning_outcomes: Construct consolidated financial statements for economic entities comprising more than one legal entity
Evaluate International Financial Reporting Standards that apply to corporations
Appraise the role of General Purpose Financial Reports for corporations
Assess the application of accounting principles to various operational areas of a corporate entity
prerequisites: BUSN1002

title: Applying Microeconomic Principles
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to deepen students’ understanding of microeconomic principles and develop their ability to apply these concepts to analyse and solve real-world problems. Students will learn to interpret and construct economic models, evaluate market outcomes, and apply economic reasoning to managerial and policy decisions. The topic bridges theory and practice, preparing students to think analytically and make informed decisions in business and economic environments.

This topic provides students with an intermediate-level understanding of microeconomic theory and its application to real-world business and policy decisions. Building on foundational economic concepts, students will explore how individuals and firms make choices under constraints, how markets function and fail, and how economic models can inform strategic and managerial decision-making. The topic emphasizes applied analysis, critical thinking, and the use of microeconomic tools to solve practical problems in business and public policy contexts.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the outcomes of various market structures and the effects of government interventions
Apply microeconomic models to analyse consumer and firm behaviour in different market contexts
Appraise key microeconomic concepts such as opportunity cost, marginal analysis, and market equilibrium
Interpret cost structures, production decisions, and pricing strategies using graphical and numerical tools
Apply microeconomic reasoning to support managerial or policy decisions in real-world scenarios
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Addressing Business and Corporations Law
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce the Australian Legal System and provide an understanding of Business and Corporations Law. Topics relevant to business and the accounting profession are covered, including Agency and Business Structures and the key features of Contract Law. It covers the concept of the company as a separate legal entity, directors’ duties and the rights of shareholders.

This topic introduces the national legal system and sources of Business and Corporations Law relevant to the accounting profession. It will enable critical analysis of legal issues for individuals, business, and accounting professionals.
learning_outcomes: Analyse fundamental principles of contract law and company law in business scenarios
Examine sources of law and important features of the Australian legal system relevant to the accounting profession
Apply knowledge of legal principles and regulation to solve problems in a business context
Evaluate data protection and privacy regulation applicable to business environments

title: Managing Diversity
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the theoretical concepts and practical issues related to managing diversity in organisations operating in Australia and the Asia Pacific Region.

This topic addresses the theory and practice of managing a diverse workforce in the social, business and legal context of organisations operating in Australia and the Asia Pacific region. Topics addressed include the theoretical and policy context of diversity, workforce and workplace diversity in Australia, forms of diversity and inclusion, approaches to diversity, promoting diversity in the workforce, and HRM issues related to discrimination, gender equity, cultural diversity, disability, and work-life balance in the workplace.
learning_outcomes: Identify and describe concepts of diversity and inclusion applied to the workplace in Australia
Identify and describe the strategic, management, compliance and human resource management issues associated with developing and implementing diversity and inclusion initiatives in the workplace
Evaluate the legal, ethical, and professional issues associated with diversity management in the contemporary workplace
Analyse practical case studies of equity, inclusion, diversity and discrimination in the workplace
Describe and apply the legal framework regulating the management of workplace diversity and inclusion issues
Identify and describe potential differences in managing diversity in Australia and selected country contexts in the Asia-Pacific
prerequisites: 36 units of credit completed

title: Managing Project, Supply Chain, and Logistics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students with an introduction to the importance of operations and supply chain management Provide students with an appreciation of the link between corporate strategy and operations and SCM Teach students to understand business processes, process performance measures and six sigma methodology Provide students with the skills to recognise the importance of quality and associated dimensions and costs Introduce students to the linkages in the supply chain, allowing them to appreciate the importance of forecasting, sourcing, purchasing and logistics Demonstrate the need for planning and controlling within the operations and SCM functions, including inventory management analysis and approaches

In the dynamic landscape of project management, supply chain, and logistics, the overarching goal is to efficiently plan, execute, and optimize operations to meet organizational objectives. Embracing the latest technological advancements, this topic integrates cutting-edge tools such as ERPs, IoT, and data analytics to enhance project visibility, supply chain transparency, and logistics efficiency. Sustainability is a fundamental consideration, with a focus on minimizing environmental impact through eco-friendly supply chain practices, waste reduction, and energy-efficient logistics solutions. Recognizing the pivotal role of human factors, the topic emphasizes effective leadership and organisation teams’ collaboration to navigate the complexities of diverse and globalized workforces. Given the international scope, students explore the intricacies of managing projects, supply chains, and logistics across borders, considering global market dynamics. Furthermore, the topic delves into the social impact of these management practices, encouraging students to evaluate socially responsible initiatives that contribute positively to the communities in which they operate.
learning_outcomes: Articulate the relationship between corporate strategy, project management, operations, and supply chain management
Integrate technology into project management, operations, and supply chain management planning
Critically analyse and propose quality improvement initiatives to optimize operational processes
Explore the interconnected functions of forecasting, sourcing, purchasing, and logistics in a dynamic international business environment

title: International Study Tour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Gain an appreciation of the cultural of the country (or countries) visited Experience the world of a student at an international educational institution Build an understanding of social, political and cultural issues in other countries Increase the understanding and skills needed to operate in a global world

This topic enables students to undertake an organised study tour to an international location. The details of individual International Study Tours will vary depending on the destination, the timing, the host organisation(s), the number of students, etc.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of major social and cutural issues relating to the country (or countries) visited
Demonstrate an understanding of the skills and attitudes needed to travel and operate in the country (or countries) visited
Discuss inter-cultural differences between the country (or countries) visited and their own
Demonstrate an increase in intercultural competence

title: International Study Tour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Gain an appreciation of the cultural of the country (or countries) visited Experience the world of a student at an international educational institution Build an understanding of social, political and cultural issues in other countries Increase the understanding and skills needed to operate in a global world

This topic enables students to undertake an organised study tour to an international location - in person or virtually. The details of individual International Study Tours will vary depending on the destination, the timing, the host organisation(s), the number of students, etc.
learning_outcomes: Discuss inter-cultural differences between the country (or countries) visited and their own
Demonstrate an increase in intercultural competence
Demonstrate awareness of major social and cutural issues relating to the country (or countries) visited
Demonstrate an understanding of the skills and attitudes needed to travel and operate in the country (or countries) visited

title: Social Media Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of social media marketing concepts and tools, and how they can be applied in a business context. It is aimed at raising student awareness of the ways social media platforms can impact businesses, and create new opportunities for them to achieve their marketing objectives. Students will learn how and why marketers use certain platforms to attain a desired objective, and how to use different metrics to interpret the success of these tactics. They will also learn how to plan, develop and implement strategies.

In this topic, through the use of collaborative and interactive approaches, students will learn about various social media platforms and best practices in social media marketing. In addition to examining the social media platforms, the topic covers analytical tools (marketing metrics) in relation to social media, implementation of social media strategies or tactics and the evaluation and impact of social media activities on buyer behaviour. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the ways social media marketing can be used to transform traditional business practices, and help businesses utilise social media platforms to improve their competitiveness. In applying this knowledge, students assume the role as consultants and work with real clients, with the ultimate aim of providing them with business advice that is actionable and evidence based.
learning_outcomes: Explain different metrics in relation to social media
Critically evaluate the effectiveness of various social media marketing platforms
Recognise the importance of social media marketing in overall marketing strategy of a business
Evaluate the impact of social media marketing on buyer behaviour and the market
Describe various social media marketing platforms
Design and implement social media marketing strategies and/or tactics

title: Procurement and Managing Supply Chain
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the principles, practices and issues relevant to effectively manage procurement in organisations. The students will evaluate the processes and systems in place for purchasing and managing supply bases. This topic aims to: Allow students to appreciate the strategic importance of the procurement function Provide students with the understanding of the purchasing policies, procedures, laws and ethics Provide students with the understanding of the key elements in strategic sourcing and link to competitiveness

This topic aims to provide students with a foundational understanding of the theories and concepts required to effectively manage procurement in organisations. Procurement involves sourcing, purchasing and selection of supplies to an organisation and hence is crucial for an efficient supply chain. As such the topic outlines the purchasing procedures and practices, key elements in strategic sourcing and analysis methods for effective procurement decision making.
learning_outcomes: Analyse business scenarios by applying purchasing and supply management theories and concepts and recommend solutions
Describe purchasing and supply management concepts, theories and principles
Critically reflect on the procedures, techniques and elements in the purchasing and supply management process, their strategic importance for organisations and the present challenges
Work collaboratively with team members to conceptualise and synthesise information obtained from various resources to develop and present an account of knowledge in purchasing and supply management
prerequisites: 18 units of BUSN topics

title: Sports Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with in-depth knowledge of sports marketing theories, practices and develop skills to critically examine and analyse marketing in sports and of sports.

This topic will provide students with a fundamental understanding of the theories and practices in the field of sports marketing. Students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to market sports products, sports teams, and various stakeholders linked to sports management. It will prepare students to examine and apply marketing knowledge to sports and in sports.
learning_outcomes: Formulate marketing strategies for sports organisations and products
Evaluate the marketing practices of sport-related offerings
Identify target markets and market segmentation of sports organisations and products
Analyse real-world application and industry practices in the sports marketing context
Apply fundamental concepts in marketing principles and consumer behaviour in sports context

title: Revolutionising Accounting Processes
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide the information required to evaluate information systems and controls, including emerging technologies. It considers the role of the Accounting Information System in helping an organisation to meet its business aims. The importance of internal controls to corporate governance as it relates to Accounting Information Systems are also explored.

This topic introduces different types of Accounting Information Systems and their impact on business processes. It introduces emerging technologies and considers their use in data analysis and decision making.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate accounting information systems for specified cases
Analyse and record business transactions using appropriate technologies
Appraise Accounting Information System elements and discuss their functions in relation to data analysis and decision making
Explore accounting information systems to analyse, interpret and communicate issues for given cases
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1001, BUSN1202

title: Building Resilience and Professional Skills
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to consider the application of resilience and emotional intelligence in dealing with challenges in today’s business environments. It also promotes diversity and inclusion in a professional context and aims to develop interpersonal skills in both formal and informal situations, including effective communication, active listening, and teamwork.

This topic is designed to empower students with an understanding of the fundamental skills to cope with challenges in today’s world. Students will be encouraged to prioritise their mental health by being resilient and they will also develop interpersonal skills in the professional context.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the value of diversity and inclusion, including contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities
Evaluate options and priorities in managing conflicts
Demonstrate teamwork and collaboration skills in achieving organisation goals
Practice resilience and emotional intelligence in thinking
Apply interpersonal skills in the professional context
prerequisites: 36 units of topics

title: Law for Decision Makers
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop students' understanding and appreciation of the Australian system of commercial law; Enable students to recognise legal problems and their implications when they arise in commercial and business practice and settings; and Provide students with the knowledge and tools to be able to seek legal advice or to make appropriate referrals to legal professionals, when and where required.

The topic provides an introduction to aspects of Australian law relevant to business including: The Australian Legal System; Agency and Business Structures; Law of Contract; Law of Property; Law of Torts and Trade Practices (Consumer Protection and Restrictive Trade Practices) to enable students to recognise legal problems and their implications.
learning_outcomes: Analyse scenarios involving commercially relevant legal issues
Interpret common forms of legal advice sought by businesses and organisations
Explain the obligations that arise and the remedies that are available in various business settings
Explain common legal responsibilities and risks of doing business for a range of business structures and operations
Explain legal concepts relevant to a range of business structures and operations

title: Applying Economics for Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to cover: critical concepts and terminology, how to read and interpret economic information, types of economic markets and their relationship to a range of business types, and the role of key players and influences on economic conditions.

This topic is designed to equip businesses and decision-makers with the crucial insights into economics necessary for enhancing strategic planning and operational effectiveness. It explores the choices and interaction of key economic decision-makers—consumers, producers, firms, regulators, and governments—examining their impact on businesses, operating in a range of markets.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the effect of economic factors and conditions on business planning and operation
Evaluate the role of economics on decision making by individuals, businesses and government and different types of market structures
Interpret determinants of economic conditions and markets
Critically apply fundamental principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics

title: Harnessing the Power of FinTech
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide a deeper insight into the concept of fintech, specifically to increase understanding of how the application of digital technology is disrupting the financial services industry. It explores the fintech sector and various business models and applications in Australia.

This topic is designed to enable students to understand the importance of financial technology (fintech) in the dynamic business environment. The topic provides students with contemporary knowledge in digital technology, such as blockchain technology and AI, and its applications in the financial services industry.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the role of banks and financial services within the Fintech ecosystem
Assess the application of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence in financial services
Appraise the emergence and implications of new financial technology
Analyse the structure and drivers of the Fintech sector
Differentiate between Fintech business models in Australia

title: Financial Markets in Action
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to introduce students to the structure, function, and participants of domestic and international financial markets. It seeks to develop students’ ability to analyse market dynamics, interpret financial instruments and data, and apply foundational tools to evaluate financial activity and its impact on economic and business decision-making.

This topic provides students with a practical and analytical understanding of how financial markets operate, both domestically and internationally. It examines the roles of key financial institutions and explores the instruments and mechanisms that underpin equity, debt, and foreign exchange markets. Students will investigate how financial markets facilitate capital flow, influence economic activity, and respond to policy and global developments. The topic also introduces government-related aspects of financial markets, such as public debt and monetary policy. Through real-world data and case studies, students will develop the skills to interpret market dynamics and assess the implications of financial activity for businesses, investors, and the broader economy.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the structure and operation of foreign exchange markets and perform calculations involving exchange rates
Apply basic analytical tools to interpret financial data and evaluate market activity
Evaluate the characteristics and functions of international financial markets and their role in global capital flows and financial integration
Differentiate between major financial instruments and markets, including debt, equity, and foreign exchange
Investigate the structure and function of financial markets and the role of financial intermediaries
prerequisites: 1 BUSN1030

title: Smart Contracts in the Digital Economy
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a practical and conceptual understanding of smart contracts and their role in the evolving digital economy. Students will learn how smart contracts function, explore their potential to improve efficiency and trust in business processes, and critically assess their implications from legal, ethical, and strategic perspectives. The topic encourages students to engage with real-world examples and propose responsible applications of smart contracts in various industries.

Smart contracts are reshaping how agreements are made and executed in the digital economy. This topic introduces students to the foundational concepts, benefits, and challenges of smart contracts, with a focus on their application in business and economic contexts. Students will explore how smart contracts operate within blockchain systems, examine real-world use cases, and evaluate the legal, ethical, and strategic implications of their adoption.
learning_outcomes: Interpret the structure and function of smart contracts
Evaluate the legal, ethical, and operational considerations involved in the use of smart contracts
Analyse real-world applications of smart contracts across different sectors of the digital economy
Critically assess the strategic opportunities and risks that smart contracts present to businesses
Propose responsible and practical smart contract-based solutions to address business challenges

title: Supply Chain Analytics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with knowledge and skills to analyse the typical decision problems involved in the major domains of supply chain and help them to master the analytical tools, techniques and methods which can be utilised to solve those problems.

Use of information and data analytical tools help managers to more efficiently and effectively design and manage their supply chains by making informed decisions regarding sourcing, warehousing, production and capacity management, distribution network design, transportation and risk analysis. This topic is designed to help graduates to develop skills for generating value from data and making better decisions regarding material flows in the supply chain. The topic also provides students with insight into supply chain digitalisation and how technology advancements and big data solutions influence supply chain analytics. The topic builds on skills in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics which are applicable in various domains of supply chain.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the fundamental perspectives of supply chain analytics and the influence of digitalisation on supply chain management
Apply supply chain analytics techniques to support decision-making across supply chain functions
Analyse the applications of data analytics across the domains of the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model
Formulate analytical models for SCOR domain areas
prerequisites: 18 units of BUSN topics

title: Transforming Economies for Sustainable Development
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to equip students with the knowledge and analytical skills to understand and evaluate the intersection of economic development and sustainability. Students will develop a critical awareness of the SDGs and their implications for economic policy and practice, and will be encouraged to think creatively about how economies can be transformed to support long-term social, environmental, and economic well-being.

This topic explores the transformation of economies through the lens of sustainable development, with a particular focus on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Students will critically examine how economic systems, institutions, and policies can be reimagined to address global challenges such as poverty, inequality, climate change, and resource scarcity. The topic encourages students to consider the roles of governments, businesses, and civil society in shaping inclusive and sustainable economic futures.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the economic, social, and environmental dimensions of selected SDGs
Interpret the key concepts and principles underpinning sustainable development and the SDGs
Evaluate policy approaches and institutional frameworks that support or hinder sustainable economic transformation
Formulate evidence-based recommendations for advancing sustainable development in specific economic contexts
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Assessing Domestic and International Wine and Spirits Markets for Profitability
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of how the wine and craft spirit market operates (with respect to regulatory, economic and retailing aspects) both locally and internationally. It will allow students to gain insight into key special markets such as monopolies and quasi-monopolies; the overarching wine marketing system, including importers, retailing, e-commerce, cellar door sales and wine tourism and how those consuming and purchasing wine and craft spirits behave with respect to taste preferences, presentation (bottle design), traditions, general preferences as well as the trends in international wine markets.

This topic explores the domestic (Australian) wine and craft spirits markets as well as key international markets, i.e. those that are leading importers wine (UK, USA, China and other emerging such as India) and the growing export markets for craft spirits. Students are provided with valuable insights into different market structures and variabilities and how these potentially effect profitability. Hence, market attributes are evaluated on both macro levels, and more micro levels with individual firm capabilities and business goals included.
learning_outcomes: Analyse distribution channels in selected target markets with respect to supply and competition on the basis of national and international wine market reports
Compare the links between laws, regulations, levels of competition and supply with regard to origin, price, and types and varieties of wine using appropriate language and inco-terms
Analyse market opportunities in target markets and plan appropriate export and market entry strategies
Compare and discuss the structure of legal and tax frameworks (free markets, monopolies and quasi-monopolies) in examined countries and regions

title: Developing an International Wine Brand
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with key insight into the: Nature and concept of brands as symbolic and experiential values added to products and services Capacity to create and communicate brands to targeted customers in both domestic and international markets Fundamentals and principles of tailoring brands while establishing and managing consumer-brand relationships

Successfully creating and managing brands is a subject of high relevance to companies ranging from small to medium to multinational. As a function of marketing, brand management involves the planning and analysis of how a brand is perceived in the market. All activities centre on attracting and then building a close relationship with targeted consumers. The course is structured in such a way that students will be introduced to brand benefits, narratives, names, logos, brand personality, consumer-brand relationships, brand communications, brand-scapes, and pricing. The topic will also introduce students to the challenges of international brands, specifically with respect to addressing the challenges of cultural variables in a selling context.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse examined brand concepts
Conduct research to assess the potential of new and existing brands in domestic and international markets
Develop a brand concept (e.g., for wine, spirits or craft beer)
Explain the key principles of creating and managing brands (wine/craft spirits)

title: The Business of Making Wine
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an understanding of the key processes involved in the production of different wine styles in the Australian context, including the various costs involved in the many stages of product development and retail; potential problems and how to manage or mitigate against them. Students will gain insight into the range of considerations needed when establishing wine grape growing business from grape to table.

This topic provides students with an understanding of the key processes involved in the production of different wine styles in the Australian context. Students will also gain an understanding of the Australian wine landscape and will learn about the different types of product and production variabilities in the local wine industry. The topic also explains the influence and importance of Australia's numerous wine regions through directed and self-directed study and sensory assessment of some of Australia's typical wine styles. The topic also covers the processes and basic costs of winemaking, problems caused by common wine faults, and the importance of winery efficiency in the context of business returns and environmental stewardship.
learning_outcomes: Assess management and production risks
Explain basic terms used in winemaking
Describe the key winemaking processes used to produce wines of different styles
Construct basic budgets for production of different wines
Classify and discriminate between key wine styles and the contributing wine grape varieties

title: Wine and Spirits in a Digital World
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with insight into the technologies transforming industrial production and agribusiness; how various technologies support and improve both vineyard and distillery productivity while supporting customer management and development and how some of these concepts may be linked to tourism engagement. It will also cover the use of analytics and other digital strategies such as e-commerce to support marketing and distribution. Additionally, the topic aims to provide students with an understanding of the principles of the international wine & spirits action market in the context of provenance, tampering, counterfeits and tracking.

The rise of new digital technology in industry - i.e. Industry 4.0 - has provided transformation that makes it possible for companies to source and analyse data across machines, enable more flexible, faster and efficient processes to produce at reduced costs, higher quality goods and services. While much attention is given to the impact and role of Industry 4.0 in manufacturing, the wine industry too is being transformed, made more productive and enhanced due to the incorporation of digital developments and capabilities. This topic will provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the digital landscape across the wine and spirits sector. This includes the use of big data & analytics, blockchain as part of the 'Internet of Things' and fintech, horizontal and vertical systems of integration, AI, the cloud, cybersecurity, distribution solutions, CRM and digital marketing.
learning_outcomes: Develop a digital management plan for that relates to their individual area of industry interest (i.e. wine and/or distillery management, winemaker, sommelier, wine tourism, marketing, operations, international sales, etc.)
Explain the key principles and the role of digital technology in the wine and spirits sector
Assess decisions and actions to identify areas for improvement
Investigate opportunities to assess the potential of new and existing digital technologies to impact the wine & spirits industry

title: Successful Strategies for Wine Tourism
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with key insight into the theoretical foundations of Wine Tourism, providing an understanding of key concepts and terms, skills in team work and access to cutting-edge knowledge and research about strategic product development, branding and marketing, distribution and fund raising and financial management.

The tourism industry is regarded as the largest industry in the world. Wine tourism is a rapidly growing segment with continued change, growth, and impact. For wine business, wine tourism is a critical value added, as it is regarded as among the most significant sources of business-to-consumer wine sales. For visitors, wine tourism can offer an immersive cultural and sensory experience. To capitalize on wine tourism, businesses must understand their position within a destination, diverse tourist profiles, tourist preferences for wine experiences, and translate visitor experience preferences into memorable, innovative experiences. Like any other business, furthermore, wine tourism businesses must also take actions to minimize negative and maximize positive impacts on the environment, communities, and economies; such commitment to sustainability is increasingly expected among consumers and positions sustainability as business best practice. In this topic, students will be introduced to the fundamentals of tourism, contemporary trends in the global wine tourism industry, and best practice in wine tourism with a focus on sustainability, technology, and innovation.
learning_outcomes: Appraise a wine business’ sustainability practices
With an emphasis on sustainability, technology, and/or innovation, reflect on contemporary trends in wine tourism and present findings
Demonstrate proficiency in foundations of tourism
Critically assess a wine tourism destination using key performance metrics
Relate essential wine tourism concepts to real world practice

title: Wine Evaluation, Rating and Pricing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to wine tasting as a professional activity. Aspects of taste and other sensory sensations are discussed alongside their relationship to specific wine styles (including the impact of specific production techniques), pricing and food pairing. Students will gain an understanding of the differing approaches to tasting taken by a range of professions and how each describes wine differently. Wines from key world regions will also be discussed as well as the fundamentals of wine rating systems.

Wine Evaluation, Rating and Pricing aims at exploring and conducting the fundamentals of tasting wine in a professional way, describing and evaluating wines, rating them and understanding the linkages between rating and wine pricing. Instructors and students will be using a globally accepted and applied rating system based on the 20- and the 100-point schemes. Additionally, pricing structures will be explained with respect to tasted wines and the relationship between objective wine attributes, their rating and subsequent likely expected price in market. Different market channels (and associated pricing structures) are also analysed and discussed (cellar-door price for end users/consumers, retail price restaurants, retail price traders). Topics include all important facts, parameters and terms to know for tasting, evaluation and the price estimation of wines.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate various wines by describing their physiological structure, fundamental tastes and other sensory sensations
Categorise selected 'Key tastes of the wine world' (e.g. German Riesling, Porto, Champagne, Burgundy, Tokaj etc.)
Conduct a wine tasting in a professional way, using tastes in wine components and applying the fundamentals of wine descriptions
Rate and price a wine
Apply the basic components in traditional wine and food pairing

title: Digital Marketing and Analysis
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students understanding and application of digital business concepts associated with Digital Marketing and Data Analysis. It is aimed at raising student awareness of the ways digital marketing can impact on existing businesses, how digital marketing can create new opportunities and assist organisations in achieving their marketing and business goals. Students will be introduced to the various concepts around digital marketing and how to apply them effectively.

This topic covers a whole range of concepts in digital marketing and analysis, including customer acquisition, conversion, retention, customer relationship management, website evaluation, search engine optimisation (SEO) and search engine marketing (SEM). As an Industry Project based topic, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the ways digital marketing technologies can transform traditional business practices, and help businesses utilise digital solutions to improve their competitiveness. In applying this knowledge, students will assume the role of consultants and work with real clients, with the ultimate aim of providing them with business advice that is actionable and evidence based.
learning_outcomes: Examine digital marketing and the various online business models
Formulate a strategic approach to the adoption of digital marketing technologies through engaging with live clients
Analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of websites
Determine digital marketing infrastructure necessary for successful communications both within the organisation and with business partners
prerequisites: 36 units of any topics at any level

title: Reducing Uncertainties with Business Planning
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic empowers you to become a risk-aware business professional. You will develop the ability to create a risk-mitigated business plan that fosters sustainable business growth. Through critical analysis, and proactive risk planning, you'll gain the confidence to navigate uncertainties and launch a successful venture and steer the organisation towards success.

In today's dynamic business landscape, uncertainty is inevitable. This topic equips you with the essential tools and knowledge to minimize risk and navigate the challenges of starting or managing a business. You'll build a robust business plan that acts as a risk mitigation roadmap, guiding strategic decisions and boosting greater chances of success in organisations.
learning_outcomes: Utilize diverse presentation techniques to craft a compelling business pitch that highlights a proactive approach to risk management strategies
Apply a problem-solving approach to identify potential business opportunities and market needs, considering industry trends
Develop risk mitigation strategies for key business areas to minimize potential disruptions
Develop a comprehensive, viable and sustainable business plan based on market and data analysis, integrating risk management strategies and contingency plans
Integrate strategic management principles into the business planning process, fostering adaptability and adoption of emerging technologies to address emerging risks
prerequisites: 1 54 units of credit completed 2 ^ BUSN2026 3 Admission into BCAFS-Bachelor of Creative Arts (Fashion) 4 36 Units of credit completed 5 BUSN2026 Must Satisfy: ((1 and 2) or (3 and 4 and 5)) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently
incompatibilities: 1 of BUSN2006, BUSN2016, ECON2015, ECON2014, ECON3038, COMP3200

title: Personal Financial Planning
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the ability to: Describe and analyse the personal financial planning profession as a part of the financial services industry Apply relevent regulatory framework within which financial planning activities are performed Understand the financial reporting, taxation and mathamatical concepts useful in personal financial planning Apply financial instruments in developing financial plans Search and analyse the implications of other factors, such as the social security system, insurance protection, and estate planning, on the financial planning process Understand the process involved in developing personal financial plans Demonstrate the information, literacy and communication skills required by financial planners

Personal financial planning has become more important for those individuals who seek some advice on financial planning, financial planners and the government regulators who ensure that ethical standards are maintained by the professionals in giving planning advice. Furthermore personal financial planning has become more prominent in the product range offered by traditional financial services providers such as banks and investment funds. This topic is presented in two main stages. First, it introduces the role of financial planners and the regulatory framework within which financial planners are required to operate. Second, it examines various aspects of personal financial planning such as credit, estate planning, insurance, investment, social security, superannuation, and taxation. These key aspects help the development and implementation of sound personal financial plans.
learning_outcomes: Identify the legal management and regulatory framework of the Australian Securities and Investment Commission (ASIC) (assignment/examination)
Identify the role of pricing and performance management in enhancing the knowledge of financial management (assignment/examination)
Describe skills required by the financial planner in ethics, disclosure and dispute resolution process (case study and assignment)
Describe the issues of taxation, allowable deductions, income, planning and dividend imputations (assignment/examination)
Describe superannuation and retirement planning options along with insurance (assignment/examination)
Discuss the cost and benefits of credit and ownership of fixed assets including home ownership (assignment/examination)
Explain the role of financial planners and the premier industry associations (assignment/examination)

Demonstrate the relationship between ethics and regulatory requirements (eg good faith, utmost good faith, full disclosure of remuneration/fees and any other conflicts of interest which may influence the adviser's recommendation (case study and assignment)
Examine the benefits available under the social security net, the need of wills, and the use of power of attorney in estate planning (assignment/examination)
Examine investment either directly into various asset classes or managed funds (assignment/examination)
prerequisites: 1 1 of ECON2001, ECON2002, ECON2008, COMM2001, BUSN2007, BUSN2037, BUSN2013, BUSN2040, BUSN2014, BUSN2043 2 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1210, BUSN2008 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Marketing for Health, Sustainability and Social Impact
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic immerses students in the exciting world of health, sustainability and social marketing through a wide range of behaviour change applications aimed to benefit individuals, organisations, communities, and society.

This topic provides students an opportunity to discover the world of social, health and sustainability marketing through innovative teaching designed and delivered by a team of active social marketers at the Centre for Social Impact (CSI) Flinders, along with their industry partners who will use real-life case studies to help students develop applied knowledge and practical industry-relevant skills of behaviour change.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate social marketing theory, mix and factors influencing behaviour change of individuals, communities and society
Work independently and collaboratively
Critique key health, sustainability and social marketing concepts, in application to industry case studies
Develop and analyse evidence-informed comprehensive social, sustainability and health marketing plans

title: Navigating Investments and Portfolio Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop students’ understanding of investment selection and portfolio management by integrating theoretical frameworks with practical application. Students will explore the valuation and analysis of individual securities, asset allocation strategies, and portfolio performance evaluation. The topic also considers the evolving landscape of investment management, including the impact of alternative assets, financial technologies, and ethical standards, with a focus on the Australian investment environment.

This topic introduces students to the principles and practices of modern portfolio theory and investment management. It explores the concepts of risk and return, the functioning of securities markets, and the analysis and valuation of financial assets. Students will examine portfolio construction and performance evaluation, with attention to recent developments such as alternative investments, FinTech, and ESG. A portfolio simulation exercise is integrated into the topic to provide practical experience in investment decision-making.
learning_outcomes: Appraise modern portfolio theory and critically evaluate asset pricing models and asset allocation strategies
Critique recent developments in portfolio management, including ethical and professional standards
Assess appropriate risk-return trade-offs for different investment vehicles
Evaluate economic and firm-level information to assess a range of investment opportunities
Justify investment decisions involving alternative assets based on risk, return, and diversification benefits
prerequisites: ^ 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1030, BUSN2007, BUSN2037 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Managing Risk Through Derivatives
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to develop students’ understanding of financial risks and the role of derivative instruments in managing them. Students will build the analytical and practical skills needed to assess different types of risk exposures, evaluate hedging strategies, and apply derivatives effectively in real-world financial contexts.

This topic explores the nature of financial risks and the use of derivative instruments to manage them in both domestic and international markets. Students will examine the structure, pricing, and strategic application of derivatives such as forwards, futures, options, and swaps. Emphasis is placed on understanding how these instruments are used to hedge various types of financial risk and support effective risk management strategies. Through applied analysis and real-world case studies, students will develop the skills to evaluate and implement derivative-based solutions in dynamic financial environments.
learning_outcomes: Apply pricing models to determine the fair value of derivative instruments
Evaluate the use of derivatives and quantitative tools within financial risk management frameworks
Design derivative-based strategies to assess performance and identify arbitrage opportunities
Assess the role of derivative instruments in managing risks across various financial contexts
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1030, BUSN1210, BUSN2008, BUSN2057

title: Work Health and Safety
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this Work Health and Safety (WHS) topic is to instil in individuals a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices necessary for creating and maintaining safe, healthy, and productive work environments. Through this topic, individuals learn to identify and assess potential hazards, develop strategies for risk management, and ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulations. The overarching goal is to foster a culture of safety within organizations, encouraging proactive measures to prevent accidents and injuries. Additionally, WHS aims to promote employee well-being, both physically and mentally, recognizing that a healthy workforce contributes to increased productivity and overall organizational success. By integrating sustainability principles, adapting to technological advancements, and considering the global context, teaching WHS equips individuals with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the complexities of modern workplaces and contribute to a culture of safety and well-being for all.

Work Health and Safety (WHS) is a dynamic and inclusive discipline designed to ensure the safety, health, and overall well-being of individuals within the workplace. This multifaceted subject integrates technological advancements to enhance safety protocols, employing tools like sensors and digital platforms for real-time monitoring and risk mitigation. Sustainability is a core principle, guiding environmentally conscious practices, ergonomic design, and an emphasis on long-term health. In the context of globalization, WHS acknowledges the diverse cultural and regulatory landscapes of different regions, aiming for universal standards that transcend borders. Additionally, it recognizes the social impact of its strategies, promoting inclusive and socially responsible workplaces that prioritize diversity, mental health, and community well-being. WHS, therefore, serves as a global framework that adapts to technological innovations, sustainability imperatives, and the interconnected nature of today's workforce, striving to create workplaces that are safe, sustainable, and socially responsible on a global scale.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply the laws, regulations, and global standards related to Work Health and Safety (WHS) to risk assessment and response formulation
Evaluate the relationship of work health and safety to operational and strategic planning
Assess the role of technology in risk mitigation and creation of safe workplaces
Identify potential workplace hazards, assess associated risks, and formulate effective risk management strategies

Critically argue the significance of individual and collective behaviours in shaping workplace safety climates, including in relation to psycho-social wellbeing, use of technology, distributed and remote workers and changing workplace practices
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN2009, BUSN2038

title: Reward and Performance Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a complete understanding of the components of the performance management cycle and the link to strategic objectives.

This topic will cover reward theory: content and process theories, the design of salary and wage systems aligned to business strategy, equality and equity, performance related pay, job design and work organisation, job evaluation, performance appraisal, objective setting and giving feedback, dealing with poor performance
learning_outcomes: Analyse and redesign an existing job set to improve performance and employee satisfaction
Advise on appropriate corrective and disciplinary approaches to deal with poor performance
Conduct an appraisal interview, and give sensitive feedback, including the setting of SMART objectives
Advise on the design and implementation of appropriate reward policies aligned to organisational objectives
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1021, BUSN2009, BUSN2038

title: Employee Relations
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an overview of employment relations issues in historical and contemporary contexts. This includes an understanding of the way in which work is organised, the nature of the employment relationship, and the plurality of interests amongst stakeholders. It also aims to track emerging international issues in the field.

Industrial relations theory and perspectives: unitarist, pluralist, radical, partnership. The nature of industrial conflict; The development of employee relations in Australia; The role of the state (including legislative framework), unions, employers and their associations; interests of other stakeholders. Workplace bargaining and dispute resolution processes; International issues.
learning_outcomes: Be conversant with various models of bargaining and types of workplace agreements
Understand the main theories of employment relations
Be able to identify emerging international issues relating to employment relations
Critically analyse the development of the Australian employment relations 'system' including the regulatory environment
Understand the nature of industrial conflict and be aware of the options available for dispute resolution
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN2009, BUSN2038

title: Import-Export Theory and Practice
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students with an appreciation of the past and present context of international trade Provide students with an understanding of the numerous organisations, at various levels, that impact on the import/export activities of a firm Teach students how to undertake research and identify opportunities for organisations in overseas markets Provide students with the skills to properly price goods to be bought or sold in international markets Introduce students to the documentation necessary to undertake international trade Provide students with an appreciation of the payment methods commonly employed during import/export activities

This topic outlines the process of importing and exporting theory, and deals with the practical issues associated with import/export activities. As such, the topic provides a history of international trade and then presents the current trends in global exporting. It explains the organisations and factors impacting on import/export activity and how to identify overseas opportunities. It then examines market research and entry, INCOTERMS, payments, risk management, pricing, transportation, and foreign currency issues among other things. Students will take on the role as consultants and work with real clients, with the ultimate aim of providing them with business advice that is actionable and evidence based. In doing so, students will work with them to critically analyse the organisations readiness to export a product overseas, critically analyse the product readiness for export, identify the strengths and weaknesses of the company, and develop a plan for the organisation to export its products overseas.
learning_outcomes: Properly price goods to be sold overseas
Undertake research that helps you identify overseas opportunities and engage in international trade
Organise the shipment of goods to or from overseas countries and deal with the documentation associated with these transactions
Understand the current international trade environment
Devise appropriate payment terms and strategies
Appreciate the role of global, national and local organisations in the trade of goods internationally
Understand what INCOTERMS are and their role in import/export activity
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1004, BUSN2019 2 Admission into BIBWST-Bachelor of International Business (Wine, Spirits and Tourism) Must Satisfy: ((1) or (2))

title: Services Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the skills to examine the particular needs of service marketers. Students will learn how to interpret and apply different methods of marketing, and be introduced to the standard 7P's designation. The focus will also be on government and not-for-profit services as well as the more traditional professional and ancillary service sectors.

The topic outlines the services sector, the differences between services and goods, the consumer and services, the marketing of services, the issues in services impacted by customer satisfaction and ethics, and the future of services marketing.
learning_outcomes: Explain the differences between the marketing of services and the marketing of goods
Describe how the services sector fits within the context of economic indicators such as GDP, employment, trade balances, taxation and policy making
Recognise consumer issues in relation to pricing, delivery, promotion and satisfaction measures of services
Compare and contrast the ethics of services marketing and the ethics of marketing goods
Compare and contrast the methods by which consumers make decisions with respect to the purchase of services and products
Discuss the specific importance and application of the three service-related marketing mix concepts; people, physical representation and process
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1022, BUSN1206, BUSN2025

title: Governing Sustainably and Ethically
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to principles, practices and contemporary issues relevant to business sustainability, governance, and ethics. It also aims to assist students in developing analytical and presentation skills.

This topic introduces students to contemporary issues in business sustainability, corporate governance, and ethics. These issues are at the heart of many of today’s critical challenges and debates locally and globally. This topic emphasizes critical analysis of real-world issues and challenges in sustainability, governance, and ethics, application of topic concepts to real world practice, discussion, and case studies. The topic also assists students in the development of report and presentation skills.
learning_outcomes: Effectively interpret core concepts in sustainability, governance, and ethics
Examine contemporary issues in sustainability, governance, and/or ethics and present findings in a professional manner
Relate sustainability, governance, and/or ethics concepts to real world practice
Appraise a company’s sustainability practices and alignment with global sustainability guidelines

title: Industry Placement
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge and skills through a placement in a business setting. The placement experience is designed to help the student become more fully prepared for a business career.

Students undertake an industry placement with the aim of increasing employability skills. Students are placed and matched with placements according to availability and suitability or students can source their own placement with approval. Students are prepared for their placement, enter into a learning contract to guide the work integrated learning experience and are supervised.
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively and appropriately with peers, industry professionals and supervisors; convey information clearly and fluently in high quality verbal and written forms appropriate for a professional audience
Engage effectively, professionally and ethically in a diverse, workplace setting
Reflect upon your learning from University and apply disciplined based knowledge and skills to a professional workplace
Develop personal goals to enable you to enhance your personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practice in a business setting

title: Marketing Planning and Strategy: Contemporary and Future Focused
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce the concepts and tools used in strategic marketing Provide an understanding of the importance of marketing strategies in business Develop an ability to analyse market opportunities in a variety of differing market contexts Develop an ability to formulate marketing strategies and develop marketing plans

This topic deals with the place a marketing plan has within the overall business plan of an organisation. It examines the marketing strategies most appropriate under a range of different market and product life-cycle circumstances. Finally, it provides a template for developing a marketing plan that meets the needs of the organisation's aims and objectives within the context of a particular product and market.
learning_outcomes: Identify and collect the information necessary to produce a viable marketing plan
Outline the requirements for the effective implementation of marketing plans
Create a strategic marketing plan that is consistent with an organisation's overall objectives
Analyse market based data for opportunities relevant to an organisation
Describe the various marketing strategies that are appropriate for different product contexts
Explain where marketing plans fit within the organisation's overall business plan
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN2015, BUSN2025, BUSN1022, BUSN1206

This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge and skills through a placement in a business setting. The placement experience is designed to help the student become more fully prepared for a business career.

Students undertake an industry placement with the aim of increasing employability skills. Students are placed and matched with placements according to availability and suitability or students can source their own placement with approval. Students are prepared for their placement, enter into a learning contract to guide the work integrated learning experience and are supervised.
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively and appropriately with peers, industry professionals and supervisors; convey information clearly and fluently in high quality verbal and written forms appropriate for a professional audience
Demonstrate effective, professional and ethical engagement in a diverse, workplace setting
Reflect upon your learning from University and apply disciplined based knowledge and skills to a professional workplace
Develop personal goals to enable you to enhance your personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practice in a business setting
