title: Start-up Ventures
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge and skills through an applied business project; to help students take an idea and find a viable business model which is scalable and repeatable, from scratch.

Students undertake an enterprise or innovation project. Students will be guided by experienced individuals who have either built successful companies or fund them. This opportunity is available to students when appropriate projects are identified and where student knowledge and ability matches the needs of the project.
learning_outcomes: Make effective presentations to financiers or Boards to secure resources and/or support for projects
Write a professional business report
Apply business knowledge to applied business settings
Conduct research on a business issue in depth and develop plans
Assess new business propositions
Develop more effective skills working in a team and manage team dynamics in a professional manner
Use the skills necessary to develop a business model
prerequisites: 1 Admission into the Bachelor of Commerce and its specialisations 1a Admission into the Bachelor of Business and its specialisations 2 54 units of any topics at any level Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a) and 2)

title: Corporate Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to the important theoretical foundations and principles that underpin modern corporate finance practice Develop an understanding of the relationship between corporate finance theory and practice and effective and responsible governance, decision making and business objectives

This topic is concerned with the theory and practice of financial management of business corporations. The concepts and issues introduced in BUSN2037 will be extended to consider investment, financing and valuation decisions of the firm at a more advanced level, and also interactions between these decisions. A number of more applied topics will also be covered including real options, corporate acquisitions, corporate restructuring, and corporate governance.
learning_outcomes: Describe the theories and applications surrounding a merger or a takeover and the similarities and differences
Describe and apply the main techniques for risk management using financial instruments
Explain the significance of agency problems and corporate governance and contrast different corporate governance regimes around the world
Identify and evaluate the role of risk in determining project cost of capital
Apply real options analysis and credit risk analysis
Evaluate investment decisions under uncertainty using a range of evaluation methods such as sensitivity analysis and decision trees analysis
Identify the various types of corporate restructuring transactions
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN2007, BUSN2037

title: Auditing and Assurance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce the nature and function of audit engagements in Australia and the statutory responsibilities of auditors, ethical implications, and the legal consequences of an audit. It introduces the audit process including audit planning, risk and internal control assessment, substantive testing procedures, statistical sampling, and the reporting and communication of audit findings to relevant stakeholders.

This topic is designed to introduce the nature and purpose of auditing and the regulatory environment in which it operates, and the professional, ethical, and legal responsibilities of auditors. It considers the role of auditing to financial reporting and has an emphasis on auditing standards and their application to the audit process.
learning_outcomes: Determine the appropriateness of different types of audit opinions and explain the key features of an audit report
Evaluate the regulatory and professional requirements of auditors and apply relevant rules, standards and pronouncements to a financial statement audit
Assess the nature and purpose of auditing
Appraise audit planning, risk assessment and evidence gathering techniques, including sampling and substantive testing, and the use of computer-assisted audit techniques
prerequisites: BUSN2036

title: International Human Resource Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to issues in, and strategies for, managing the workforce in international business operations. Much of the topic is based on international business case studies and International Human Resource Management (IHRM) theory, research and practice, and involves a high level of student participation. Students will be expected to develop an understanding of: IHRM vs. domestic HRM International HRM planning, staffing and organisational structure International recruitment and selection Staff training and development Expatriation and repatriation Performance appraisal and compensation International employment relations Managing multicultural teams Managing diversity HRM issues in international joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions

This topic provides students with an introduction to issues in, and strategies for, managing the workforce in international business operations. It extends basic principles in Human Resource Management (HRM) to the international business arena, and examines HRM issues that are distinctive features of global, transnational and multidomestic business operations. Areas covered include: international HRM planning and staffing; international recruitment and selection; staff training and development; expatriation and repatriation; international employment relations; managing multicultural teams; managing diversity; performance appraisal; compensation; HRM issues in international joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and report on the IHRM components of contemporary business operations including IHRM planning, recruitment, staff training and development
Investigate and critically analyse IHRM theory and research
Compare and contrast the issues in relation to international HRM and domestic HRM
Analyse international business cases, with particular emphasis on IHRM elements
Discuss international employment relations and problems in managing multicultural teams

title: Building Leaders of the Future
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to cultivate critical thinking skills to evaluate existing leadership theories and frameworks and effectively develop relevant leadership skills necessary to navigate the complex and ever-evolving business landscape. By integrating technology, human factors and social responsibility dimensions into the study of leadership, the topic prepares you to lead effectively the workforce of the future.

This topic equips you to become a future-ready leader by fostering a critical understanding of the dynamic interplay between people, technology and social responsibility dimensions within the leadership domain. In this topic, you will explore the core theories and principles of leadership, delve into ethical considerations, and analyse how technology, human and social factors shape leadership in the 21st century and vice-versa. You will gain critical insights into various leadership styles, communication strategies, and techniques for influencing and motivating teams in a diverse and tech-driven environment. The topic also examines the importance of diversity, cultural awareness and strategies to effectively lead through change and crisis in a rapidly changing environment.
learning_outcomes: Critically apply strategies to effectively communicate, inspire and motivate the future workforce
Apply effective change management strategies to lead and inspire teams through crisis in a rapidly changing business environment
Navigate complex situations in business ethically and responsibly, leading with a strong sense of social purpose
Critically evaluate various leadership styles, theories, and frameworks, and their application in diverse and technologically driven work environment
prerequisites: 36 units of any topics at any level

title: International Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the concepts and tools used in international marketing. International marketing is a subject that touches several small to medium to multinational companies, and can be defined as how various parties satisfy their needs through exchange. The thrust of international marketing is to manage this exchange process at an international level. The effect of internet/ e-commerce on international marketing will be evaluated. This topic will introduce students to a strategic approach to the international marketing mix. It will ultimately lead to an appreciation of the complexities of developing an international marketing strategic plan. Its aim is to investigate: The role of international marketing in society and the organisation The environment of international marketing Foreign consumers and foreign markets Product strategies for world markets International distribution strategies International dimensions of pricing strategies International dimensions of promotion strategies The opportunities of marketing to the bottom of the pyramid The service organisation in international markets Managing international distribution channels The internet and international marketing

Students will be introduced to international marketing research, product development, pricing, distribution, exporting and promotion. The topic will examine problems of global strategic marketing, strategic formulation in multinational marketing, managing network connections in international business and the internationalisation of service firms. The myth of globalisation, the role of bribery, gift and donations on negotiating, the impact of international law and international marketers, the role of international marketing in society and the firm, the impact of the internet and international market and the environment of international marketing are critically investigated. Bottom of the Pyramid Marketing will be analysed as a new paradigm shift in marketing to developing countries, in a way that jointly reduces poverty and adds profitability to a firm. Sustainable issues in international marketing are discussed as a path to corporate social inclusion.
learning_outcomes: Design an international marketing research process
Analyse case studies of international marketing
Develop an international marketing plan
Demonstrate skills in researching international markets
Demonstrate skills of analysing economic, political, legal and cultural aspects of global trading environment
Explain the concepts and tools used in international marketing and the difference between domestic and international marketing
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1022, BUSN1206, BUSN2025 2 36 units of BUSN topics Must Satisfy: (1 or 2)

title: Using Strategy for Business Transformation
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to equip students with a multifaceted understanding of competitive advantage, fostering a dynamic perspective on how macro-environmental trends and industry-level analysis can enhance organisational transformation.

This topic will enable students to leverage strategy to drive fundamental change and achieve sustainable competitive advantage and business transformation. Specific areas covered in this topic includes the importance of organisational strategy in determining performance and the role of such factors as mergers, acquisitions and strategic alliances, product positioning, strategic marketing in relation to business transformation, innovation and globalisation. By applying the knowledge, students will act as transformation consultants, working with real clients to develop actionable strategies for achieving breakthrough results.
learning_outcomes: Develop evidence-based transformation strategies for real clients, demonstrating the effective use of strategic levers while considering stakeholder perspectives and alignment.

Critically evaluate the effectiveness of organizational strategies as drivers of firm performance, considering the influence of Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal factors
Critically assess an organisation’s internal capabilities and external environment to identify opportunities and challenges for business transformation.
Apply strategic theories, concepts and frameworks to develop effective organisational strategies for business transformation
prerequisites: 1 72 units from any topics 2 1 of BUSN1007, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2028, BUSN1020, BUSN2054 3 1 of BUSN1001, BUSN1011, BUSN1201, BUSN1202 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2 and 3)

title: Navigating International Trade and Policies
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to equip students with a robust understanding of international trade theories and policies. It emphasizes the application of economic models to analyse trade data and policy impacts. Students will develop advanced analytical and empirical skills, enabling them to interpret trade-related datasets and assess theoretical frameworks. The topic also fosters the development of clear and effective communication of economic insights.

This topic explores the practical dimensions of international economics, emphasizing the exchange of goods and services across borders. The topic uses trade theories and models to understand global trade patterns and evaluate policy issues. The topic also emphasizes trade benefits, the impact on income distribution, effects of tariffs, and trade barriers.
learning_outcomes: Estimate empirical models of international trade using contemporary econometric techniques and theoretical foundations
Assess the effects of various forms of government intervention in international trade, including tariffs and subsidies
Evaluate the economic benefits and challenges of international trade and the implications of global economic integration
Appraise the role of the World Trade Organization and regional trade agreements in shaping the global trading system
Analyse the economic forces shaping the global division of labour and assess their impact on labour markets
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1007, BUSN1013, BUSN1020, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: International Placement
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide a practical orientation to the workplace in preparation for a business career. This orientation takes the form of a placement experience in an international business setting.

Students undertake an industry placement while abroad. Students are placed and matched with placements according to availability and suitability; or students can source themselves with approval. Students are prepared for their placement, enter into a learning contract to guide the work integrated learning experience and are supervised.
learning_outcomes: Apply business knowledge to professional work situations in another country
Demonstrate the ability to operate effectively in an international workplace

title: Human Resource Strategy and Change Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic is the capstone topic of the human resource management specialisation and it aims to integrate and extend the professional and theoretical knowledge and skills provided in earlier topics in the specialisation to align outcomes of the HR capabilities of strategic architects, stakeholder managers and culture and change agents.

This topic is the capstone topic in the Human Resource Management specialisation. It focuses on the concepts and processes for understanding strategic human resource management and the management of change in contemporary organisation settings, the role of the HR professional as strategic architect, stakeholder manager, and culture and change agent, and the application of that knowledge to improve business performance through human resource effectiveness. Topics addressed include HR strategy and policy, the HR professional as an agent for change and strategic architect in creating dynamic and productive organisational environments; developing excellence; improving workforce competency and creating profitable and sustainable organisations.
learning_outcomes: Analyse strategic human resource and change management issues and make recommendations on human resource management actions to contribute to a profitable and sustainable organisation, increase workforce competency and engagement, develop excellence in people management and create a dynamic and productive work environment
Identify, discuss and apply the theory and practice of strategic human resource management
Demonstrate knowledge of the role of the HR professional in these activities
Identify, discuss and apply the theory and practice of change management
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN2009, BUSN2038

title: Interpreting Financial Statements
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this subject is to introduce fundamental valuation theory and concepts and a framework for business analysis and valuation using both financial and non-financial data. It will evaluate competitive and corporate strategy analysis, factors influencing the quality of financial statements and develop an understanding of business analysis and valuation applications.

This topic introduces a framework for using financial statement data in a range of business analysis and valuation contexts. It will develop the knowledge required in a range of business analysis and valuation applications.
learning_outcomes: Determine required accounting adjustments in the recasting of financial statements for business analysis
Assess business valuation theory concepts and the external and internal environmental factors that influence the strategy of an organisation
Evaluate information from various sources to undertake business analysis and valuation
prerequisites: BUSN2036

title: AI, Cybersecurity and the Future of Work
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the knowledge and capabilities to address the challenges and opportunities presented by rapid developments in technologies and cybersecurity in the evolving workplace. Through critical analysis and practical exercises, students will explore ethical considerations in the use of advanced and cutting edge technology, common cybersecurity threats, and their impact on jobs, skills, and inequality. Students will gain the skills to navigate technological change processes, contributing to the design and management of solutions that prioritise both human well-being and socio-economic advancement.

This topic examines the practical implications of advanced technologies, transformative business models and national/domestic digitalisation policies and strategies for the future of work, professions, and workplaces. It will enable students to critically examine the likely impact of rapid advancements in technology and digitalisation on work, including technological challenges like cybersecurity and automation, from a multi-disciplinary perspective. The topic will provide students with a foundational understanding of Industry 5.0 and its socio-economic and cultural impacts. Students will have the opportunity to work on real-world problems and interact with cutting edge technology preparing them for the future of work.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and participate in debates surrounding the Fifth industrial revolution and Industry 5.0
Apply tools to assist with the management of workplace and technological change
Collaborate effectively with the team to develop a cohesive conceptualisation of the future of work, focusing on the social, political, and economic impacts of technological change processes
Critically assess the implications of digitalisation on the future of work, workplaces, and society by linking the theories of technological change and practices
Align discipline-specific skills with current industry requirements, employability trends, and potential employment opportunities with a strong future focus
prerequisites: 36 units of any topics

title: Logistics and Supply Chain Strategy
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with in-depth knowledge of concepts of logistics and supply chain strategy and develop skills to critically analyse a company's supply chain strategy in practice.

Effective supply chain and logistics strategy drive improved business performance. Supply chain management can play a strategic role in delivering customer value and companies can achieve competitive advantage through leveraging the management of their supply chains. This topic is designed to provide graduates with in-depth knowledge of the concepts of logistic and supply chain strategy. They will also learn how companies in practice can utilise the supply chain strategy to respond to the needs of end-consumers and build competitive advantages.
learning_outcomes: Apply the appropriate supply chain strategy concepts and theories to critically analyse the real-life business cases
Explain the concepts and theories of logistics and supply chain strategy and how they can be operationalised
Evaluate the appropriateness and effectiveness of a company's supply chain strategy considering the supply chain strategy drivers
Discuss how companies can compete through their supply chains
prerequisites: 18 units of BUSN topics

title: Supply Chain Analytics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with knowledge and skills to analyse the typical decision problems involved in the major domains of supply chain and help them to master the analytical tools, techniques and methods which can be utilised to solve those problems.

Use of information and data analytical tools help managers to more efficiently and effectively design and manage their supply chains by making informed decisions regarding sourcing, warehousing, production and capacity management, distribution network design, transportation and risk analysis. This topic is designed to help graduates to develop skills for generating value from data and making better decisions regarding material flows in the supply chain. The topic also provides students with insight into supply chain digitalisation and how technology advancements and big data solutions influence supply chain analytics. The topic builds on skills in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics which are applicable in various domains of supply chain.
learning_outcomes: Effectively use supply chain analytics techniques with computing packages such as Excel
Explain the applications of data analytics along the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model domains
Explain the fundamental perspectives of supply chain analytics and how digitalisation may influence supply chain management

Formulate the analytical models along the SCOR model domain areas (demand forecasting, supplier selection, inventory management, production and capacity planning, transportation problems, and distribution network design)
prerequisites: 18 units of BUSN topics

title: Sports Leadership and Governance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to prepare students for a career in sports and develop skills and knowledge in sports development, leadership and business management, to prepare them for career in sports industry or other business-related areas.

This topic will introduce students to leadership skills and knowledge in sports context. Students will learn various leadership theories and how they apply in sports settings.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the systemic governance of sport and the role of the board in managing external relations
Evaluate the actual practice of leadership, applying relevant theories, frameworks and concepts in sports context
Critically examine the contribution of leadership to effective sport organisations

title: Sports Law
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide an understanding of principles of law that are relevant to sports, and enhance students' ability to apply these principles, as well as to critically discuss those laws relevant to sports.

This topic will provide students with in-depth understanding of sporting contracts, commercial law, competitive law in sports, sporting tribunals, laws and policies related to discrimination and misconduct in sports. Students will apply principles of law in relation to sporting organisations, teams and products.
learning_outcomes: Develop the capacity to use the law as a resource in a sports environment

Critically discuss the development of mechanisms for the legal regulation of sport including such issues as sport-related governance, dispute settlement, the commercial regulation of sport, and the anti-doping in sport regime
Describe the legal issues that are common in sports law practices
Demonstrate understanding of state, national and international law in relation to sports

title: Credit Analysis and Lending Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
Students will develop an understanding of credit risk analysis and management Students will develop an understanding of loan types, structures and lending practices Through problem solving activities students will develop critical analysis and skills and ability to clearly communicate outcomes of analysis

This topic provides an introduction of the various lending activities of Australian financial institutions and the risks related to these activities. It includes credit risk assessment, credit risk management, and the management of lending activities. Methodologies related to structuring a loan, traditional techniques for credit analysis, distressed firm prediction and reviewing of the newer models of assessing credit risk will be discussed. Retail lending, commercial lending, corporate lending and corporate services and valuation of assets will be explored.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the behavioural aspects associated with lending decisions
Analyse the risk return characteristics and pricing of a loan application
Examine the major types of lending products from basic economic principles
Apply statistical techniques used in decision making at the approval, monitoring and termination stages of lending
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1210 2 1 of BUSN1009, BUSN1209 3 1 of BUSN1001, BUSN1202 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2 and 3)

title: Engaging with Industry
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to enable students to gain practical skills through engagement with industry partners.

This topic is designed to enhance employability skills. Students will be given an opportunity to engage with industry partners to apply knowledge and practice their skills gained from the course.
learning_outcomes: Apply a broad range of technical, digital, and professional skills in a business context
Critically evaluate the personal and professional development derived from the industry project, at both an individual and team-based level
Assess a wide range of business issues and contribute to developing possible solutions

title: International Business Finance and Banking
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide an understanding of financial management in an international setting. At the outset we study the macro-environment in which the multinational firm operates. This encompasses an understanding of: The forces of globalization and its implications for the multinational firm The operation of the international financial system, its current state, challenges for the future Determination of exchange rates, and their relationship with interest rates and inflation Consequences of misalignment of exchange rates, the origins of financial crises The second part of the topic addresses foreign exchange risk management challenges faced by firms operating in an international setting. Specifically, we examine: Different types of foreign exchange exposure faced by the MNC Identification and measurement of these risks Management of foreign exchange risk via initiatives on, as well as off the balance sheet. The use of derivative instruments will be considered in detail The third part of the topic addresses financing issues and options faced by international banks: The structure of international financial markets and institutions, the range of instruments traded therein Innovations in international financing, the forces leading to these innovations, the role they play, the mechanisms facilitating trade in financial assets across national boundaries

This topic examines the financial issues facing firms and banks involved in the international transfer of assets, goods and services. The main topics explored will be the foreign exchange market, the management of foreign exchange risk, and investment and financing decisions in international capital markets.
learning_outcomes: Identify the characteristics of international capital and foreign exchange market
Identify and analyse current issues in international banking
Develop strategies to deal with other types of country risks associated with foreign operations
Identify risk relating to exchange rate fluctuations and develop strategies to deal with them
Evaluate alternative international trade finance options
Identify and appraise investment opportunities in the international environment
prerequisites: 1 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1210 2 BUSN2037 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: HR Information Systems & Analytics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop your critical thinking and analytical skills to understand the design, implementation, and utilisation of HRIS effectively. You'll learn to leverage technology and data for strategic HR decision-making, while considering the human factor and the social responsibility implications of HR data management.

This topic equips you with the knowledge and skills to navigate the dynamic world of HR information systems (HRIS) and analytics in the digital age. We'll explore the strategic and administrative value of HRIS for organisations. You'll gain insights into HRIS technologies, data management principles, and how to leverage analytics to optimise HR processes and decision-making. The topic also examines ethical and legal considerations surrounding HRIS, preparing you to navigate this critical aspect of modern HR management.
learning_outcomes: Develop and present evidence-based recommendations for HRIS implementation, considering ethical and legal frameworks for data management
Critically evaluate HRIS technologies and examine issues related to the use of HRIS in organisations
Critically analyse the strategic value of Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS), considering ethical implications
Utilise HRIS platform to support human resource functions
Apply HR analytical techniques in HRM functions for effective decision-making

title: Data Warehousing and Decision Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary to design, implement, and manage data warehouses as well as making students familiar with tools to facilitate decision making process. Students will also be introduced to key concepts such as fundamentals of data warehousing, ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes, data quality, and data warehouse architecture.

This topic introduces the critical need for data warehousing and covers essential aspects, including data warehouse architectures, design, and modelling. Emphasizing data quality and the implementation process (including ETL), students will learn how data warehouses facilitate decision-making by offering an integrated repository of high-quality data, enabling flexible and multi-dimensional retrieval and analysis. Additionally, the topic explores effective utilization of decision-making tools within data warehouse environments.
learning_outcomes: Justify the purpose and significance of data warehousing within organisations
Discuss principles of data warehouse design
Assess the impact of data quality on decision-making
Argue and critique real-world scenarios where data warehousing plays a crucial role
Evaluate how data warehouses support decision-making processes
prerequisites: COMP1711

title: Responsible Financial Decision-Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop students’ ability to make informed and ethically sound financial decisions in complex and evolving business environments. It focuses on building awareness of professional responsibilities, understanding the impact of financial decisions on stakeholders and society, and applying frameworks for ethical reasoning and sustainable finance. Students will engage with contemporary issues in finance, including ESG integration, green finance, and the ethical challenges faced by financial professionals.

This topic explores the principles and practices of responsible financial decision making, with a focus on ethical conduct, sustainability, and long-term value creation. Students will examine the ethical responsibilities of finance professionals, the integration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into financial analysis, and the role of finance in promoting sustainable economic systems. The topic draws on global standards, including the CFA Institute’s Code of Ethics, to guide students in evaluating real-world financial decisions through an ethical and sustainability lens.
learning_outcomes: Apply ethical principles to assess the impact of financial decisions on diverse stakeholders and broader societal outcomes
Evaluate ethical dilemmas in financial decision-making using established professional standards and ethical reasoning frameworks
Appraise financial practices for their adherence to integrity, transparency, and accountability in line with professional ethical codes
Develop responsible financial recommendations that align with sustainable finance principles and long-term value creation
Analyse the role of sustainable finance in shaping long-term financial strategies and responsible investment decisions
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1014, BUSN1030

title: Exploring FinTech Revolution in Banking and Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a practical and strategic understanding of FinTech innovation and its impact on the banking and finance sectors. Students will explore the technological enablers of FinTech, evaluate its influence on financial services and customer expectations, and assess how institutions can adapt and compete in a rapidly evolving digital environment. The topic encourages students to think critically about disruption, innovation, and the future of financial services.

The financial services industry is being rapidly transformed by FinTech innovations that are redefining how banking, payments, lending, and investment services are delivered. This topic explores the technologies, business models, and market dynamics driving the FinTech revolution. Students will examine how FinTech disrupts traditional financial institutions, assess emerging trends such as digital wallets, robo-advisors, open banking, and embedded finance, and develop strategic responses to innovation. The topic emphasizes applied analysis, innovation strategy, and future-focused thinking in the context of digital financial transformation.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the technological foundations and market forces driving FinTech innovation
Design innovative and practical FinTech strategies or solutions that respond to real-world financial needs
Evaluate the impact of FinTech on traditional financial services, customer experience, and competitive dynamics
Appraise emerging FinTech business models and platforms across different segments of the financial industry
Assess the strategic challenges and opportunities FinTech presents for incumbents and new entrants
prerequisites: 2 of BUSN1030, BUSN2056

title: Business Strategy with Game Theory
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to develop students’ ability to think strategically using the principles and tools of game theory. Students will learn to identify strategic situations, model interactions between economic agents, and predict likely outcomes using equilibrium concepts. The topic fosters analytical reasoning, structured problem-solving, and the ability to apply strategic thinking to a range of business contexts, from competition and cooperation to regulation and innovation.

This topic introduces students to the strategic foundations of business decision-making through the lens of game theory. Students will explore how firms and individuals make interdependent decisions in competitive and cooperative environments, using formal models to analyse strategic interactions. Emphasis is placed on applying game-theoretic tools to real-world business scenarios such as pricing, market entry, negotiation, and strategic partnerships. The topic balances theoretical understanding with practical application, equipping students with a strategic mindset essential for navigating complex business environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse strategic issues in business scenarios using a game-theoretic perspective
Apply game-theoretic tools to analyse strategic problems and predict likely outcomes
Interpret core concepts of game theory and their relevance to strategic decision-making in business contexts
Evaluate the usefulness and limitations of game-theoretic models for informing business and policy decision
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Optimising Decisions with Behavioural Economics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to deepen students’ understanding of economic behaviour by examining how psychological factors influence decision-making. Students will learn to critically evaluate the limitations of standard economic models, explore the role of experimental and empirical evidence in behavioural economics, and apply behavioural insights to improve outcomes in economic, business, and policy contexts. The topic encourages reflective thinking about personal decision-making and the design of more effective interventions and policies.

This topic introduces students to behavioural economics, a field that integrates insights from psychology into economic thinking to better understand how people make decisions. It challenges the traditional assumptions of rationality and self-interest by exploring cognitive biases, heuristics, framing effects, and social preferences. Students will apply behavioural economics principles to tackle complex real-world problems and critically examine how behavioural insights reshape traditional economic models. Building on this foundation, they will develop evidence-based interventions to optimise decision-making across business, government, and everyday life.
learning_outcomes: Apply behavioural economic principles to analyse and interpret economic behaviour in practical contexts
Explain key behavioural economic concepts and how they differ from traditional economic assumptions
Evaluate the effectiveness of behavioural interventions in addressing economic and policy challenges
Analyse how cognitive biases and heuristics influence individual and group decision-making in economic contexts
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Understanding Taxation Systems
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce taxation law and the administration of the taxation framework, including income tax, the Goods and Services Tax, capital gains tax and fringe benefits tax. It identifies and applies taxation principles associated with calculating the taxable income and tax payable for individuals and business entities.

This topic introduces the sources of taxation law and the analyses and application of taxation principles to individuals, partnerships, and companies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the sources of tax law and framework of the taxation system in Australia
Determine the taxable income and tax payable for individuals and business entities
Assess various types of taxation including income tax, capital gains tax, fringe benefits tax and goods and services tax
prerequisites: 1 ^ BUSN2042 1a 1 of BUSN1029, BUSN2018 2 1 of LLAW2224, LLAW2323 Must Satisfy: (((1 or 1a)) or (2)) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Critiquing the Economics of Natural Resources
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to equip students with the analytical tools to understand and critique the economic principles underpinning natural resource management. Students will explore how economic models explain resource allocation, scarcity, and sustainability, and will evaluate the effectiveness of various policy instruments in addressing environmental and resource challenges. The topic encourages critical thinking about ethical, ecological, and intergenerational implications of resource use in Australia and globally.

This topic explores the economic dimensions of natural resource use, management, and sustainability. Students will examine how economic theory and policy tools are applied to renewable and non-renewable resources, including water, energy, fisheries, forests, and minerals. The topic critically evaluates market failures, property rights, and externalities associated with resource use, and considers the role of government, markets, and institutions in managing these challenges. Through real-world case studies and policy analysis, students will develop the skills to assess the trade-offs and complexities involved in balancing economic development with environmental stewardship.
learning_outcomes: Apply economic models to analyse issues involving renewable and non-renewable resource use
Identify key economic concepts related to the use and management of natural resources
Evaluate the effectiveness of policy instruments (e.g. taxes, permits, regulation) in managing natural resources
Assess the trade-offs and ethical considerations involved in natural resource policy and decision-making
prerequisites: 1 of BUSN1020, BUSN1013, BUSN1204, BUSN2054

title: Selling Wine and Spirits
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic 'Selling Wine and Spirits' aims to examine the major wine and spirits/craft beer distribution options to market, including cellar doors (wine/spirit/craft beer producers) and brand websites, fine wine stores and 'big box' outlets ('Bricks & Mortar' retailers), as well as online retailers (third party operators).

A significant moment in marketing wine, beer and spirits is centred around the point of purchase. This is the destination where consumers are faced with a vast range of products and ultimately decide on which brand to choose. This topic 'Selling Wine and Spirits' aims to examine the major destination options, including Cellar Doors (wine/spirit producers), Fine Wine stores and 'Big Box' outlets ('Bricks & Mortar' retailers), as well as Online retailers (third party operators). As part of this examination, students will look at the various paths to purchase employed by these different retailers, the strategies used to attract and retain sales plus emerging trends in wine and spirit consumer purchase behaviourist. Topics include select advertising strategies, target marketing, building customer relationships, the importance of brand stories, pricing, convenience, retail store layout.
learning_outcomes: Examine and critically analyse the impact of technology on existing and future consumer buying behaviours
Critically analyse the various retail categories and their potential
Conduct situational analysis to assess best options for retail strategy and develop a retail strategy for a wine, craft beer or craft spirit brand
Explain key principles of wine, beer and spirit retailing

title: Workplace Preparation
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to prepare students for topics with work integrated learning.

This workplace preparation topic is designed to combine industry insights, alumni experiences, and practical skill-building modules to ensure students are ready to apply, engage, and thrive in professional environments. Delivered prior to students undertaking their Industry Placement or Engaging with Industry topic through self-paced modules and interactive workshops, students develop capabilities in resume writing, interview techniques, professional conduct, and goal setting. The preparation topic additionally helps student make informed decision about their Work Integrated Learning topic choices.
learning_outcomes: Interpret insights from employers and alumni to generalise current industry expectations and emerging trends
Specify the value of Work Integrated Learning and relate the key differences between the Industry Placement and Engaging with Industry topics
Develop tailored resumes and cover letters, build a professional online presence, and practice effective interview techniques to secure placements and career roles

Demonstrate workplace readiness and professional conduct, such as communication, teamwork, cultural competency including indigenous awareness and ethical conduct, to perform effectively in diverse workplace environments
Construct a career development plan by combining reflective insights with SMART goal setting to guide their Work Integrated Learning readiness and growth
prerequisites: 36 units of study

title: Critical Readings in Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This research topic aims to develop students' abilities to read critically business related research papers. It also aims to develop critical thinking capabilities.

This is a research topic that allows students to focus on, and develop, their critical thinking abilities that will contribute to their understanding of business related research and ultimately their Honours thesis. This topic develops students' abilities to read critically relevant research works.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate critical thinking abilities through oral and written communications
Prepare a series of reports that critique business-related research papers
prerequisites: 1 Admission into HBCOM-Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) 1a Admission into HBBUS-Bachelor of Business (Honours) 1b Admission into HBBSC-Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Honours) 1c Admission into HBA-Bachelor of Arts (Honours) 1d Admission into GDPRM/BGL-Graduate Diploma in Research Methods Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d))

title: Future Leaders: Industry and Research Skills
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic has three aims: Enhance students' ability to communicate, publish and present research for academia and industry Develop students' interpersonal skills and applicability in professional contexts Increase students’ leadership capabilities and appreciation of diverse leadership styles

This topic prepares Honours students for future careers in academic, private or government sectors. The topic focuses on three central sets of competencies: presenting and communicating research, interpersonal skills, and developing leadership capacity. The topic concerns the practices and knowledge associated with the communication of research, which requires students to present their research in a variety of ways (other than the thesis), and for academic and non-academic audiences. The topic trains students in a range of verbal and written forms of communication relevant to their discipline and builds skills and confidence in relation to the sharing of research ideas and knowledge beyond discipline boundaries, within academic and public life generally. The topic also encourages students to reflect on principles of leadership, including their own, to build knowledge of diverse leadership styles and foster students’ capacity to lead, now and in the future.
learning_outcomes: Recognise the importance of interpersonal skills in diverse professional contexts and reflect on your own level of interpersonal competency and ways to further develop these skills
Evaluate different leadership and communication styles and use understanding of your own style and capacity to become a more effective leader
Communicate research to diverse audiences in both written and verbal form

title: Wine Tourism 4.0
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to facilitate insights into contemporary trends in wine tourism relating to Industry 4.0, and related elements of technology, sustainability, and resilience. Students will gain a holistic understanding of these multidimensional concepts and also learn how these concepts are applied in practice through an experiential education component. This topic further aims allow students to build skills in critical analysis on the challenges, opportunities, and innovations. Collectively, this topic aims to guide students in the: Examination of the multidimensional concepts of wine tourism, industry 4.0 and its relationship to sustainability, and resilience Assessment of innovation across the winescape Assessment of challenges and opportunities in Wine Tourism 4.0 Examination of Wine Tourism 4.0 concepts as applied in real-world practice

The tourism industry is regarded as the largest industry in the world. Wine tourism is a rapidly growing segment with continued change, growth, and impact. For wine business, wine tourism is a critical value added, as it is regarded as among the most significant sources of business-to-consumer wine sales. For visitors, wine tourism can offer an immersive cultural sensory experience. In an increasingly competitive and evolving landscape, wine tourism businesses must constantly innovate through diverse means, and identify how emerging technology can assist them in providing a state-of-the-art experience. Technology can also assist wine tourism businesses in marketing, product development, and service quality. Furthermore, wine tourism businesses must also take actions to minimize their negative, and maximize their positive impacts on the environment, communities, and economies; such commitment to sustainability is increasingly expected among consumers and positions as best business practice. At the same time, recent uncontrollable events, such as COVID-19, have significantly affected global tourism, underscoring the importance of resilience. Thus, the modern wine tourism industry must strive for best practice in sustainability and resilience. In this topic, students will examine contemporary trends in the global wine tourism industry with a focus on Tourism 4.0-5.0 emphasising innovation, technology, and sustainability. With this context, students will learn about successful strategies for building sustainability, resilience, and innovation in wine tourism.
learning_outcomes: Assessment of innovation across the winescape
Examination of the multidimensional concepts of wine tourism, industry 4.0 and its relationship to sustainability, and resilience
Assessment of challenges and opportunities in Wine Tourism 4.0
Examination of Wine Tourism 4.0 concepts as applied in real-world practice

title: Research Methods
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop student understanding of a range of research methods Introduce students to the most commonly used qualitative and quantitative research methods in the social sciences and how to design and implement them Familiarise students with the application of research methods to support examination of specific research questions Cultivate students' capacity to evaluate the benefits and limitations of a range of research methods

In this topic students will investigate the central importance of methodology in social science research. Students will be introduced to the most commonly used quantitative and qualitative research methods in the social sciences. Students will critically reflect on the relationship between research questions and research methods, the benefits and limitations of specific research methods, and how to design and implement a range of methods.
learning_outcomes: Justify commonly-used qualitative and quantitative research methods in the social sciences
Develop a research question based on an appropriate research method
Critique the benefits and limitations of a range of research methods
Discuss the appropriate use of a range of research methods

title: Honours Thesis (9/22.5 units)
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide an opportunity for students to develop an understanding of research and the skills necessary to conduct a study in an area of the student's interest, with the assistance of a supervisor Provide the chance to enhance research skills by working in an intensive way and reading widely on a particular issue Enable a student to show originality in the writing of an extended piece of argument which is supported by a range of evidence Adequately prepare the student for postgraduate work

Define an appropriate research problem and relate it to the relevant theoretical literature
Communicate research results clearly and concisely according to scholarly practice
Collect, and/or analyse and interpret data relating to the selected research problem
