title: Quantitative Business Research Methods
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Equip students with knowledge and skills in quantitative methods which they can apply to arrange of business research problems

Essential data management techniques: transformation of variables, seasonality, missing variables, frequency tables and cross-tabulation; Linear regression models; Use of dummy variables and interaction effects; Simultaneous-equation models; Time series models; Cross-sectional models; Panel data models; Logit and probit models for binary choice; Multiple choice models; Tobit models.
learning_outcomes: Prepare an individual project which features sound analysis of data and is correctly presented
Estimate different types of models using appropriate software
Understand and critique the data analysis of research papers
Model the relations among variables and draw inferences about relations

title: Driving Financial Performance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide an insight and understanding of the accounting process, specifically to increase understanding of what managers must do to make an organisation financially successful. No prior knowledge of accounting or work experience is expected. You will learn how to assess an organisation's current cash flow and profitable position together with how to deal with internal and external environmental complexities and constraints. An overview is provided on how businesses formulate, implement and control accounting practices. Topics covered include internal controls, financial statements and performance ratios. Cognitive skills are applied to analysing accounting information and evaluating options. Behavioural skills (especially personal and interpersonal skills) are applied in explaining and presenting different options.

Driving Financial Performance is designed to enable students to understand the importance of accounting and financial information in making strategic business decisions. The topic provides students with a fundamental understanding of accounting, in which students will be equipped with the skills to analyse and interpret financial statements. Emerging concepts such as fintech, blockchain, data analytics and sustainability reporting will also be explored.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the key aspects of financial performance and the financial position of an organisation and its significance in strategic decision making
Appraise accounting techniques critical to effective management decision making
Determine the basic concepts and principles of accounting

title: Ethics, Sustainability and Governance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to expose students to critical concepts and practice of sustainability, ethics, and governance in contemporary business. Students will examine the multidimensional concepts of sustainability, resilience, and corporate social responsibility. To convey how these concepts are applied in practice, students will examine global sustainability guidelines and other practical tools for business sustainability and resilience (e.g., certification programs, policies, codes of conduct). This topic additionally exposes students to concepts, issues, and challenges associated with governance and ethics, which are also relevant to businesses earning the social license to operate. Collectively, this topic aims to: Examine multidimensional concepts of sustainability, resilience, and corporate social responsibility Assess triple bottom line business practices Assess company alignment with global sustainability guidelines Examine ethical theories and ethical issues in the workplace Explore diverse governance structures and environmental, sustainability, and governance (ESG) ratings

Businesses impact communities, natural environments, and economies in which they operate, which can be both positive (e.g., job creation) and negative (natural resource exploitation). Because the modern businesses must also earn the social license to operate, it is critical that future business leaders are well versed in the concept and practice of sustainability, ethics, and governance. Addressing this imperative, students will gain an understanding of the multidimensional concept of sustainability and how it is applied in real world practice. Students will additionally engage concepts, issues, and challenges associated with governance and ethics. This topic embraces discussion, analysis of real-world issues in sustainability, ethics, and governance, and concept to practice analysis. This topic also assists students in developing research and presentation skills.
learning_outcomes: Relate essential sustainability, corporate social responsibility, and resilience concepts to real world practice
Appraise a company’s sustainability practices and their alignment with global sustainability guidelines
Relate essential ethics and governance concepts to real world practice
Critically evaluate a company’s governance structure

title: Building Teams and Networks
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide in-depth knowledge and skills on team building and networking skills in virtual and face-to-face contexts. Students will learn team dynamics, cohesion and interpersonal communication skills to effectively work, build teams and develop effective networks within, and across, organisations. Students learn how to engage with the team and capitalise on the power of diversity. Students evaluate different types of leadership styles for building and fostering teamwork in an era of Industry 4.0 and 5.0.

This topic equips students with advanced knowledge and skills on building workplace teams and networks which address strategic priorities and key challenges facing today's organisations. High performance teams and self-managed teams have created maximum impact in organisations in the way projects are effectively managed. Therefore, students will learn how to work in a team and be an effective contributor to the building of high-performance teams and networks. Subsequently, students will learn how to recognise valuable team and network relationships in the pursuit of organisational as well as personal career goals.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate team and network building models and frameworks
Assess the importance of capitalising on the power of diversity in teams and networks
Appraise team, cohesion, interpersonal communication and structure frameworks
Critically appraise the key challenges faced by employees and organisations working in, and with, teams and networks
Critically evaluate leadership styles for building and fostering team and network activity in times of discontinuity, Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0

title: Creating Resilient Supply Chains and Procurement
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the principles, practices and issues relevant to effectively manage procurement in organisations. The students will evaluate the processes and systems in place for purchasing and managing supply bases. This topic aims to: Allow students to appreciate the strategic importance of the procurement function Provide students with the understanding of the purchasing policies, procedures, laws and ethics Provide students with the understanding of the key elements in strategic sourcing and link to competitiveness

This topic aims to provide students with a foundational understanding of the theories and concepts required to effectively manage procurement in organisations. Procurement involves sourcing, purchasing and selection of supplies to an organisation and hence is crucial for an efficient supply chain. As such the topic outlines the purchasing procedures and practices, key elements in strategic sourcing and analysis methods for effective procurement decision making.
learning_outcomes: Critique organisations’ challenges in relation to supply chain management processes
Appraise supply chain theories in business scenarios to recommend solutions
Evaluate purchasing and supply management concepts, theories and principles

title: Leveraging FinTech and Digital Ecosystems
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide a deeper insight into the key ideas of fintech, specifically to determine how the application of digital technology is disrupting financial services. It assesses the fintech sector and various business models and applications in an Australian context.

This topic is designed to enable students to evaluate the importance of financial technology (fintech) in the dynamic digital ecosystem. The topic equips students with the practical application of digital technology, such as blockchain technology and AI, in the financial services industry.
learning_outcomes: Determine the role of financial services institutions in fintech and digital ecosystems
Evaluate the application of blockchain technology and AI
Assess the emergence of new technologies in accounting
Critique various fintech business models in an Australian context

title: Leadership for Social Impact
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to deepen students’ understanding of what it takes to lead transformational social change in for-purpose, for-profit and government sectors.

This topic guides students through the theory and practice of leadership to influence and drive social impact in any context. Students will examine values and mission-driven leadership, power and influence, leading for outcomes and cross-sector leadership with diverse stakeholders. Students will examine their own capacity to lead for social impact.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively
Critically evaluate contemporary theories of leadership and how these apply to efforts to influence and drive social impact
Determine the most appropriate leadership approaches to respond to the complexity of leading and collaborating for social impact
Assess leadership styles across the social impact ecosystem

title: Social Impact in Context
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to introduce students to the evolving concept of social impact and the context within which social impact is seen, considered and valued.

What is social impact? Why does it matter? This is a foundational topic in social impact. The topic provides an understanding of the evolving concept of social impact and its value to contemporary organisational practice, systems and communities.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively
Critique the value of social impact in contemporary organisational, community and political settings
Formulate social impact responses in a range of practical settings for real world impact
Discuss social impact processes and principles to demonstrate conceptual understanding

title: Innovation for Social Impact
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is for students to develop an understanding of the role of social innovation for social impact, with a focus on business models, cross-sector collaboration, and the application of design and systems thinking.

This Topic explores the difference between traditional innovation and social innovation, and how social innovation can influence, create, and drive positive social change as part of the social economy.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the ways that innovative business models create social impact
Critically evaluate the role of social innovation in a whole-of-system approach to addressing complex social issues
Demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively
Critique key concepts such as social innovation, systems thinking, and design for social innovation in real-world scenarios
Apply appropriate social innovation design methods and cross-sector collaboration techniques for social impact

title: Applying Principles of Project Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Integrate project management methodologies, tools and PMI® knowledge areas to manage tasks within defined scopes, timeframes and budgets. Formulate effective solutions to navigate project challenges and support innovation. Assess project demands and evaluate strategies for successful project execution and control. Justify project-related decisions by relating them to evidence-based practices and collaborative approaches across industries.

In this topic, you will be introduced to Project Management Principles by integrating essential methodologies, tools and Project Management Institute (PMI®) knowledge areas to help you effectively plan, organise and manage tasks within defined scopes, timeframes and budgets. You will examine a project life cycle that consists of key phases like initiation, planning, execution, monitoring and closure and develop the ability to formulate solutions, adapt to challenges and support innovation. By mastering these principles, you will be able to assess project demands, design collaborative approaches and justify decisions that support consistent success across diverse industries.
learning_outcomes: Select an appropriate approach for managing collaboration across local, virtual, and global project teams
Evaluate project management approaches to address dynamic project challenges across the project lifecycle
Justify project decisions through critical reflection on internal and external factors impacting outcomes
Design innovative project strategies by integrating theoretical frameworks to address evolving project scenarios

title: Data Analytics and Business Intelligence
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to give the graduate the confidence to explore business intelligence and various analytical approaches from both managerial and practical perspectives. In this topic, the students will be equipped with analytical tools and skills that can be applied to address real-world business problems and enhance the decision making process.

This topic gives the graduates the confidence to explore business intelligence and various analytical approaches from both managerial and practical perspectives. In this topic, the students will be equipped with analytical and artificial intelligence tools and skills that can be applied to address real-world business problems and enhance the decision making process.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of AI enabled data analytics and business intelligence in the decision-making process
Use data analytics/business intelligence tools to extract insights from different types of datasets
Evaluate and verify quality and accuracy of data for use in predictive and forecasting analysis.
Analyse and evaluate the ethical and social impacts of AI technologies in data analytics and business intelligence to support responsible decision-making
Identify trends, relationships and solutions to address operational and strategic business problems.
Critically evaluate the challenges, advantages and limitations of data analytics and business intelligence in the context of AI technologies
Summarise and graphically present data.
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MCDABI-Professional Certificate in Data Analytics and Business Intelligence Microcredential

title: Demonstrating Social Impact
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to introduce students to methods and frameworks for measuring, monitoring and evaluating social impact in human service delivery and other for-purpose activities.

The aim of this topic is to introduce students to methods and frameworks for measuring, monitoring, and evaluating social impact in human service delivery and other for-purpose activities.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the benefits and challenges of evaluation and social impact measurement, including in relation to specific frameworks and tools
Determine the most effective methods for demonstrating social impact in real-world scenarios
Demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively
Critically analyse key concepts in data collection, evaluation, and social impact measurement

title: Marketing Strategy and Decision Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with: The fundamental theories relating to strategic marketing Knowledge to recognise the strategic aspects of marketing and understand how the marketing strategy fits within the overall business strategy of an organisation An appreciation of the effects of the product life cycle on marketing plans, and the marketing mix, which includes product, price, promotion and distribution The skills necessary to decide between different marketing strategies and marketing plans for businesses

This topic introduces students to the topic of marketing strategy and how decisions are made when determining the best strategy. It provides an appreciation of where marketing strategies fit within the overall corporate and business strategies of an organisation, and the importance of these. The topic explains how the focus of marketing plans will vary according to the stage of the product's life cycle. Other key subject areas will include the marketing mix, target marketing, consumer segmentation, and strategic market planning.
learning_outcomes: Examine and analyse the internal and external environment that influences strategies and decisions
Explain various marketing concepts, their connection with marketing strategies and their application in a marketing plan
Identify the best approach amongst different alternatives when determining marketing strategy
Develop a concise marketing plan
Critique concepts and theories in relation to marketing strategies and planning
Identify tools and models for developing marketing strategy and planning
Use marketing planning concepts and critical thinking to provide the rationale for strategic decisions
Communicate well in a group environment and work collaboratively

title: Managing Project Risks
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Integrate theoretical frameworks, models, and tools to manage project risks effectively within diverse project environments. Assess potential project risks and determine proactive planning and response strategies. Formulate structured approaches for qualitative and quantitative risk analysis and mitigation. Justify risk response decisions by evaluating their impact on project objectives and stakeholder expectations.

In this topic, you will explore project risk management by integrating essential theories and concepts applicable to project environments. You will assess the importance of proactive risk planning, prepare appropriate response strategies and manage risks through identification, assessment, monitoring and control. You will learn qualitative and quantitative risk analysis techniques which will help you formulate structured approaches for effective risk mitigation. By evaluating risk impacts and justifying response decisions, you will develop the capability to design risk management strategies that support project objectives and enhance decision-making in complex project scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Formulate evidence-based insights and mitigation plans to support effective risk-related decision-making
Communicate risk concepts clearly while collaborating within diverse and distributed project teams
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of risk management frameworks and processes across the project lifecycle
Evaluate risk identification, analysis and response strategies to manage uncertainty in projects

title: Implementing Project Control Methods
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Integrate theoretical concepts and practical processes to manage and monitor project activities across the project lifecycle. Assess project schedules, costs, quality, scope and stakeholder relationships to ensure alignment with project objectives. Formulate structured approaches to risk control, communication, and process improvement in line with PMBOK® standards. Appraise project control practices to design effective methods that enhance project performance and delivery outcomes.

In this topic, you will explore project control methods by combining theoretical concepts with practical processes to effectively manage and monitor project activities. You will assess project schedules, costs, quality compliance, scope control and stakeholder relationships, while evaluating performance through monitoring, auditing and reporting. You will learn to formulate risk control measures, communication strategies and process improvement techniques. By appraising control practices, you will develop the ability to design structured methods that ensure project objectives are achieved efficiently and effectively.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge of project monitoring and control processes across the project lifecycle
Evaluate project control tools and techniques to improve decision-making and enhance project performance
Appraise project control data and concepts to support collaboration and stakeholder engagement
Adapt project control methods to effectively manage project environments

title: Organisational Behaviour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the core theories of organisational behaviour and management that underpin and influence contemporary Human Resource Management practices.

Roles and functions of managers; management and leadership styles; organisational structures; theories of organisational behaviour: perception, personality, communication, motivation; the formation and development of groups and teams; handling conflict and change.
learning_outcomes: Understand the core theories of organisational behaviour and their influence on contemporary human resource management approaches
Discuss the historical development of management thought with particular emphasis on the study of people in organisations
prerequisites: Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology

title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to the notion of entrepreneurship Give students an appreciation of the broader economic importance of entrepreneurship Provide knowledge and to develop skills which may assist students in becoming successful entrepreneurs Make students aware fo the special role of SMEs in the economy and the particular challenges facing small and medium enterprises

This topic focuses on the notion of entrepreneurship, its importance in the economic system, and on the skills and knowledge required to be a successful entrepreneur. Specific issues covered include: defining and understanding entrepreneurship; the role and importance of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in modern market-based economies; planning a new business venture; competitive advantage, marketing strategies and financing options; and forms of business ownership. The importance of entrepreneurial activity in promoting economic growth is also considered; as is the relevance of entrepreneurial concepts to managing larger businesses.
learning_outcomes: Explain the challenges in managing the growth of a small entrepreneurial firm and in 'harvesting' the wealth created by entrepreneurial endeavours
Define and discuss the concept of entrepreneurship and explain the challenges in being an entrepreneur
Identify and explain the important role played by entrepreneurs in realising economic growth
Identify and discuss the 'entrepreneurial process' and 'entrepreneurial outcomes'
Illustrate the development of analytical skills, communication skills and other skills appropriate to pursuing a career as an entrepreneur

Identify and explain the various challenges and issues involved in starting a small innovative business, including across areas such as researching and analysing business opportunities, formulating a business plan, addressing legal issues, analysing financial projections, obtaining finance, and developing a marketing strategy
Understand and explain the importance of small and medium enterprises to an economy and the particular challenges facing small and medium enterprises
prerequisites: Admission into MNT-Master of Nanotechnology

title: Sustainable Resource Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a solid understanding of the fundamentals of sustainable resource management, in particular, the basic skills required to deal with environmental issues from an economic perspective.

The objective of this topic is to introduce students to the basic concepts and techniques of sustainable resource management. These concepts and techniques are of great value to people wishing to work towards the sustainable management of environmental systems and the improved efficiency of resource use. The topic focuses on: The economic reasons for environmental damage and the means by which economic instruments can be used to alleviate environmental problems The economics of sustainable development The main areas covered include: market failure and the environmental problem; the economics of pollution; the concepts of discounting and present value; environmental valuation techniques; benefit-cost analysis; project evaluation; green national accounting; and sustainable development policy.
learning_outcomes: Identify appropriate policy solutions to environmental problems by combining an understanding of the fundamentals of environmental economics and the knowledge of environmental indicators
Identify environmental economic problems, the reasons for their existence, and the economic instruments applicable to their resolution
Demonstrate that you are adequately conversant with environmental economics data (in particular its strengths and weaknesses), national accounting statistics, and alternative economic indicators
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 BUSN9017 - Economics for Business Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Market Research
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to marketing research in its business context, as a means of assessing consumer markets nationally and internationally and providing a communication channel between consumers and management. It will develop a template for transforming business problems into research objectives, designing a research plan and communicating the results effectively to management. The topic will also address at an applied level a range of issues in the design and practice of market surveys and other research methodologies. The course will also aim to equip students with the skills to apply market research and develop and further enhance decisions to amend marketing mix factors of an enterprise.

This topic aims to provide an applied introduction to the theory and practice of marketing research, and its use as a management tool in business.
learning_outcomes: Analyse a marketing data base
Draw inferences from marketing research data using appropriate computer software
Explain the role of marketing research in providing information for management planning and control
Critique marketing research designs and make practical recommendations about future marketing research needs
How marketing research impacts on the nature of the international marketing mix factors modified by an enterprise
Develop group work, report writing and data analysis skills
Prepare a marketing research report for management and effectively present the results
Develop a qualitative and quantitative research instrument
Understand the different uses of marketing research in the business environment and as an aid to decision making, and the ethics involved in marketing research
Conduct exploratory marketing research based on focus groups and in-depth interviews
Perform survey-based descriptive research and relationship-based causal research
Methods of selecting and accessing marketing data
Understand the marketing research process
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 STAT5702 - Statistical Methods for Engineering and Science Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Human Resource Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to, and provide an overview of concepts, practices and functions associated with HRM. Students will be expected to develop an understanding of: The roles of HRM Strategic HRM HR planning Job analysis and design The legal context of HRM Recruitment and selection Performance management Remuneration Training and development Managing workforce diversity

This topic introduces students to, and provides an overview of, concepts, practices and issues associated with Human Resource Management (HRM). Key areas to be covered include: the roles of HRM, strategic HRM, HR planning, the law and HRM, job analysis and design including work-life balance, recruitment and selection, performance management, remunertion and training and development. The topic also provides a foundation upon which students may undertake specialised courses in areas including human resource planning; recruitment and selection; training and development; and reward and performance management.
learning_outcomes: Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with training and development
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with performance management
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with managing workforce diversity
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with strategic HRM
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with job analysis and design
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with the legal context of HRM
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with remuneration
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with recruitment and selection
Describe and discuss the roles, functions and practices associated with HR planning
prerequisites: Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology

title: E-Business
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the business concepts and models associated with E-Commerce. It is aimed at raising student awareness of the ways E-Commerce can impact on existing businesses, how E-Commerce can create new business and the issues facing consumers, business and society as a whole. Students will be introduced to the various E-Commerce business models and how they relate to business strategy. At the completion of this topic students should understand how E-Commerce is transforming traditional business practices and models and be able to identify the potential for existing businesses to utilise E-Commerce to improve their competitiveness.

This topic aims to introduce students to the business concepts of electronic commerce. It is an introductory topic aimed at raising student awareness of the ways electronic commerce can impact on existing businesses, how electronic commerce can create new business and the issues facing users. Students will be introduced to the various electronic commerce business models and how they relate to business strategy.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and evaluate the effectiveness of websites
Demonstrate an understanding of e-business infrastructure necessary for successful communications both within the organisation and with business partners
Outline the basic functions of online payment systems
Identify the types of online security threats and how they may be addressed
Show an appreciation of contemporary social, legal and business issues associated with e-commerce
Apply a strategic approach to the adoption of e-commerce by existing businesses
Evaluate the main elements of Supply Chain Management and its relationship to the value chain
Describe e-business and the various online business models
Discuss how traditional marketing approaches may be integrated with e-marketing and e-CRM
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MIT-Master of Information Technology 1a Admission into GDPIT-Graduate Diploma in Information Technology 2 36 units of any topics at any level Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a) and 2)

title: Services Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the skills to examine the particular needs of service marketers. Students will learn how to interpret and apply different methods of marketing, and be introduced to the standard 7P's designation. The focus will also be on government and not-for-profit services as well as the more traditional professional and ancillary service sectors.

The topic outlines the services sector, the differences between services and goods, the consumer and services, the marketing of services, the issues in services such as customer satisfaction and ethics, and the future of services marketing.
learning_outcomes: Recognise problems consumers have with the pricing, delivery, promotion and satisfaction measures of services - such recognition should cover these issues as they relate specifically to services as well as more generally to all marketing
Understand the specific importance and application of the three service-related marketing mix concepts - people, physical representation and process
Place the services sector within the context of economic indicators such as GDP, employment, trade balances, taxation and policy making
Discuss the methods by which consumer decisions are made for services in comparison with the ways they are made for products
Understand the differences between the marketing of services and the marketing of goods
Reach conclusions on the ethics of services marketing and how they differ from the ethics of goods marketing
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 BUSN9022 - Marketing Principles Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: International Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the concepts and tools used in international marketing. International marketing is a subject that touches several small to medium to multinational companies, and can be defined as how various parties satisfy their needs through exchange. The thrust of international marketing is to manage this exchange process at an international level. The effect of internet/ e-commerce on international marketing will be evaluated. This topic has primarily as its focus/aim to introduce students to a strategic approach to the international marketing mix. It will ultimately lead to an appreciation of the complexities of developing an international marketing strategic plan. To investigate: The role of international marketing in society and the firm The environment of international marketing The essence of international marketing Foreign consumers and foreign markets Product strategies for world markets (influence of internet) International distribution strategies (influence of internet) International dimensions of pricing strategies International dimensions of promotion strategies (influence of internet) The opportunities of marketing to the bottom of the pyramid The service firms in international markets Managing international distribution channels (influence of internet) Internet and international marketing

Students will be introduced to international marketing research, product development, pricing, distribution, exporting and promotion. The topic will examine problems of global strategic marketing, strategic formulation in multinational marketing, managing network connections in international business and the internationalisation of service firms. The myth of globalisation, the role of bribery, gift and donations on negotiating, the impact of international law and international marketers, the role of international marketing in society and the firm, the impact of the internet and international market and the environment of international marketing are critically investigated. Bottom of the Pyramid Marketing will be analysed as a new paradigm shift in marketing to developing countries, in a way that jointly reduces poverty and adds profitability to a firm. Sustainable issues in international marketing are discussed as a path to corporate social inclusion.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the ability to effectively design an International Marketing Plan from an organisational perspective
Make constructive recommendations for further improvement in international business exchanges with global customers
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 BUSN9022 - Marketing Principles Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Leadership in Business and Society
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to achieve: Understanding of the nature and importance of leadership in business and society Understanding of the differences between leadership and management An appreciation of the types of leadership and how they impact on business, society and those led An understanding of how leaders lead and how leadership is practised

The topic aims to teach those aspects of leadership relevant to business and society. Subjects covered will include: the nature and importance of leadership; the differences between leadership and management; types of leadership and their impacts on business, society and followers; how leaders lead and leadership in practice, leadership development, experiential leadership.
learning_outcomes: Develop leadership skills
Work within a group using both leadership and followership skills at appropriate times
Recognise leadership in practice in business and society
Initiate appropriate change through the application of well-chosen leadership strategies
Recognise the differences between management and leadership and know how and when to apply these differences
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 36 units of any topics at any level Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Strategic Management (BT)
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a solid understanding of the fundamentals of strategic planning, as it applies to businesses operating in modern competitive environments.

This topic is about competitive advantage and the fundamentals of realising and sustaining an 'above-normal' profit. The significance of both external and internal environments of the firm are explored, including concepts such as Michael Porter's Five Forces model and the Resource-Based View of the firm. Specific areas covered include: the importance of organisational strategy in determining firm performance; competitive rivalry and responses; mergers, acquisitions and strategic alliances; innovation; globalisation as a strategy; product positioning, strategic marketing and competitive pricing; and (if time) the role of executive compensation schemes. Case studies are used to illustrate concepts.
learning_outcomes: Explain the concepts of product positioning, strategic marketing and competitive pricing
Explain the notion of 'competitive advantage' and how a firm might acquire and sustain a competitive advantage
Explain importance of organisational strategy in determining firm performance
Explain when a strategy of globalisation may be appropriate
Explain when strategies such as diversification, mergers, acquisitions and strategic alliances may be appropriate
Explain the role of executive compensation schemes in affecting firm performance
Explain how and why industry specific factors affect the profitability of a firm
prerequisites: Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology

title: Financial Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the major concepts and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of financial management. The topic will cover the role and objectives of financial management, business financial planning and ratio analysis, working capital management, risk and return, capital budgeting, the capital market, sources of finance, the cost of capital, operating and financial leverage and the financial structure decision.

This topic introduces students to the major concepts and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of financial management. The topic will cover the role and objectives of financial management, business financial planning and ratio analysis, working capital management, risk and return, capital budgeting, the capital market, sources of finance, the cost of capital, operating and financial leverage and the financial structure decision.
learning_outcomes: Define and calculate operating, financial and total leverage, and explain the implications for the target capital structure
Understand the relationship between risk and return, diversifiable and non-diversifiable risk, and their impact on asset pricing
Explain the factors influencing the appropriate level of working capital for a firm and how to manage cash and marketable securities, accounts receivable, and payables
Distinguish the financial objective governing a firm's decisions
Value long-term debt, preference shares and ordinary shares, and to determine the cost of capital of the firm
Explain the importance, role and techniques of capital budgeting in a firm
Forecast a firm's future cash flow needs and prepare budgets and pro forma financial statements
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 BUSN9017 - Economics for Business Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: International Business Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the ability to: Identify and analyse the distinctive features of international management roles Examine the internal and external influences on management of international organisations Understand the concepts and tools used in international business management Practise the case study method, leading to better skills in extracting manageable order from the chaos of information that faces international managers every day Appreciate the basics of international negotiation Effectively design and run meetings

This topic assists students to develop a global outlook on business and other management. The focus is on managerial responses to complex cultural, political, economic, competitive and other contextual forces firms encounter when they engage in international business activities. The content includes aspects of organisational design, strategic planning, negotiation, and human resources management for firms involved in international business.
learning_outcomes: Apply basic skills in international negotiation
Lead seminars/meetings with confidence and skill
Recognise internal and external influences on management of international organisations
Work efficiently in study teams
Use the case study method to identify, analyse and suggest solutions to international management problems in specific cases
Apply SWOT analysis and other tools used in international business management
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology 2 BUSN9019 - International Business Context Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Strategic Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to the concepts and tools used in strategic marketing Provide students with an understanding of the importance of marketing strategies in business Develop students' ability to analyse market opportunities in a variety of differing market contexts Develop students' ability to formulate marketing strategies and develop marketing plans

This topic firstly deals with the place a marketing plan has within the overall business plan of an organisation. It then examines the marketing strategies most appropriate under a range of different market and product life-cycle circumstances. Finally, it provides a template for developing a marketing plan that meets the needs of the firm's aims and objectives within the context of a particular product and market.
learning_outcomes: Create a strategic marketing plan that is consistent with the firm's overall objectives
Understand the various marketing strategies appropriate for different product contexts
Appreciate where marketing plans fit within the organisation's overall business plan
Understand the requirements for the effective implementation of marketing plans
Analyse market based data for opportunities relevant to a firm
Obtain the information necessary to produce a viable marketing plan
prerequisites: Admission into MBUST-Master of Business and Technology

title: Coding for Business Professionals
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with applied knowledge of technology in business using coding and computational thinking skills. It assesses various issues in analysing and presenting data to solve business problems.

This topic is designed to prepare students with digital skills that will be useful in their career. The topic provides students with knowledge about digital technology, including the concept of Big Data and the role of machine learning and AI.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the importance of digital skills in business professions
Determine the importance of ethics in analysing data
Utilise technology for coding and computational thinking skills for business
Assess various types of data in business

title: Enabling Diversity and Inclusion
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to appreciate the score of diversity, reflect on and understand the relationships between inclusion, equity, and diversity.

This topic will embrace diversity and inclusion concepts and practices, which are imperative in workplaces and society to foster participation, belonging, and enabling individuals to be valued and thrive. The topic will focus on learnings and practices that highlight how individuals are uniquely diverse in many ways including neurodiversity, geographical diversity, among others. It will prepare students for future workforce to be a leader and effective manager.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate bias, assumptions and practices of self and others
Articulate and argue perspectives on inclusion, its advantages and challenges
Analyse how the appreciation of diverse others influences a sense of belonging, enhances valuing of individuals, business and society
Formulate plans to foster inclusion
Critically evaluate diverse perspectives

title: Coordinating Programs and Portfolios
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Integrate program and portfolio management principles to align initiatives with strategic business objectives. Prioritise projects and programs to balance current operations with future organisational needs. Design governance structures that support effective oversight, control and benefit realisation. Formulate strategies for portfolio selection and program execution in dynamic and evolving market contexts.

In this topic, you will learn to manage multiple related projects through coordinated program management to achieve strategic business and organisational goals. You will explore how portfolio management aligns programs and projects with broader strategic objectives. You will gain the skills and understanding needed to oversee complex project groupings and deliver targeted benefits. Throughout the topic, you will learn to apply appropriate processes for both program and portfolio management, and you will develop the ability to use these frameworks effectively in the right context and situation.
learning_outcomes: Appraise performance data to shape program and portfolio outcomes
Evaluate portfolio needs and organisational constraints to prioritise and select optimal investments
Design governance and risk management frameworks that support effective delivery and stakeholder engagement
Integrate advanced knowledge of portfolio and program management to align initiatives with strategic organisational objectives
prerequisites: ^ BUSN8016 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Artificial Intelligence in Business Practice
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide greater understanding of Artificial Intelligence system and aims to equip students with capabilities to confidently articulate their AI related requirements to their organisational team.

This topic will provide students with a fundamental understanding of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its various forms, including machine learning and generative AI, which will empower them to make smart informed decisions about the deployment of AI and its various forms in organisations. Students will identify the challenges of deploying AI, assess the advantages and limitations of AI, critique ethical issues in AI, and prescribe a strategic framework for deploying AI in organisations.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the challenges, advantages and limitations of AI deployment in organisations
Critically apply problem-solving and decision-making skills to identify innovative solutions to complex business problems using AI technologies
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of AI technologies, and address the ethical issues in deploying AI in organisations
Present professional judgements creating logical, engaging material in a format best suited for an executive audience

title: Leading Complex Projects
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop your ability to lead and manage projects in complex and dynamic environments. Explore strategic approaches to managing large-scale, global and collaborative initiatives. Apply systems thinking and portfolio management frameworks to enhance project outcomes. Enhance your leadership and communication capabilities for effective teamwork in virtual and multicultural project settings.

In this topic, you will learn to lead and manage effectively in complex and challenging project environments. You will explore strategies for managing large collaborative initiatives, including global projects, programs and portfolios. You will develop an understanding of leadership roles in complex settings and learn to implement portfolio management frameworks that support benefit realisation. You will also apply systems thinking to develop creative and adaptive project management approaches. By using collaborative communication tools, you will enhance your ability to navigate dynamic environments and deliver strategic outcomes across complex projects.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate leadership approaches and management strategies applicable to complex and dynamic project environments.
Appraise team dynamics and communication strategies to function effectively as a leader or team member in complex projects
Formulate solutions for managing international, global and virtual projects including the use of collaborative tools
Integrate portfolio, program and project management practices to support benefit realisation in diverse contexts
prerequisites: ^ BUSN8016 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Managing Project Procurement and Contracts
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Evaluate procurement and contract management strategies across all phases of the project lifecycle. Apply ethical, legal, and practical principles to procurement planning, tendering and contract administration. Integrate contemporary procurement approaches such as green procurement, e-procurement and supply chain management. Formulate solutions for effective contract performance, risk mitigation, and dispute resolution in complex project settings.

In this topic, you will learn to apply advanced theoretical and practical knowledge of procurement and contract management across the project lifecycle. You will explore procurement planning, tendering methods, contract strategies and evaluation techniques to support the delivery of project outcomes. You will examine key areas such as procurement ethics, contract law, administration and dispute resolution, while also considering contemporary practices like green procurement, e-procurement and supply chain management. Through this topic, you will develop the skills needed to manage procurement processes and contract obligations effectively in complex project environments.
learning_outcomes: Integrate ethical, legal and practical considerations into procurement planning and contract administration
Formulate appropriate tendering and evaluation approaches to address diverse project requirements
Evaluate procurement and contract strategies to support project delivery across different lifecycle phases
Manage procurement processes and contract obligations within complex and dynamic project environments
prerequisites: ^ BUSN8016 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Developing Project Schedules and Managing Costs
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Evaluate key concepts and constraints that influence effective project time and cost management. Design accurate schedules and cost estimates using appropriate tools and techniques. Critique scheduling and budgeting practices to support efficient project delivery and strategic decision-making. Integrate scheduling and cost control processes to optimise resource use and maintain quality across project lifecycles.

In this topic, you will learn to create value through effective scheduling and cost management in predictive and hybrid projects. You will explore how to balance the triple constraints of scope, time and cost while planning, executing and controlling projects. You will use industry-standard scheduling tools and develop the discipline and flexibility needed for practical scheduling. You will also learn to prepare accurate cost estimates, manage resources efficiently and apply techniques to minimise cost without compromising quality. Additionally, you will critique planning, budgeting, cost control, profitability analysis and value management to support strategic decision-making.
learning_outcomes: Critique project scheduling and budgeting approaches to support strategic decision-making and continuous improvement
Assess key concepts related to project time and cost to understand their impact on project performance
Integrate scheduling and cost management practices to optimise resource use and maintain project quality
Design project schedules and cost estimates using appropriate tools and techniques to support planning and control
prerequisites: ^ BUSN8016 ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Project Management Research Project
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Integrate academic knowledge with real-world project management practices. Evaluate project challenges and opportunities within diverse organisational and sectoral contexts. Construct practical solutions and project deliverables based on needs and unstructured information. Critique professional practices related to industrial relations, health and safety, and sustainability in project environments.

In this topic, you will undertake a research project in respect to a topic of your choice as aligned to project management. This topic will broaden your appreciation of the dynamic nature of project management and prepare you to navigate the unique challenges and opportunities present in various project environments, supporting your transition into professional practice. The content covered includes reviewing published literature, building on research methodology knowledge, addressing the topic via qualitative or quantitative secondary research data and drawing conclusions in respect to research outcomes. You will need to apply the skills required to develop a research proposal, presentation and final report based on extending current knowledge.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate project performance, stakeholder engagement and contextual challenges
Integrate theoretical project management knowledge with practical industry applications
Construct project deliverables and solutions in response to needs and project briefs
Synthesise key findings and communicate them in a manner suitable to a range of stakeholders
prerequisites: 3 of BUSN8016, BUSN8017, BUSN8018

title: Exploring Accounting Principles
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce the technical aspects of recording and reporting accounting information for the relatively less complex sole proprietorship form of business organisation. It also aims to provide students with an understanding of the importance of financial information in business practice. The topic includes introductory financial accounting, introductory management accounting, preparation of the three financial statements, and elementary financial statement interpretation and analysis.

This topic deals with the technical aspects of recording and reporting accounting information for sole trader business entities, focusing on the importance of financial information in business practice. The topic includes introductory financial accounting, introductory management accounting, preparation of financial statements, and elementary financial statement interpretation and analysis.
learning_outcomes: Explain the accounting equation and analyse the effects of business transactions on the accounting equation
Apply technical financial accounting skills to produce financial statements
Conduct a basic financial statement analysis and critically evaluate the results
Explain accrual accounting and prepare adjusting entries and reversing entries
Complete the accounting cycle, including recording business transactions in journals and ledgers and reporting financial performance and financial position for sole traders and retailers
Discuss and appraise the professional accounting body ethical standards and apply them to professional and business scenarios
Describe the accounting controls in relation to cash and prepare a bank reconciliation statement
Account for and manage inventories, accounts receivable and bad debts

title: Transforming Accounting Processes
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to accounting information systems, business computing and computerised accounting packages. It also builds on and extends the accounting foundations studied in Accounting Fundamentals. In the second half, it aims to introduce students to accounting for more complex transactions and forms of business organisations such as companies. It includes accounting for liabilities, cash flows and fixed assets. In addition, the Australian conceptual framework will be examined. This will include an overview of the reporting entity concept, objectives of financial reporting and the definitions and recognition criteria of the elements of financial statements.

The topic provides students with an introduction to accounting information systems and business computing systems. In the second half, the topic then builds on, and extends, the accounting foundations studied in BUSN9113 Exploring Accounting Principles. This topic also introduces students to accounting for more complex transactions involving liabilities, cash flows and fixed assets.
learning_outcomes: Comprehend, identify and evaluate computerised business packages such as spreadsheets and databases
Critically evaluate the information needs and flows of business organisations
Prepare accounting journal entries for liabilities including accounts payable and bills payable
Analyse and comprehend the theoretical framework upon which Australian Accounting Standards are developed
Comprehend and account for the acquisition, depreciation, re-valuation and disposal of non-current assets
Prepare financial statements using both manual and computerised accounting procedures
Prepare and comprehend the reasons for using a statement of cash flows
Account for the formation, operation, reporting and dissolution of partnerships

title: Analysing Business Data
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to define measurable data and information. Theory will be illustrated with worked examples, and mathematical and statistical techniques will be applied to real world problems with a business focus. Computing workshops are an important component of the topic. In the workshops the spreadsheet program Microsoft Excel will be used to solve problems in financial mathematics and carry out statistical analyses.

The topic provides an introduction to basic mathematical and statistical techniques useful in accounting, management, finance and economics. Subjects covered include a basic algebra review, simple functions and their graphical representation, mathematical finance, data presentation, descriptive statistics, sample design, elementary probability, the normal distribution, sampling distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, simple regression analysis and analysis of covariance.
learning_outcomes: Use their initiative and creativity to apply their knowledge and technical skills of quantitative methods to solve 'real world' problems
Use Excel spread sheets to perform statistical and financial mathematics procedures and to present results in formats appropriate for business professionals
Describe and apply quantitative analytical techniques in financial mathematics and statistics
Describe and interpret measures of central tendency and dispersion
Present quantitative data in summarised and graphical formats suitable for management
Carry out hypothesis testing procedures and interpret the results
Undertake sample surveys and critically interpret survey results
Explain tests of goodness of fit and differences in population bases, on nominal data
Perform and interpret regression analysis and Chi-square tests

title: Measuring Operational and Financial Performance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to a variety of costing systems, models and techniques relevant to managerial planning, control and decision making in the services, merchandising and manufacturing industries. The topic also aims to make students aware and develop the students' ability to critically evaluate management accounting issues in areas such as professional ethics, budgeting and cost/volume/profit analysis, quality and customer management

This topic distinguishes between financial accounting and management accounting systems. Management accounting is concerned with supplying organisational management with relevant, timely and accurate information to promote the efficient and effective use of resources, thereby enhancing customer and shareholder value. A variety of costing systems, techniques and models relevant to the service, merchandising and manufacturing sectors are examined, with an emphasis on the need for management accounting systems to adapt to a constantly changing business environment. As such, contemporary developments in areas such as cost, quality, customer and social and environmental management are considered
learning_outcomes: Discuss the nature and importance of management accounting, and the current roles and responsibilities of management accountants
Apply various costing systems and techniques to calculate and report the costs of various cost objects, including products, services and departments, in various organisational settings
Discuss and critically analyse some of the contemporary issues confronting organisations and the management accounting discipline
Categorise and identify the nature of the various types of costs, cost objects and cost behaviours
Apply various techniques to analyse cost and other management-related information for effective planning, control and decision-making
prerequisites: 1 BUSN9113 2 Admission into MAF-Master of Accounting and Finance 2a Admission into MAM-Master of Accounting and Marketing 2b Admission into MACC-Master of Accounting 2c Admission into MAFFP-Master of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus 2d Admission into MAMFP-Master of Accounting and Marketing - Flinders City Campus 2e Admission into MACCFP-Master of Accounting - Flinders City Campus 2f Admission into CACSI-Master of Accounting/Graduate Certificate in Social Impact - Flinders City Campus Must Satisfy: (1 and (2 or 2a or 2b or 2c or 2d or 2e or 2f))

title: Appraising Economic Environments
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to outline economic principles that guide the decision-making processes of consumers, businesses and organisations. Students will examine purchasing, pricing, production and investment decisions, drivers of the economy, and competitive market environments.

This topic introduces the economic principles that can usefully guide the decision-making processes of consumers, businesses and other organisations including purchasing, pricing, production and investment decisions. It considers these decision processes in different competitive market environments. The topic also introduces the workings of the overall economy. It focuses on national output and expenditure, inflation, unemployment and international economic relationships including trade and capital flows and the role of fiscal and monetary policies.
learning_outcomes: Identify the role of comparative advantage and the gains from trade, the role of prices in a market system. Evaluate how market structure affects prices and output
Identify the impact of globalisation on the domestic economy. Examine the relationship between the changing structure of the domestic Macroeconomy and international trade policy
Identify the basic economic issue of scarcity, choice and opportunity cost, how markets allocate resources and outputs, and the role of marginal analysis in decision making

Identify information problems in economics and acquire the ability to clearly illustrate the analysis of information problems through the application of economic principles such as rationality and efficiency

Clearly illustrate the specific roles and functions of Monetary and Fiscal policy in the economy and explain how these are applied to the process of stabilising the economy, specifically with regard to controlling inflation, promoting full employment and facilitating economic growth
Identify strategic considerations when making choices. Predict how other people or organizations behave when they are in strategic settings
Evaluate the role government plays in a market economy. Identify how economic principles affect individuals' lives
Identify the process of how the nation's output of goods and services is measured. Analyse the income and expenditure approaches to measuring national output and national income
Analyse economic behaviour of consumers and firms, and explore how they respond to changes in the opportunities and constraints that they face and how they interact in markets

title: Resolving Accounting Issues
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to financial accounting issues, and develop their ability to appraise these issues based upon the conceptual framework for financial reporting as well as the application of relevant accounting theory Provide students with a detailed knowledge of the impact of specific regulatory requirements, including the conceptual framework and applicable accounting standards, upon reporting entities' accounting procedures Provide students with an understanding of specific accounting standards, illustrate the accounting procedures required, give a theoretical understanding of the principles involved, and outline the relevant disclosure requirements Develop students' ability to critically evaluate these accounting and reporting requirements Develop generic cognitive skills (especially analytical and evaluative skills) Develop behavioural skills (especially personal and interpersonal skills) which can be employed in an organisational work environment

This topic examines selected issues in financial accounting and reporting. Current and proposed accounting standards and generally accepted accounting principles are considered and evaluated within the conceptual framework for financial reporting and application of accounting theory. The topic also examines the Financial Reporting Environment, Regulation and Current Developments in International Accounting Standard Setting. Topics to be examined may include: applicable accounting theory, share capital and reserves; accounting for leases; foreign currency translation; intangibles; and financial instruments.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to accounting for foreign exchange and the translation of the accounts of foreign operations
Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to financial instruments

Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to the financial reporting environment, conceptual framework, regulation and current developments in international accounting standard setting
Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to accounting for intangibles
Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to accounting for leases
Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to accounting for share capital and reserves
Critically evaluate and apply accounting standards relating to other current issues in accounting

title: Managing Company Finances
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: • Equip students with essential tools and analytical concepts for effective financial management. • Define the role and objectives of financial planning and management in business organisations.

This topic equips students with the critical tools and analytical concepts necessary for excelling in financial management. By focusing on three pivotal financial decisions - capital budgeting, capital structure, and working capital management - it provides a comprehensive understanding of the role and objectives of financial management.
learning_outcomes: Select working capital and dividend policies efficiently
Determine capital budgeting techniques for informed investment decisions
Evaluate an organisation’s performance by analysing financial statements
Assess investment risks and determine the value of financial instruments, including bonds, preference shares, and ordinary shares
Weigh up leverage implications for effective capital structure decisions

title: Building Confidence with Audit and Assurance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the nature and function of audit and assurance engagements in Australia, including: Statutory responsibilities, ethical implications and the legal consequences of an assurance engagement Auditing principles and standards in the context of risk management Practical auditing methods and techniques in evidence gathering and evaluation, including the audit of computerised systems and the use of computer-assisted audit techniques (CAATs) Reporting and communication of audit findings to relevant stakeholders Develop general cognitive skills (especially analytical and evaluative skills Develop behavioural skills (especially personal and interpersonal skills) which can be employed in an organisational work environment

This topic provides an introduction to the nature and purpose of auditing and assurance, and the regulatory environment in which it operates. The topic has an emphasis on essential auditing standards and their application to the audit process, as well as principles and professional practices. Practical issues of audit methodology including risk assessment, analytic review procedures, internal control assessment, substantive testing procedures, statistical sampling, fraud assessment and applied project management principles are covered. Contemporary issues such as the expectation gap as well as professional, ethical and legal responsibilities of auditors are considered. The audit implications of information technology and electronic commerce are examined. Other assurance functions (e.g. forensic accounting, environmental auditing, performance auditing) are dealt with through elective study.
learning_outcomes: Determine the appropriateness of different types of audit opinions and explain the key features of an audit report
Identify and explain the nature and purpose of auditing and assurance services
Describe audit evidence gathering techniques, including sampling and substantive testing, and the use of computer-assisted audit techniques
Explain the regulatory and professional requirements of auditors, and apply relevant rules, standards and pronouncements to a financial statement audit
Demonstrate an understanding of audit planning and risk assessment in an IT environment

title: Accounting for Companies
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:

This topic provides students with a detailed knowledge of the impact of specific regulatory requirements and generally accepted accounting principles upon corporate accounting procedures. It will enhance students' existing knowledge of the factors regulating corporate accounting in Australia, and develop their ability to critically evaluate these accounting and reporting requirements. The topic traces the life-cycle of the company with emphasis upon the accounting procedure and problems involved.
learning_outcomes: Understand the need for and be able to prepare consolidated financial statements for economic entities comprising more than one legal entity
Apply the principles of the balance sheet approach to tax-effect accounting, and evaluate its desirability
Account for business combinations
Explain the process of liquidation of companies and be able to account for the winding up of a company

title: Placement
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge, skills and experience through an applied project in the workplace.

Students undertake an industry project in Australia. The Project is termed as the Space Entrepreneurship Program (SEP). Through the SEP students will be working in multidisciplinary teams (4-5 students) to solve some of the most exciting challenges of the Australian Space industry. The SEP is offered as a Work Integrated Learning (WIL) topic where students will work with the Space Industry Sponsor supported by the Topic Coordinator and industry mentors.
learning_outcomes: Develop and apply the following workforce skills: complex problem-solving; critical thinking; creativity; collaboration and teamwork; judgement and decision-making; cognitive flexibility; negotiation; building professional networks; and prototyping
Operate effectively in a workplace
Develop and apply the following research skills: market research (including qualitative interviews); qualitative data analysis; "White Paper" drafting; and implement a market research plan
Develop a strong understanding of the context and tools of Industry 4.0
Demonstrate an understanding of and the ability to apply the Design Thinking Framework, Customer Discovery and Validation, and the Business Model canvas

title: Understanding Taxation Law
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to taxation law and policy principles, covering a broad range of Commonwealth taxation law Provide students with an understanding of the principles of taxation law Equip students with skills to keep up to date with ongoing reforms Develop generic cognitive skills (especially analytical and evaluative skills), and behavioural skills (personal and interpersonal skills) which can be employed in an organisational work environment

This topic examines Australian taxation law and has a specific focus on the following: tax and policy, goods and services tax, income tax law, residence and source, ordinary income, statutory income, capital gains tax, general deductions, specific deductions, entities - basics, anti-avoidance, tax planning, fringe benefits tax, and tax technical research.
learning_outcomes: Develop oral communications skills and exercise professional judgement in addressing practical tax issues
Identify and apply legal research principles to solve complex tax issues
Write a tax law research paper exercising professional judgement for audiences such as tax administrators, accounting and legal practitioners as well as non-specialists
Identify, analyse and synthesise the sources of tax law and apply them to practical situations and transmit that knowledge

title: Upholding Business Law and Regulations

syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce, and familiarise, students with the areas of law that are relevant to business Develop students' appreciation of the Australian system of commercial law that has been developed and enforced by the Parliaments and the Courts Enable students to recognise legal problems in business and implications when they arise in commercial and business practice and settings; and Provide students with the knowledge and tools to be able to seek legal advice or to make appropriate referrals to legal professionals, when and where required

title: Industry Placement

This topic aims to provide a practical orientation to the workplace in preparation for a business career. This orientation takes the form of a placement experience in a business setting.

Students undertake an industry placement. Students are placed and matched with placements according to availability and suitability with the aim of increasing employability skills. Students are prepared for their placement, enter into a learning contract to guide the work integrated learning experience and are supervised.
learning_outcomes: Reflect upon your learning from University and apply disciplined based knowledge and skills to a professional workplace
Develop personal goals to enable you to enhance your personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practice in a business setting

Communicate effectively and appropriately with peers, industry professionals and supervisors; convey information clearly and fluently in high quality verbal and written forms appropriate for a professional audience
Demonstrate effective, professional and ethical engagement in a diverse, workplace setting

title: Placement
