Students undertake an industry project in Australia. The Project is termed as the Green Economy Entrepreneurship Program (GEEP). Through the GEEP students will be working in multidisciplinary teams (4-5 students) to solve some of the most exciting challenges of the green economy industry. The GEEP is offered as a Work Integrated Learning (WIL) topic where students will work with the Green Economy Problem Sponsor supported by the Topic Coordinator and industry mentors.
learning_outcomes: Develop and apply the following workforce skills: complex problem-solving; critical thinking; creativity; collaboration and teamwork; judgement and decision-making; cognitive flexibility; negotiation; building professional networks; and prototyping
Operate effectively in a workplace
Demonstrate an understanding of and the ability to apply the Design Thinking Framework, Customer Discovery and Validation, and the Business Model canvas
Develop a strong understanding of the context and tools of Industry 4.0
Develop and apply the following research skills: market research (including qualitative interviews); qualitative data analysis; "White Paper" drafting; and implement a market research plan

title: Advanced Industry Practicum
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to enable students to gain practical skills through engagement with industry partners.

The topic will be in partnership with Flinders Factory of Future. In this topic students will be given the opportunity to be working in multidisciplinary teams working on the projects at the Flinders Factory of the Future. The students will be supported by academics throughout the journey as well as project engineers/managers from Flinders Factory of the Future.
learning_outcomes: Operate effectively in a workplace
Develop and apply the following research skills: market research (including qualitative interviews); qualitative data analysis; "White Paper" drafting; and implement a market research plan

Demonstrate an understanding of and the ability to apply a range of Design Thinking Frameworks in Business.
Develop a strong understanding of the context and tools of Industry 4.0 and 5.0

title: Derivatives and Risk Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to deepen students’ understanding of financial risk and the strategic role of derivative instruments in managing it. Students will develop analytical and practical skills to assess risk exposures, evaluate and design hedging strategies, and apply derivative-based solutions effectively in complex and dynamic financial environments.

This topic introduces tools and concepts for understanding financial risk and managing it with derivatives. Students explore the structure, valuation, and application of forwards, futures, options, and swaps, focusing on hedging strategies and informed decision-making through quantitative analysis and case studies.
learning_outcomes: Assess the integration of derivatives and quantitative tools within comprehensive risk management frameworks
Critically evaluate the role of derivative instruments in managing financial risk across diverse contexts
Apply pricing models to determine the fair value of derivatives under varying market conditions
Justify derivative-based strategies for hedging and identifying arbitrage opportunities
prerequisites: 1 BUSN9119 2 Admission into MAF-Master of Accounting and Finance 2a Admission into MACC-Master of Accounting 2b Admission into MAFFP-Master of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus Must Satisfy: (1 and (2 or 2a or 2b))

title: Applied Security Analysis and Valuation
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with the knowledge, understanding and skills required to conduct in-depth valuation of financial securities. The content covered in this topic is essential for any student seeking a career in funds management or corporate finance. This topic will examine a variety of cornerstone valuation models and analytical techniques that can be used to derive the intrinsic value of publicly traded corporations. Students will learn to apply their knowledge in a practical setting and develop an awareness of the advantages and limitations of different equity valuation models and analytical techniques.

This topic is concerned with the valuation of securities using fundamental and quantitative techniques. Subjects covered include economic and industry analysis, growth and discount rate estimation, discounted cash flow analysis and relative valuation modelling.
learning_outcomes: Estimate a company's value using free cash flow analysis, relative valuation and asset pricing models
Evaluate whether a financial security is mispriced
Identify inputs required for valuation and analysis
Work collaboratively and communicate findings via verbal presentations and written assessment items
Explain and justify the use of different valuation models
Discuss model limitations and the purpose of sensitivity analysis in asset valuation
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MAF-Master of Accounting and Finance 1a Admission into MBAF-Master of Business Administration (Finance) 1b Admission into MAFFP-Master of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus 1c Admission into MBAFFP-Master of Business Administration (Finance) - Flinders City Campus Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c))

title: New Venture Finance and Private Equity
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic focuses on the financing and valuation of early-stage and entrepreneurial start-up firms from both entrepreneur and investor perspectives. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of funding sources, transaction arrangements, and valuation techniques through case studies and worked examples. The topic examines the mechanisms and processes used to balance responsibilities and rights between management and providers of capital. Students will have the opportunity to engage with industry practitioners and entrepreneurs to integrate their academic learning with real-world application.

This topic is concerned with the financing and valuation of early stage and entrepreneurial start-up firms. Students will develop the insights necessary to formulate business-ready solutions to funding constraints that new venture firms often encounter.
learning_outcomes: Assess exit strategies and restructuring options for ventures at different lifecycle stages, including financially distressed situation
Analyse start-up performance using various methods to evaluate venture potential and risk
Apply valuation methods to determine the cost of capital and enterprise value for investment and financing decision-making
Critique the role of financing throughout the entrepreneurial process to inform investment and funding decisions
Evaluate different sources of financing for start-ups to recommend appropriate funding strategies
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MAF-Master of Accounting and Finance 1a Admission into MBAF-Master of Business Administration (Finance) 1b Admission into MBUSFN-Master of Business (Finance) 1c Admission into MACC-Master of Accounting 1d Admission into GDPBUSA-Graduate Diploma in Business Administration 1e Admission into MAFFP-Master of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus 1f Admission into MBAFFP-Master of Business Administration (Finance) - Flinders City Campus 1g Admission into MACCFP-Master of Accounting - Flinders City Campus 1h Admission into GDPBUSAFP-Graduate Diploma in Business Administration - Flinders City Campus 1i Admission into GDPEG-Graduate Diploma in Entrepreneurial Growth 1j Admission into MTF- Master of Technology in Finance Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g or 1h or 1i or 1j))

title: Enterprise and Innovation Project
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge and skills through an applied business project; to help students take an idea and find a viable business model which is scalable and repeatable, from scratch.

Students undertake an enterprise or innovation project. Students will be guided by experienced individuals who have either built successful companies or fund them. This opportunity is available to students when appropriate projects are identified and where student knowledge and ability matches the needs of the project.
learning_outcomes: Use the skills necessary to develop a business model
Write a professional business report
Conduct research on a business issue in depth and develop plans
Develop more effective skills working in a team and manage team dynamics in a professional manner
Apply business knowledge to applied business settings
Make effective presentations to financiers or Boards to secure resources and/or support for projects
Assess new business propositions

title: Economic Environments: Assessing Current and Future Markets
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to introduce students to current economic environment in which business and society functions and aims to enhance application of foundational micro and macro economic concepts in decision making.

This topic introduces the economic principles that can usefully guide the decision-making processes of consumers, businesses and other organisations including purchasing, pricing, production and investment decisions. lt considers assessing current micro and macro environments and future markets to improve decision processes in different competitive market environments. The topic also introduces the workings of the overall economy. lt focuses on national output and expenditure, inflation, unemployment and international economic relationships including trade and capital flows and the role of fiscal and monetary policies.
learning_outcomes: Assess information problems in economics through the lens of rationality and efficiency
Critique strategic choices and predict the reaction of other people and organisations
Critically evaluate the measurement of the nation’s output and goods, utilising the income and expenditure approaches
Evaluate the economic behaviour of consumers and firms when faced with opportunities and constraints

title: Leading a Future Workforce
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide in-depth knowledge and skills on various traditional and contemporary theories of leadership. Students learn how to utilise various theoretical frameworks to lead a highly digitised workforce. Students will familiarise themselves with various new technologies that have digitised the modern day workforce, and analyse various ethical leadership challenges associated with it. Students will learn how to lead the multigenerational workforce and provide an effective leadership to balance human and machine collaboration.

This topic aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills on leading the future workforce. The arrival of artificial intelligence and highly digitised workforce presents unique and diverse motivational and ethical challenges for the leadership and management today. Leaders need new paradigms and frameworks to make a positive impact on the evolving future workforce. Therefore, students learn both traditional and contemporary leadership theories and practices to apply relevant theoretical frameworks and best industry practices to manage and lead the future workforce.
learning_outcomes: Critically argue the application of traditional and contemporary leadership theories and frameworks in leading a future workforce
Determine appropriate ways leaders can create a culture of innovation
Evaluate crisis leadership principles and interventions in times of uncertainty
Evaluate leaders’ ethical challenges involved in human and machine collaboration
Critically assess the impact of new technologies in leading a future workforce

title: Marketing in a Digital Age
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic is structured such that the basic concepts and principles of marketing management are introduced, providing students a foundation/framework within which to work. Students will be required to apply these concepts in their assignment. Students will compare the theories they learn in the class with marketing practices in the real world situations. To improve student team skills, group assessment has been included.

This topic aims to provide students with an introduction to the concepts and tools used in marketing management. Concepts such as: market segmentation, consumer behaviour, marketing mix (product, place, price and promotion), branding and marketing are discussed in the context of new technology and digital environment. The topic concludes by discussing issues such as internet marketing, marketing strategy and planning.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate marketing mix and factors influencing marketing decisions
Argue the relationship between theory and practice in contemporary and future issues in marketing
Critique key marketing concepts as applied within the business context
Argue the importance and application of marketing concepts

title: Business Analytics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to develop students’ analytical and problem-solving skills. The topic will introduce students to contemporary analytic tools and students will learn to handle big data and undertake descriptive and predictive analysis.

This topic aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills required to strategically align performance management and rewards practises with organisational priorities. Students will be equipped with skills and knowledge to differentiate between different approaches and then to select those that best meet with organisational needs - covering large organisations to SMEs. The topic will require a critical analysis of the performance management and rewards strategies used in an organisation and to design an intervention that improves outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Integrate the knowledge and skills acquired to conduct business research
Determine data analytic techniques to solve complex business problems
Critically evaluate the best strategy to acquire evidence relevant to the business problem
Effectively communicate the findings of the data analysis using visualization techniques

title: Researching Markets
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide you with a range of research methods and theories upon which you will conduct project based research on your chosen area of specialisation. You will be required to communicate your findings, both orally and in writing, in a manner appropriate for a selection of audiences. You will be encouraged to think creatively, to integrate and apply knowledge and skills acquired throughout your studies, to identify and solve real business problems or address existing issues present in organisations.

This topic develops research knowledge and skills that are appropriate for business-related research that identifies and solves real business problems or addresses existing issues present in organisations. Students will be required to conduct research in their chosen field of specialisation and communicate the results to a variety of audiences.
learning_outcomes: Synthesize a body of literature relevant to new business markets including opportunities
Assess local and global business markets to identify a new business market
Apply an appropriate research methodology to solve a contemporary business issue relevant to Industry 4.0 or Industry 5.0 for a specific organizational case study
Critically analyse data and evidence used to inform business decisions at the leadership level

title: Trends in Business Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Identify the concepts and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of financial management Define the role and objectives of sound financial planning and management in business organisations

This is an introductory topic on business finance. It will introduce students to the recent practices and tools of financial analysis related to existing businesses and new entrepreneurs. This topic will discuss the principles of finance, time value of money and the risk-return trade-off between financing and investment alternatives. The concept of time value of money will later be applied to the valuations of shares and bonds, capital budgeting and estimating the cost of capital for businesses.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate financial statements to formulate future financial strategies of a firm
Critique the concept of time value of money and its usage in the valuation of debt and equity and estimating cost of capital of a firm
Argue the trade-offs of raising finances for businesses through alternative channels and their impact on the capital structure of a firm
Appraise techniques of capital budgeting and appropriate methods for capital investment decisions
Assess the financial implications of business formation and planning process

title: Legal Signposts for Decision Makers
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with key insight into the: Different sources of law and different types of legal strategies and their relevance to operating within domestic and international markets Legal regulatory environment in which domestic and international entities operate and how legal disputes may be resolved

A broad introduction to the various legal aspects of the business life cycle - ranging from major relevant points of legislation to contract law. This topic reflects the questions, concerns and perspectives that people in all aspects of business life (including not for profit organisations) have highlighted as important. There is a need to understand what aspects of the law will impact on your business and how to use legal protections to grow your business. The topic identifies the intersection between the legal interests of business people, consumers and regulators. It will enable you to understand when and where legal responsibilities and risks arise.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate different approaches available to the resolution of legal disputes
Critically evaluate the key legal issues that may arise in the business life cycle and their different types
Determine appropriate legal principles pertaining to the conduct of sustainable, socially responsible governance and business practice
Assess the relevant legal issues faced by business professionals and the legal imperatives impacting on the business sector relevant to Industry 4.0 and 5.0

title: Emerging Business Models: Disruptions, Collaboration and Competition
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to equip students with an understanding of the key strategic management theoretical concepts, frameworks, and planning techniques in order for them to employ them in a broad range of business situations and use them to find solutions to business problems. The topic also includes exploration of new and emerging business models disrupting the status quo in many business sectors nationally and internationally and providing inspiration for entrepreneurial undertakings.

This topic provides a broad overview of the strategic planning process and provides students with the skill to develop and understand the implications of the implementation and control aspects. The topic also uses case study examples to illustrate the modern world of emerging business models and provide them with the ability to extend their thinking beyond traditional business frameworks and structures. Ultimately the students will complete a strategic plan of their own for assessment and reflection.
learning_outcomes: Critically appraise the external and internal industry environments employing digital technologies and methods
Critically assess the business models that are applied in various business contexts
Propose relevant responses to the potential impacts of a changing business environments to Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0 in various business contexts
Design business, corporate, and global strategies relevant to the development of a business strategic plan in view of the future of work

title: Working in Australia
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide in-depth knowledge and skills on various components of Australian workplace culture and employee expectations. Students make cross cultural comparisons of national cultures and understand the uniqueness of Australian culture. Australian cultural dimensions will be key to understanding the implications of those national dimensions in Australian workplaces, work etiquettes and employee expectations.

This topic aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills on working in Australia. Students learn about cultural characteristics of Australian workplace, national cultural dimensions and their implications in Australian workplaces, work etiquettes, networking skills within the industry and employee characteristics and expectations.
learning_outcomes: Debate the various challenges faced while entering the Australian business workforce during times of discontinuity, Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0
Critically analyze the way in which Australian and various global cultures impact on an organization's workplace processes and outcomes
Critically assess the dominant work etiquettes, including employee expectations, in Australian organizations
Appraise the way in which Australia's national culture impacts on an Australian business's organizational culture
Evaluate the skills required to forge a successful career within various Australian industry contexts

title: Digital Marketing and Analytics
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to develop students’ analytical and problem-solving skills. The topic will introduce students to contemporary analytic tools and students will learn to handle big data and undertake descriptive and predictive analysis.

This topic will equip students with leading-edge digital marketing techniques. It will provide students will necessary descriptive, predictive and analytical skills and knowledge. They will learn the importance of consumer data management and how to utilize data to solve real world marketing problems.
learning_outcomes: Appraise concepts relevant to data management and reporting
Critically evaluate the importance of analytics in product and consumer decision-making
Assess marketing data to assist in problem-solving and decision-making
Apply analytics tools for web and social network analysis

title: Investments and Portfolio Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic is designed to help students to understand both the theory and practice of investment selection and management. Students will be introduced to the modern portfolio approach to investments, the valuation and analysis of individual securities, and the selection, management and performance evaluation of a portfolio of securities. The topic concepts will be applied to the Australian investment environment with frequent discussion of Australian institutions, instruments, markets and ethical professional standards. Recent developments in the field i.e. alternative investments, FinTech and ESG will be accounted for in the topic. Students will be encouraged to apply the theory and concepts studied to current market developments. The case study and the portfolio management simulation will require students to analyse and value securities and track portfolio performance.

This is an introductory topic on modern portfolio theory and investment analysis and management. It analyses the concepts of risk and return, the securities markets, securities analysis and portfolio management. The topic looks at the operations of Australian financial markets and the investment opportunities available to investors. It has a broader focus on equity and fixed income securities, along with a range of alternative investments and recent developments in portfolio management. A portfolio investment simulation game running through the semester will comprise part of the assessment.
learning_outcomes: Argue and justify the rationale behind investing in different alternative investment vehicles
Determine the appropriate trade-off between risk and return for investment vehicles
Evaluate the impact of recent developments in portfolio management and ethical standards in practice
Evaluate economic, firm and individual investor related information to assess different types of securities
Appraise modern portfolio theory and critically evaluate different asset pricing models and asset allocation strategies
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MAF-Master of Accounting and Finance 1a Admission into MACC-Master of Accounting 1b Admission into MAFFP-Master of Accounting and Finance - Flinders City Campus 1c Admission into MACCFP-Master of Accounting - Flinders City Campus Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c))

title: Investments and Portfolio Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to help students to understand both the theory and practice of investment management. Students will be introduced to the institutional background to investments, the valuation and analysis of individual securities, and the selection, management and performance evaluation of a portfolio of securities. The topic will be applied to the Australian investment environment with frequent discussion of Australian institutions, instruments and markets. The impact of international market developments will also be highlighted and the role of international investments in a portfolio will be discussed. Students will be encouraged to apply the theory and concepts studied to current market developments.

An introductory course on modern portfolio theory and investment analysis and management. It analyses the concepts of risk and return, the securities markets, securities analysis and portfolio management. The topic looks at the operations of Australian financial markets and the opportunities available to investors. A major focus in the topic is share markets, although parts of the topic are devoted to bond and property investments. A simulated investment game running through the semester will comprise part of the assessment.
learning_outcomes: Perform security selection
Define steps in investing
Discuss the relative role of Australian markets in global financial markets
Discuss portfolio management strategies
Locate and utilise information available to participants in financial markets
Utilise asset pricing models and be aware of their limitations
Explain modern portfolio theory and the benefits of diversification of assets held in a securities portfolio
Evaluate portfolio performance
Assess ethical issues arising from participation in the securities industry
Discuss the structure of securities markets
Construct an optimal risky portfolio
Discuss the features of fixed- income securities and the principles of managing bond portfolios
Assess capital and asset allocation strategies
Apply the important relationship between risk and return
Explain and apply the concept of market efficiency

title: Small Business: International Perspectives
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to give students: An appreciation and understanding of entrepreneurship, small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and the individuals in these business units A practical perspective on issues associated with managing and operating a business

This topic is concerned with the nature of entrepreneurship and small and medium enterprises (SMEs). It examines the economic and social contribution of SMEs, the roles of creativity and innovation, and planning and management issues in business development and growth. Other topics covered include home-based businesses, family businesses, gender issues in SMEs and the financing of SMEs. The topic draws on a range of international experience, with a particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region. It also explores the expansion of SME activities into international markets.
learning_outcomes: Discuss business innovation and competitiveness
Discuss the nature and characteristics of entrepreneurs and entrepreneurship
Discuss the nature and economic significance of SMEs
Discuss expansion of SMEs into export markets
Discuss aspects of business planning
Discuss financing and growth issues in SMEs

title: Accounting for Managers
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide an insight and understanding of the accounting process, specifically to increase understanding of what managers must do to make an organisation financially successful. Emphasis will be placed on how to assess an organisation's current cash flow and profitable position together with how to deal with internal and external environmental complexities and constraints. In attempting to cover these issues formulation, implementation, and control of an organisation's accounting, internal controls, and financial statements need to be understood and performance ratios required to be interpreted. In addition, the topic aims to develop: Generic cognitive skills (especially analytical and evaluative skills) Behavioural skills (especially personal and interpersonal skills) which can be employed in an organisational work environment

The topic introduces students to the way in which a manager utilises accounting, finance, and information systems in decision making. The topic provides students with a solid grounding in accounting fundamentals including statements of comprehensive income, balance sheets, changes in equity and cash flows. Emphasis will be placed on how to assess an organisation's current cash flow and profitable position together with how to deal with internal and external environmental complexities and constraints. Students will be involved in the formulation, implementation, and control of an organisation's accounting, internal controls, and financial statements, and will produce and interpret performance ratios. The topic consists of four main parts: The accounting environment and accounting reports - their nature and use The recording and external reporting focus Accounting and financial management Accounting for management decisions
learning_outcomes: Explain the nature and scope of capital investment decisions and explain some of the practical issues in making investment decisions, and apply the following concepts: payback period; accounting rate of return; Net Present Value
Prepare an accounting worksheet and a simplified Income Statement and Balance Sheet
Use ratio analysis to identify the key aspects of financial performance and financial position, identify limitations of ratios analysis and evaluate alternative techniques
Describe the basic concepts and principles of accounting and the nature and purpose of accounting reports as applied to different business entities
Critically evaluate the usefulness of break-even analysis and apply the concept to a make or buy decision and a decision to close or continue a sbusiness unit
Explain the importance of cash flow and distinguish between accrual and cash-based transaction recognition
Explain the importance of a detailed understanding of cost behaviour, distinguishing between fixed and variable costs to determine a break-even point
Identify and explain the management of net working capital and related issues including the sources of both short term and long term finance and equity financing instruments
Discuss the components of the Cash Flow Statement and its significance in strategic decision making

title: Financial Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Identify the major concepts and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of financial management Examine the role and objectives of sound financial planning and management in business organisations

This topic introduces students to the major concepts and analytical tools used in the theory and practice of financial management. The topic will cover the role and objectives of financial management, business financial planning and ratio analysis, working capital management, risk and return, capital budgeting, the capital market, sources of finance, the cost of capital, operating and financial leverage, the financial structure decision and the dividend decision.
learning_outcomes: Value long-term debt (bonds/debentures), preference shares and ordinary shares
Discuss the importance of managing working capital
Work collaboratively to conduct research and present the findings in report format
Describe the procedures for assessing and measuring the risk of investment assets
Apply capital budgeting techniques in capital investment decisions
Perform financial statement analysis
Determine the cost of capital of a firm
Define and calculate operating, financial and total leverage, and understand their implications for the target capital structure of a firm

title: Strategic Marketing
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with: The fundamentals of strategic marketing Strategic aspects of marketing and where the marketing strategy fits within the overall business strategy of an organisation An appreciation of the effects of the product life cycle on marketing plans, and the marketing mix, which includes product, price, promotion and distribution The marketing knowledge and skills necessary to develop appropriate marketing strategies and marketing plans for businesses

This topic introduces students to the concepts and tools used in strategic marketing. It provides an appreciation of where marketing strategies fit within the overall corporate and business strategies of an organisation, and the importance of these. The topic explains how the focus of marketing plans will vary according to the stage of the product's life cycle. Other key subject areas will include the marketing mix, target marketing, consumer segmentation, and strategic market planning.
learning_outcomes: Provide succinct and well researched analysis of tools and models for marketing strategy and planning
Examine and analyse the internal and external environment that influences strategies and decisions
Communicate well in a group environment and work collaboratively
Use marketing planning concepts and critical thinking to provide the rationale for strategic decisions
Explain various marketing concepts, their connection with marketing strategies and their application in a marketing plan
Critique concepts and theories in relation to marketing strategies and planning
Develop a concise marketing plan

title: Data Analysis for Decision Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to equip students with the knowledge and confidence to apply a range of data analysis techniques across various business contexts. The overarching goal is to empower students to make data-driven decisions while understanding how to effectively safeguard data in workplace environments.

This topic introduces students to the principles, tools, and methods of data analysis relevant to managerial decision-making in a business context. Students will explore various types of data, applying techniques such as different machine learning models, and the fundamentals of cybersecurity. By focusing on practical business use cases, students will develop the skills to transform raw data into meaningful insights that support strategic decisions, while also understanding how to protect sensitive information. Real-world case studies will illustrate how these techniques influence decision-making across a range of business scenarios, integrating theory with practical application.
learning_outcomes: Transform raw data into actionable insights by organising, analysing, and presenting it effectively in visual formats
Understand and implement the fundamentals of cybersecurity, ensuring the protection of sensitive data in business contexts
Apply data analysis techniques to solve business problems and support decision-making
Use machine learning models to predict business outcomes and inform strategic decisions

title: Data Analysis for Decision Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to give the graduate the confidence to explore various mathematical and statistical tools, some through Microsoft Excel. The topic aims to provide analytical tools and skills that students can apply to their work environments to enhance the decision making process by the inclusion of appropriate data analysis. The overarching aim of this topic is to give the students the understanding and confidence to explore the various analytical options made available in their workplace and to be able to utilise these options.

This topic will introduce students to the platform, tools, types of data and analysis applicable to managerial decision making in a business context. Decisions requiring mathematical analysis within accounting, finance, management and economics will be reviewed and explored. Basic mathematical and statistical concepts will be briefly refreshed and then utilised, including within the Microsoft Excel platform. Within this platform data will be assessed for its relevance and then manipulated to produce information of value to the user.
learning_outcomes: Perform various statistical tests
Utilise financial mathematical and statistical concepts and techniques applicable to the analysis of relevant data for business decisions
Summarize the data and present them graphically
Organise and analyse data relevant to the problems they encounter as managers within both business and large institutional organisations

title: Leadership: Theory, Practice and Experience
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to have students understand: How leadership and management are different and how they are used to achieve business and societal goals The roles of leaders, teams, followers and situations in business and society How leaders should act in times of crisis and how and why what they should do often differs from what is actually done Why leadership development is important for continuing success of businesses and other entities The role played in history by leaders whose actions can teach us about modern society The role of experiential learning in leadership and personal development

The topic aims to provide students with skills and knowledge to improve their potential to assume or further develop leadership positions in all three business sectors. The topic builds on skills in problem recognition and solving, in business practices and human interaction issues. The topic covers leadership and management differences, the development of leadership, teams and followers, situational effects, leadership in crises and change and leadership skills. The approach is multi-faceted with business, politics, society and historical aspects covered. A special feature of the format is the experiential program designed to give students exposure to team work and reflection within an experiential context.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise and analyse current research in leadership and apply theory of leadership to practice
Determine their likely roles as leaders or active followers in a work situation through group discussions and self-reflection
Apply leadership knowledge and skills during group exercises, through written assignments and presentations to class groups and guest business people
Assess leadership capabilities through cases, using judgment and interaction with others
Demonstrate an understanding of leadership in action through class interaction and case studies that draw on leadership knowledge

title: Financial Markets and Institutions
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a background in the operations of financial institutions and intermediaries, the instruments they use and the contributions they make to the efficient flow of funds within the economic system. The broad objective of the topic is to introduce students to the Australian financial system. In doing so, it also provides a framework for understanding financial systems of other countries. The understanding gained will significantly assist students in other finance topics that they may study, and in operating in the financial sector.

The topic provides students with an introduction to the financial system. It covers different financial markets, the financial instruments which are used, and the institutions which operate in the markets. Emphasis is on the Australian financial market, but sections of the topic also introduce international financial markets and their impact on the Australian economy. The topic focuses on debt, equity, foreign exchange and derivative security markets.
learning_outcomes: Explain the characteristics of various forms of short-term, medium to long-term and government debt and identify the advantages and disadvantages for borrowers and lenders. Calculate the pricing of and evaluate the various debt instruments

Describe equity funding alternatives and the associated regulatory controls and factors that influence equity capital markets. Calculate the price of shares based on the various equity funding alternatives
Discuss the functions of the modern financial system, the role of financial institutions and markets and the different types of financial instruments

Identify the participants in and describe the mechanics of foreign exchange markets. Describe the conventions for the quotation of foreign exchange, determine a forward exchange rate and recognise other factors which influence foreign exchange rates
Describe the main activities of banks and non-bank financial institutions including their sources and uses of funds and the way in which their activities are regulated
Explain the role of derivative products in risk management and develop a hedging strategy using futures contracts and options
Explain the interest rate risk and analyse the structure and benefits associated with interest rate risk measurement

title: Advanced Issues in Finance
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic builds on the financial management principles introduced in BUSN9227 Financial management. It analyses the concept of value and the financial objectives of corporations. The investment, financing and dividend decisions of the organisation are analysed at a more advanced level, and whether these decisions add value. A number of more applied topics will also be covered including real options, corporate acquisitions, corporate restructuring, lease financing and project financing.

This topic builds on financial management principals, and analyses the concept of value and the financial objectives of organisations. The investment, financing and dividend decisions of the organisation are analysed at a more advanced level. The topic focuses on whether these decisions add value to the organisation. A number of more applied topics will also be covered including real options, corporate acquisitions, corporate restructuring, lease financing and project financing.
learning_outcomes: Offer relevant normative advise on a number of areas of corporate finance practice including real corporate options, corporate acquisitions, corporate restructuring lease financing and project financing
Discuss the important theoretical foundations that underpin modern corporate finance practice
Analyse the prospects of particular business capital budgeting and financing decisions for increasing the value of the organisation
Identify emerging issues in the world of corporate restructuring, lease financing and project financing

title: International Business in the Asia Pacific Region
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
With emphasis on the next ten years, the aim of this topic is to provide students with individual and group opportunities to: Analyse the business context (past, present and trends) of specific industries within selected Asia-Pacific countries Place the aforesaid countries in a regional and global business context Identify and analyse ethical, security, political (bilateral and multilateral), environmental and other issues in the evolving business climate of the region

The topic theme is 'Contextual change: The past, present and future of international business in the region'. Weekly seminars explore political, environmental, cultural, security and other issues that influence business. Student projects speculate on the future of an industry in a specific country.
learning_outcomes: Advise businesses on trends in a particular industry in a specific country in the region after completion of thorough research
Contribute original ideas and analysis in interactive seminars
Write well-researched consulting reports with feasible recommendations for managerial action
Work efficiently in study teams
Apply the case study method to international business situations
Identify and understand the internal and external influences that an organisation needs to consider when operating across national borders in the Asia-Pacific Region

school: College of Business, Government and Law

learning_outcomes: Apply the case study method to international business situations
Contribute original ideas and analysis in interactive seminars
Work efficiently in study teams
Advise businesses on trends in a particular industry in a specific country in the region after completion of thorough research
Write well-researched consulting reports with feasible recommendations for managerial action
Identify and understand the internal and external influences that an organisation needs to consider when operating across national borders in the Asia-Pacific Region

title: International Business Finance and Banking
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The focus of this topic is the financial management environment and issues faced by international business enterprises because of their international operations. Many financial management issues are common to domestic and international businesses. Businesses with international operations have available to them economic advantages and opportunities that are not available to enterprises which only operate in domestic economies. International businesses also face additional risks because of the cross-border nature of their business. Taking advantage of these opportunities and managing these additional risks with the financial markets and banks are a recurring theme through the topic. Emphasis will be given to managing the multinational corporation and banks, but many of the issues discussed in the topic are also relevant for firms with more restricted international business dealings.

The topic introduces students to international business and banking transactions and their impact on financial decision-making within an organisation having an international perspective. The topic will include study of the international monetary system and foreign exchange rate determination, foreign exchange risk analysis and management, international investment decisions and the financing of international business operations.
learning_outcomes: Calculate the cost of capital for foreign investments
Compare and contrast different ways for managing foreign exchange risk
Explain how exchange rates are determined and the different exchange rate systems faced by international business dealings
Discuss the nature, characteristics and economic importance of multinational corporations
Describe the features of international banking and liquidly management through global financial markets
Explain capital budgeting in a multinational corporation
Discuss the factors affecting foreign exchange rates
Distinguish different types of international transactions, such as trade and capital flows, and their economic consequences

title: International Human Resources Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce issues in, and strategies for, managing the workforce in international business operations. Much of the topic is based on international business case studies and International Human Resource Management (IHRM) theory, research and practice, and involves a high level of student participation. Students will be expected to develop an understanding of: IHRM vs. domestic HRM International HRM planning, staffing and organisational structure International recruitment and selection Staff training and development Expatriation and repatriation Performance appraisal and compensation International employment relations Managing multicultural teams Managing diversity HRM issues in international joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions

This topic provides students with an introduction to issues in, and strategies for managing the workforce in international business operations. It extends basic principles in Human Resource Management (HRM) to the international business arena, and examines HRM issues that are distinctive features of global, transnational and multidomestic business operations. Areas covered include: international HRM planning and staffing; international recruitment and selection; staff training and development; expatriation and repatriation; international employment relations; managing multicultural teams; managing diversity; performance appraisal; compensation; HRM issues in international joint ventures, mergers and acquisitions.
learning_outcomes: Conduct collaborative research and deliver oral international IHRM case presentations and written reports
Analyse and report on the IHRM components of contemporary business operations
Examine and interpret written international business cases, with particular emphasis on IHRM elements
Write reflectively on the effect of national culture and other personal attributes on student motivation and learning
Investigate and critically analyse IHRM theory and research

title: International Marketing and Export Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Identify key elements in the selection of export markets Examine various aspects of international marketing and export management Explain the fundamentals of international marketing Analyse export market selection and entry, product and pricing decisions Examine financing options and methods of payment Identify key promotion and marketing communications in overseas markets

This topic introduces students to various aspects of international marketing and export management. The topic will include the fundamentals of international marketing, export market selection and entry, product and pricing decisions, financing and methods of payments, and promotion and marketing communications in overseas markets.
learning_outcomes: Understand key international marketing concepts
Create well-structured outcomes focused strategic international business reports
Carry out the research necessary for effective international marketing
Design sustainable export marketing strategies

title: International Marketing and Export Management
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Identify key elements in the selection of export markets Examine various aspects of international marketing and export management Explain the fundamentals of international marketing Analyse export market selection and entry, product and pricing decisions Examine financing options and methods of payment Identify key promotion and marketing communications in overseas markets

This topic introduces students to various aspects of international marketing and export management. The topic will include the fundamentals of international marketing, export market selection and entry, product and pricing decisions, financing and methods of payments, and promotion and marketing communications in overseas markets.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain key international marketing concepts
Create well-structured outcomes focussed business reports
Exhibit valuable interpersonal and teamwork skills
Carry out the research necessary for effective international marketing
Demonstrate effective oral, written and presentation leadership skills commensurate with a professional business role
Design and implement sustainable export marketing strategies
Interpret and extrapolate data for a relevant business and social context

title: Business Research Methods and Project
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide you with a range of research methods and theories upon which you will conduct project based research on your chosen area of specialisation. You will be required to communicate your findings, both orally and in wiritng, in a manner appropriate for a selection of audiences. You will be encouraged to think creatively, to integrate and apply knowledge and skills aquired throughout your studies, to identify and solve real business problems or address existing issues present in organisations.

This topic develops research knowledge and skills that are appropriate for business-related research that identifies and solves real business problems or addresses existing issues present in organisations. Students will be required to conduct research in their chosen field of specialisation and communicate the results to a variety of audiences.
learning_outcomes: Choose and apply relevant theory to a business issue
Apply an appropriate research methodology to solve an authentic business related issue
Present a research proposal and project findings in both written and oral formats that are appropriate for academic and business audiences
Gather, analyse, and interpret data
Critically analyse and synthesise a body of literature
Undertake independent research using a recognised methodology and framework

title: International Study Tour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
Gain an appreciation of the cultural milieu of the country (or countries) visited Experience the world of a student at an international educational institution Build understanding of social, political and economic issues in other countries Gain knowledge relating to the actual topics studied (usually including content about management, international relations, intercultural issues, etc

This topic enables students to undertake an organised study tour to an international location. The details of individual International Study Tours will vary depending on the destination, the timing, the host organisation(s), the number of students, etc. Students can enrol only when they have been accepted for a study tour.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of major social and political issues relating to the country visited
Recognise the implications of study and travel in the country (or countries) visited
Demonstrate knowledge gained from actual topics studied
Discuss inter-cultural differences

title: Advanced Recruitment and Selection
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop the skills and knowledge required to equip students to understand the options available to practitioners in designing an evidence-based selection and recruitment solution. Students learn to evaluate different methods and to determine the best methods that are fit-for-purpose taking into account the scale of the Organisation, the number of appointments and the scale of the recruitment campaign required.

This topic aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills required to strategically align recruitment and selection practises with organisational priorities. Students will be equipped with skills and knowledge to differentiate between different approaches and then to select those that best meet with organisational needs - covering large organisations to SMEs. Part of the course work will require a critical analysis of the recruitment and selection strategies used in an Organisation and to design an intervention that improves outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Assess strengths and weaknesses of different selection methods
Critically evaluate recruitment and selection methods used in Organisations
Appraise the alignment between an Organisation's strategic objectives and recruitment strategy
Critique methods and psychometric properties of different selection methods
Determine options for different recruitment campaigns
Design an intervention to improve recruitment and selection within an Organisation

title: Performance Management and Rewards
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop the skills and knowledge required to equip students to understand the options available to practitioners in designing an evidence-based performance management and rewards program. Students learn to evaluate different methods and to determine the best methods that are fit-for-purpose taking into account the scale of the Organisation, the number of employees and management objectives.

This topic aims to equip students with advanced knowledge and skills required to strategically align Performance Management and Rewards practises with organisational priorities. Students will be equipped with skills and knowledge to differentiate between different approaches and then to select those that best meet with organisational needs - covering large organisations to SMEs. Part of the course work will require a critical analysis of the Performance Management and Rewards strategies used in an Organisation and to design an intervention that improves outcomes
learning_outcomes: Identify options for managing employees and rewarding performance that align with Organisational objectives
Identify the alignment between an Organisation's strategic objectives and performance management systems
Design an intervention to improve Performance Management and Rewards within an Organisation
Identify strengths and weaknesses of different reward schemes at an individual, group and organisational level
Critically evaluate a Performance Management and Rewards system used in an Organisations

title: Consumer Behaviour
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide knowledge about consumer behaviour and to develop their critical thinking through an understanding of the individual, group, and external factors that affect consumer behaviour. This involves the identification of patterns of purchase, understanding various theories and schools of thoughts related to consumer decision making and understanding how customer analysis affects marketing strategy.

This topic focuses on one of the essential marketing subject: consumer behaviour. Students will learn various Schools of thoughts related to consumer decision making and choice. They will learn how knowledge about consumer behaviour relates to the marketing of products and services in both the private and public sectors. Subjects covered include: the role of consumer behaviour in marketing; the consumer as an individual; the consumer in social and cultural settings; the marketing decision-making process.
learning_outcomes: Identify key implications for organisational success
Apply the key conceptual consumer behaviour tools in support to strategic and tactical marketing
Distinguish examples of successful v. unsuccessful marketing practices
Illustrate the importance of consumer behaviour to marketing practices
Develop and summarise a consumer behaviour project relevant to real and scenario-based marketing practices
Identify and discuss the key theoretical principles of consumer behaviour

title: Data Warehousing for Business Decision Making
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aim of this topic is to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary to design, implement, and manage data warehouses to aid data-driven decision making in complex organisational contexts. This topic provides students with a comprehensive understanding of data warehousing concepts and various data warehousing architectures commonly used in industry. In this topic students will learn best practices for data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL); as well as ethical practices for maintaining high quality data. This topic equips students with knowledge and skills to utilise data warehousing for strategic decision making by providing an integrated repository of analysed data.

This topic explores the intricacies of data warehousing for business leaders, with an emphasis on advanced areas including data warehouse architectures, design, and modelling. It provides students with a comprehensive introduction to key concepts and applications of data warehousing in modern organizations, such as Extract, Transform and Load (ETL) processes. The topic highlights how these processes facilitate decision-making through the use of advanced analytical tools.
learning_outcomes: Apply data warehousing techniques and best practices to create and maintain data warehouses
Implement data warehouses to support decision-making processes for organisations
Critique real-world scenarios where data warehousing plays crucial role in business decision making in different contexts
Justify the purpose and significance of data warehousing within organisations
Evaluate and analyse the impact of data quality on decision-making
prerequisites: Admission into MABAFP-Master of Applied Business Analytics - Flinders City Campus

title: Industry Placement
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to broaden a student's knowledge and skills through a placement in a business setting. The placement experience is designed to help the student become more fully prepared for a business career.

Students undertake an industry placement. Students are placed and matched with placements according to availability and suitability or students can source their own placement with approval. Students are prepared for their placement, enter into a learning contract to guide the work integrated learning experience and are supervised.
learning_outcomes: Apply discipline based knowledge and skills to professional workplace practice
Formulate personal workplace competencies goals
Appraise personal workplace performance
Apply effective and appropriate communication, interpersonal and organisational competencies in workplace setting
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MBAIF-Master of Business Administration Industry Focused - 2 years 1a Admission into MBAIFFP-Master of Business Administration Industry Focused - Flinders City Campus - 2 years 1b Admission into MHADFFP-Master of Health Administration 2 GPA minimum of 5 across 36 units Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b) and 2)

title: Higher Degree Thesis (Master)
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aims of this time-based thesis topic are to support students to develop specialised knowledge and research skills related to the area of their chosen research field. They will acquire the appropriate research skills and training to enable them to work independently and complete a body of research at the level of a Masters by research qualification.

This time-based thesis topic supports students to acquire the skills and knowledge to independently complete a Master's degree by research in their chosen field and develop the capacity to complete a body of work to meet the standards of a Masters by Research award. It is only available to students admitted to a Master's degree by research.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate their capacity to formulate a significant problem and synthesise a complex body of knowledge
Validate research through critical analysis of source material, results of experiments (where appropriate), and published works
Justify and disseminate acquired knowledge and skills through the presentation of well-written work
Demonstrate their review and application of the literature in writing and orally (where appropriate)
Explain their understanding of chosen methodological practices

title: Higher Degree Thesis (PhD)
school: College of Business, Government and Law
syllabus_overview:
The aims of this time-based thesis topic are to support students to develop specialised knowledge and research skills related to the area of their chosen research field. They will acquire high-level research skills and training, to enable them to work independently and complete a body of original research at the level of a Doctorate by research qualification.

This time-based thesis topic supports students to acquire the skills and knowledge to independently complete a Doctorate by research in their chosen field and develop the capacity to complete a body of work to meet the standards of a Doctorate by research award. It is only available to students admitted to a Doctorate by research.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate their review and application of the literature in writing and orally (where appropriate)
Justify and disseminate acquired knowledge and skills through the presentation of well-written work
Explain their mastery of appropriate conceptual and methodological skills
Independently assess evidence of an original investigation or testing of ideas and competence in independent research or experimentation
Validate the originality of their research topic in relation to a broader framework of knowledge
Assess research through critical analysis of source material, results of experiments (where appropriate), and published works

title: Chemistry 1A
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Reinforce and expand upon Year 12 Chemistry in South Australia while introducing students to new areas of chemistry Provide students with foundations of theorectical and practical skills that are essential to a career as a professional chemist Provide the necessary grounding in basic chemistry for students who will eventually major in other disciplines Explore modern methods of molecular identification, redox and organic chemistry, kinetics and physical chemistry

This topic will cover aspects of the following chemistry concepts: • Chemical equilibrium • Acid – base equilibria • Molecular geometry • Intermolecular forces • The chemistry of organic compounds • Polymers and biopolymers • Electrochemistry • Thermodynamics and reaction kinetics In addition, students will use their knowledge of chemistry to solve ‘real world’ problems and will gain expertise in conducting chemical experiments using laboratory apparatus.
learning_outcomes: Develop skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation.
Develop independent study skills.
Develop useful generic and scientific skills in Chemistry and start to develop chemical intuition for type of reactions or chemical transformations that might occur as relevant to the topic syllabus.
Demonstrate an understanding of and the ability to apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic syllabus.
Develop teamwork and problem-solving skills in addition to strengthening their own self-learning skills.
Develop communication skills, skills in solving problems and build self-confidence.

title: Chemistry 1B
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Reinforce and expand upon Year 12 Chemistry in South Australia while introducing students to new areas of chemistry Together with related higher year topics, provide students with the full complement of theorectical and practical skills that are essential to a career as a professional chemist Provide the necessary grounding in basic chemistry for students who will eventually major in other disciplines Explore modern methods of molecular identification, redox and organic chemistry, kinetics and physical chemistry Prepare students to undertake higher year studies in chemistry

This topic will cover advanced aspects of the following concepts: Chemical Structure and Bonding Reaction Kinetics Thermodynamics Electrochemistry Organic reactions Students will use laboratory equipment related to the above concepts. Attendance at laboratory classes is compulsory.
learning_outcomes: Develop independent study skills
Develop useful generic and scientific skills in Chemistry and start to develop chemical intuition for type of reactions or chemical transformations that might occur as relevant to the topic syllabus
Apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic syllabus
Demonstrate communication skills, skills in solving problems and build self-confidence
Demonstrate teamwork and problem-solving skills in addition to strengthening self-learning skills
Demonstrate skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation

title: General Chemistry
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with a little or no chemistry background enough information to be able to continue studies in chemistry and to assist in other topics offered within the university.

The subject matter in the topic has been chosen and organised to provide students with a background of chemical knowledge. It will be of special value to students who are insufficiently prepared in chemistry to enter CHEM1010 Chemistry 1A and who intend to proceed to a degree in chemistry, another area of science or social science. The topic deals with classification of matter, chemical symbols, formulae and equations, laws of chemical combination, atomic and molecular structure, bonding, relationships between bond type and physical properties, intermolecular forces, acids and bases, molarity, gas laws, liquids and their vapour pressures, elementary kinetics and thermodynamics.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of and ability to apply basic chemical concepts as outlined in the syllabus
Use calculations to determine the quantities of reagents or products needed or produced in a chemical reaction, and quantities needed to prepare solutions
Show an understanding of various types of chemical reactivity by producing balanced chemical equations to describe reactions
Develop an ability to accurately record and interpret results in a laboratory setting

Develop skills in safe handling and disposal of chemicals, and careful use of relevant equipment and instrumentation, which enable experimentation in a chemistry laboratory with due regard for the occupational health and safety of themselves and others

title: Analytical Chemistry II
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide an understanding of how X-Ray, IR, Raman, UV/vis and NMR techniques work and are used to give molecular information Provide laboratory experience in using the above techniques Give students skills and expertise in the analysis of spectral data for the identification of molecular structure

This topic covers the use of analytical chemistry to determine information about a substance in order to determine it's chemical structure. It will cover aspects of sample isolation and purification, and explore the use of spectral techniques including X-Ray, IR, NMR, Raman and UV spectroscopy along with mass spectrometry for determination of molecular structure.
learning_outcomes: Develop useful generic and scientific skills in Chemistry and expand the chemical intuition for type of reactions or chemical transformations relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus
Refine communication skills, skills in solving problems and build self-confidence
Refine skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus
Develop teamwork and problem-solving skills in addition to strengthening self-learning skills
Improve independent study skills
Apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic syllabus

title: Physical Chemistry II
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an insight into how and why reactions occur and what drives particular outcomes of reactions. Students will be exposed to discussions on what variables can be used to control chemical reactions and what techniques can be used to follow chemical reactions. The topic will give students an appreciation of the measurement of both the rate of a chemical reaction and the energy flow during the chemical reaction. The topic also aims to introduce fundamental concepts in electrochemistry and quantum chemistry.

This topic will teach the basis for physical processes and the factors governing physical processes. It will cover the following concepts: Thermodynamics Chemical Kinetics Electrochemistry Quantum Chemistry
learning_outcomes: Improve independent study and problem solving skills.
Develop useful generic and scientific skills in Chemistry and expand the chemical intuition for type of reactions or chemical transformations relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus
Apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic description.
Refine communication skills, skills in solving problems and build self-confidence.
Refine skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus.
prerequisites: CHEM1011

title: Environmental Chemistry
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to enable students to better understand the environment in which they live and the impact of natural and anthropogenic changes. Students will have knowledge that will enable them to consider areas of environmental science from a solid scientific base and make informed decisions.

This topic will teach the variation in elemental composition in the environment both natural and anthropogenic and the techniques used to investigate and interpret these. It will cover the following concepts: Creation of elements hydrogen and helium by fusion and light elements through Big Bang and subsequent production of heavier elements. Natural abundance in universe, solar system and earth. Difference in terrestrial (land), aquasphere (water) and atmosphere (air). Perturbations in composition - natural - water cycle, nitrogen cycle. Perturbations due to humans - mercury cycle - industrial revolution, fossil fuel burning etc Variations in geographical and geological distribution of elements and compounds. Leading to use of variations in environmental forensics - detection of unexpected chemicals or increased or decreased amounts and attributing to environmental polluters. Fundamentals presented in lectures and expanded and discussed in workshops and highlighted with reference to real examples in case studies. Case studies and hands-on lab work will cover topics such as Algal bloom and deslination plants, Micro/Nano Plastics, composition of the Flinders living lake and more.
learning_outcomes: Refine communication skills, skills in solving problems and build self-confidence
Improve independent study skills
Develop teamwork and problem-solving skills in addition to strengthening their own self-learning skills
Refine skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus

Develop useful generic and scientific skills in Chemistry and expand the chemical intuition for type of reactions or chemical transformations that might occur relevant to concepts outlined in the topic syllabus
Apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic syllabus

title: Organic Reactions
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with an appreciation of the basic reactions encountered in organic chemistry. This topic will teach students why and how organic reactions are carried out as well as an understanding of the underlying mechanism of the main reactions. Further, students will gain an appreciation of the factors affecting the main organic chemical reactions as well as stereochemical and regiochemical characteristics for these reactions. In addition students will be trained to carry out reactions safely and independently in a laboratory and to analyse and characterise the materials produced.

This topic will present students with the fundamentals of organic chemical synthesis. These are introduced initially by discussing the philosophy behind synthesis, a presentation on the mechanistic approach to understanding organic reactions followed by discussion on the main organic chemical reactions. The main organic reactions include for example; nucleophilic substitution and elimination, anion based chemistry (acetylenic anions, enolates, Grignard and organolithium reagents), addition reactions, and both electrophilic and nucleophilic aromatic substitution reactions. In addition students will learn about the stereochemical aspects of organic molecules and how these are influenced by organic reactions.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding about why basic organic reactions occur
Carry out basic organic chemistry reactions safely and independently in a laboratory and examine and characterise the compounds produced
Predict and rationalise mechanistically the products from a variety of chemical reaction conditions, and factors that may influence them
Evaluate and present results from laboratory work in written form
prerequisites: 1 of CHEM1011, CHEM1102

title: Analytical Chemistry III
school: College of Science and Engineering
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide students with advanced knowledge and skills in analytical chemistry techniques. Students will be introduced to a wide variety of techniques. A main focus of the topic is the practical use of analytical techniques.

This topic aims to cover the quantitative analytical chemistry. It will cover aspects of electrochemical analysis, chromatography, electrophoresis, and spectroscopic techniques including AAS, UV/Vis and fluorescence.
learning_outcomes: Apply skills in handling chemicals, apparatus and instrumentation relevant to concepts outline in the topic syllabus
Apply chemical concepts as outlined in the topic syllabus
Apply communication skills, skills in solving problems and build on their self-confidence
