Explain historical and social developments that have shaped both special and inclusive education, terminologies, concepts, roles, and service models
Outline legal and ethical professional practice standards and relevant policies and identify their implications for children and young people across a range of settings

title: Professional Experience: Year 1 (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce the professional experience program, its requirements and expectations Explain the professional expectations of teachers, including legal and ethical responsibilities Support the transitioning from student to teaching professional Establish understandings that will lead to successful professional experiences

This topic prepares students for their professional experiences. It introduces the Professional Standards for Teachers and includes an introduction to the legal and ethical responsibilities of the teaching professional. Students will be introduced to the expectations for their behaviour and learning during the days of their first professional experiences. This lecture series is an essential pre-requisite for placement.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the professional experience program and its requirements
Transition from the role of student to that of teaching professional
Demonstrate awareness of the many factors that will contribute to successful professional experiences
Recognise the legal and ethical responsibilities they will assume as they enter the teaching profession
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDPRBA-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into BEDPRSEBDS-B Education (Primary R-7 & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1b Admission into BEDPRBGSC-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of General Science 1c Admission into BAEPRP-Bachelor of Arts (Education (Primary) Pathway) 1d Admission into BAMTPR-Bachelor of Arts, Master of Teaching (Primary) 1e Admission into BGSCMTPR-Bachelor of General Science, Master of Teaching (Primary) 1f Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education 1g Admission into BEDPRBSE-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Special Education Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g))

title: Students with Learning and Behavioural Difficulties
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the general characteristics that define students with learning difficulties and those with learning disabilities. It also aims to develop the following broad special education principles: All children and youth can learn Learning is best supported when measured school-wide and classroom supports and strategies are put in place in a timely manner The school experiences of individuals who find learning difficult habitually have a direct and lasting impact on academic progress, social interaction, motivation and/or wellness Thoughtful, inclusive educational practices promote access to, participation in and achievement through the curriculum The elements of self-efficacy, curriculum, instruction, assessment, learning, engagement and behaviour are interdependent

This topic reviews the field of learning difficulties through an Australian and international context. It compares and contrasts the general characteristics of students who present with learning difficulties and those who present with learning disabilities in classrooms. It debates the appropriateness of professionally observed school-wide practices against published research studies in order to make judgements about the effectiveness of available programs, strategies and supports for students who find academic learning difficult at school. Using scenario-based learning participants will consider innate and environmental influences on learning to evaluate then determine suitable ways to promote participation, academic progress and emotional wellbeing for these individuals.
learning_outcomes: Make judgements about the appropriateness of research based and professional practices, strategies and supports for students with learning difficulties and learning disabilities
Describe the field of learning difficulties in Australian and international contexts
Provide reasoned suggestions for ways of improving school and curriculum access, participation and progress for students with learning difficulties and those with learning disabilities
Define the general characteristics of students with learning difficulties and those with learning disabilities
Summarize the wide-ranging impact of stress on learning and behaviour
prerequisites: 1 9 units of EDUC topics 1a Admission into BEDSEOS-Bachelor of Education (Special Education) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Professional Experience: Year 1 (Middle and Secondary Schooling)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce the professional experience program, its requirements and expectations Explain the professional expectations of teachers, including legal and ethical responsibilities Support the transitioning from student to teaching professional Establish understandings that will lead to successful professional experiences

This topic will prepare pre-service teachers for their initial professional experience participation days in Year 2 of their degree. It will introduce the expectations of professional behaviour for the teaching profession, including legal and ethical responsibilities. Pre-service teachers will be introduced to the expectations for their behaviour and learning during the days of their professional experiences. This lecture series is an essential pre-requisite for placement in school settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the professional experience program and its requirements
Demonstrate understanding the transition from the role of student to that of a teaching professional
Demonstrate recognition of the legal and ethical responsibilities they will assume as they enter the teaching profession
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDMSSBA-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Arts 1a Admission into BEDMSSBSC-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Science 1b Admission into BEDMSSBHS-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Health Sciences 1c Admission into BEDMSSEBDS-B Education (Middle & Secondary/Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1d Admission into BEDSBA-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Arts 1e Admission into BEDSBHS-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Health Sciences 1f Admission into BEDSBSC-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Science 1g Admission into BEDSBSE-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Special Education 1h Admission into BEDSBLANG-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Languages 1i Admission into BAESP-Bachelor of Arts (Education (Secondary) Pathway) 1j Admission into BAMTS-Bachelor of Arts, Master of Teaching (Secondary) 1k Admission into BSCMTS-Bachelor of Science, Master of Teaching (Secondary) 2 4.5 units of any first level Education topic Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g or 1h or 1i or 1j or 1k) and 2)

title: Language Development and Early Reading Skills
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce pre-service teachers to evidence-based pedagogies in language and early literacy development aligning with the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum English Language and Literacy strands and consider how their development is represented within these two frameworks. Cultivate knowledge of how communication, oral language, speech and early literacy develop in the early childhood and primary school years, including signals for language difficulties and characteristics of language difficulties or disorders. Evaluate and interpret research-informed models of language development and the components of language across receptive, expressive, spoken and written modalities. Provide an opportunity for pre-service teachers’ to appraise their own linguistic knowledge through the components of phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics and pragmatics and their relevance to language and literacy development.

This topic will introduce pre-service teachers to early language and literacy development in the early childhood and primary school years. The components of language are explored, and pre-service teachers learn how to appraise their own linguistic knowledge using metalanguage, and exploring phonology, morphology, syntax, semantic and pragmatics.A key focus of the topic is to understand how language is presented and taught in the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum Language and Literacy strand including language variation and change, language for interaction, text structure and organisation, expressing and developing ideas, and phonics and word knowledge.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate your own level of linguistic knowledge with associated metalanguage and appraise methods of constructing this knowledge further throughout your degree and beyond

Explain the components of speech sound, language, communication and early literacy development including linking spoken and written language and understanding the importance of oral language, phonological awareness and phonics instruction

Interpret what constitutes typical and atypical speech, language and early literacy development and apply this to relevant case studies in the early childhood and the primary school years using knowledge of evidence based cognitive research into effective classroom instruction
Organise knowledge of speech, language and emergent literacy development around the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the Australian Curriculum literacy and language sub-strands

title: Introduction to Contemporary Education: Pedagogy and Practice
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic provides pre-service teachers with an awareness of the key elements of grammar for education, introducing key terms and concepts, theories, and figures that impact education more broadly and teaching specifically.

This topic introduces pre-service teachers to the broad and contested field of education. Pre-service teachers will engage with historical, political, and sociological lenses for inquiry as frameworks for analysis and a basis for understanding their future work as teachers. As an induction to the profession, pre-service teachers will explore and position a range of pedagogical approaches with consideration of the range of contexts in which they will work.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate skills in analysing research literature and reflecting knowledgeably and critically on their own and others' educational experiences
Define and employ key concepts in education; including pedagogy, curriculum and assessment
Evaluate a range of pedagogical approaches and their application across multiple contexts
Identify and critically analyse the influence of social issues, including class, ethnicity, race and geographical location, on educational outcomes

title: Histories and Philosophies of Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Introduce pre-service teachers to a range of historical, theoretical, and philosophical perspectives in Early Childhood Education Provide pre-service teachers with the skills necessary to understand and interpret the socio-political intentions of these perspectives and their implications for practice Document a teaching philosophy statement informed by historical, comparative, and contemporary Australian and international Early Childhood perspectives Explore neuroscience and brain research findings to recognise the importance of optimal children’s learning and development in the first years of their life

Early Childhood Education is deeply enshrined in its historical origins and philosophical beginnings. In this topic, pre-service teachers will explore historical, comparative, and contemporary Australian and international perspectives of early childhood teaching by investigating a range of sociological drivers that sit behind early childhood theories, policies, and practices. Pre-service teachers will explore brain and neuroscience research findings to enrich their understandings of children’s learning and development. Using an inquiry approach, pre-service teachers will develop and revise a teaching philosophy statement informed by multiple perspectives and their own emerging values and beliefs as early years professionals.
learning_outcomes: Explain how Early Childhood Education perspectives shape our practice and how children’s early brain development influences their learning
Identify specific Early Childhood Education perspectives and their origins
Describe your own teaching values and beliefs in relation to these perspectives
Develop a philosophy statement that is written in an accessible, inclusive and actionable format

title: Multi‐tiered Systems of Support in Inclusive Educational Settings
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce preservice teachers to inclusive policies, practices and learning environments that embody a strengths‐based approach and empower children, families and local communities Cultivate a foundational understanding of multi‐tiered systems of support (MTSS) as a framework for inclusive and specialised education across academic, social and behavioural domains Encourage the development of critical, creative, reflective and collaborative understandings of teachers’ work with diverse students within a human rights framework Provide preservice teachers with a historical perspective on the education of students with special educational needs

Children and young people in educational settings may require particular attention at different times to support their academic engagement and progress, behaviour, and/or mental health and wellbeing. Rather than waiting until children experience difficulties requiring intensive intervention, contemporary approaches to student support emphasise a coordinated, flexible continuum of responses. This topic introduces preservice teachers to multi‐tiered systems of support approaches (MTSS), which incorporate (1) deliberate efforts to promote engagement and skill‐development for all students, and prevent academic, social and behavioural difficulties; (2) targeted, more intensive supports for students at risk or beginning to experience difficulties; and (3) specialised supports for students requiring more tailored responses. Preservice teachers will examine MTSS as a collaborative framework for inclusive and specialised education.
learning_outcomes: Compare MTSS approaches in inclusive and specialised education to historical practices in the education of students with disabilities and specific needs
Examine principles of primary prevention, transdisciplinary collaboration and student‐centred planning underpinning multi‐tiered systems of support (MTSS)
Interpret targeted programs and intensive interventions designed to support diverse children in the areas of academic learning, behaviour, communication and social‐emotional wellbeing
Employ key elements of a multi‐tiered systems of support (MTSS) framework
Analyse journal articles and write a critical analysis
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BISEEC-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) 1a Admission into BISEP-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Primary) 1b Admission into BISES-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Secondary) 1c Admission into BEDSEC-Bachelor of Education (Secondary) 1d Admission into BEDSHPE-Bachelor of Education (Secondary Health and Physical Education) 1e Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 1f Admission into BEDIE-Bachelor of Education (Inclusive Education) Must satisfy: (1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f)

title: Introduction to Teaching Learners with Complex Needs
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Prepare preservice teachers to know, understand and apply evidence‐based pedagogical practices designed for learners with complex needs Build preservice teacher knowledge and skills in authentic assessment, monitoring and evaluation of personalised pedagogical practices for learners with complex needs Prepare preservice teachers to understand the roles and responsibilities of diverse professionals who support learners with complex needs and how varied disciplines collaborate to develop highly personalised instructional programs.

This topic introduces preservice teachers to work effectively with students who have complex needs and learning difficulties. It explores research informed pedagogies, resources and practices aimed at enhancing learning and it develops knowledge about the roles and responsibilities of paraprofessionals and allied professionals who work in education settings. The construct of evidenced‐based practice (EBP) and the use and application of explicit and systematic instruction is a focus.
learning_outcomes: Develop authentic methods of informal assessment to inform the design and application of personalised instructional programs (e.g., observational baseline assessment)

Describe how to monitor, evaluate and review the effectiveness of personalised instructional programs for learners with complex support needs as an approach to formative assessment of learning and assessment of application of evidence‐based practice
Determine what constitutes evidence‐based teaching practice for learners with complex needs such as explicit and systematic instruction
Apply evidence‐based pedagogical practices to the design of personalised instructional programs for learners with complex needs

Describe the role and responsibilities of the specialist educator, the roles of support staff and the roles of other disability related professionals in the design and/or implementation of highly personalised instructional programs
prerequisites: EDUC1224 – Foundations of Inclusive and Specialised Education

title: Pedagogical Documentation in Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Assist pre-service teachers to synthesise theory and practice of how pedagogical documentation provides opportunities for early childhood educators to document, assess and plan for learning which supports children learning and engagement. Enable pre-service teachers to understand the characteristics, practices and purposes of pedagogical documentation in supporting children’s learning and development

Pedagogical documentation encompasses the work of educators and children as co-constructors of knowledge, positioning pre-service teachers to reflect on their practice to enhance the learning journeys of both child and educator. Drawing on contemporary early childhood research and the Early Years Learning Framework, this topic will explore the various approaches of pedagogical documentation which are reflected in the repertoire of meaningful and authentic planning in the early years. This includes pedagogical conversations with children, families and fellow educators to ensure that the process of documentation is collaborative and meaningful with multiple perspectives represented. Pre-service teachers will consider how pedagogical documentation contributes to the assessment of children’s learning and development, through giving all participants voice and further facilitating meaningful engagement in the curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Examine what is meant by pedagogical documentation to gain insight into how this documentation supports children’s engagement, understanding and development in the early years
Engage in professional conversations with colleagues and relate understanding about practice and the use of pedagogical documentation
Explore examples of various strategies and formats for gathering and analysing information about what children know, can do and understand

title: Science ‐ Exploring a Changing World
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enhance confidence, knowledge, and skills of pre‐service teachers in teaching integrated Chemical and Earth and Space Sciences with an Indigenous perspective and supported by inter‐curriculum links where appropriate Promote skills of pre‐service teachers in using experimental thinking for developing a series of learning experiences by reflecting and identifying opportunities to plan for professional learning needs Develop critical analysis skills of pre‐service teachers for evaluating teaching and assessment plans with considerations for connecting to professional networks and communities

This topic provides a detailed look at how people have discovered new wonders in a changing landscape. Pre‐service teachers will explore different methods for how experimentation can be purposefully integrated amongst science‐based explorations with children. Building on the everyday science concepts, play and inquiry processes are used to explore diversity and concepts of a changing world. Through a focused look at integrating Chemical Sciences and Earth and Space Sciences curriculum and Indigenous perspectives; pre‐service teachers will examine how humans have learnt to understand the world through trial and error. By generating data and combining materials from natural and manufactured origins, experimentation will demonstrate how scientists and engineers develop solutions to problems and change our world. Supported by Humanities and Social Sciences and Mathematics curricula, pre‐service teachers will explain how they plan to implement and assess to connect local and global perspectives through an integrated teaching approach with children.
learning_outcomes: Plan for integrated curriculum assessment strategies including moderating children’s work samples
Explore the roles of natural and manufactured resources and tools for constructing and building with a range of materials through experimentation
Examine the range of age‐appropriate skills and cross curriculum priorities relevant to science learning

Explain how Earth’s landscape, sky and natural resources are changed due to human activity, daily and seasonal changes, weather and cycles including day/night cycle and moon phases can be explored including how pre‐service teachers plan to engage with professional teaching networks and broader communities

Design a series of learning experiences using every day and specialised materials and equipment which challenge children to examine how earth and space can influence or direct activities through free‐form and structured experimentation

Evaluate through experimentation how objects are made from different materials to suit a purpose, can be changed in a variety of ways and combined, their physical properties can influence purpose and can change states and behave differently
prerequisites: EDUC1241

title: Science - Inquiring in a New World
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enhance the confidence, knowledge, and skills of pre‐service teachers in Biological Sciences, with a strong sustainability perspective and supported by inter‐curriculum links where appropriate Promote scientific thinking using inquiry processes with play approaches for developing a series of learning experiences and unit plans Develop critical analysis skills for developing and critiquing teaching plans using multimodal communication techniques which help engage and explain living things and the natural world to children

This topic provides a detailed look at how an inquiry process of discovery can be purposefully integrated amongst science explorations with children. Building on everyday science concepts, play and inquiry processes are used to discover concepts of the new world. This topic provides inter‐curricular teaching strategies for the investigation of the new world by connecting children with nature. By looking at integrating Biological Sciences curriculum content with the skills of inquiry and strong links to sustainability practices and nature‐based learning, pre‐service teachers will explore the natural environment and use of technologies to design solutions to solve real world environmental problems. Drawing upon children’s literature as provocations, pre‐service teachers will learn how to develop children's scientific concepts intentionally and incidentally. Supported by English, Technologies and Arts curricula, this topic will explore techniques to discover and analyse integrated learning and teaching practices in the Early Years and Primary Years.
learning_outcomes: Explore the roles of natural world and simple tools for investigating the world through inquiry and play‐based teaching approaches
Evaluate plans for learning experiences and assessment with peers by providing feedback and identify gaps in knowledge and skills to plan for professional learning needs

Explain how living things have needs for survival, have observable features which differ and change over time, have life cycles, and features of adaptations to help them survive and grow in different environments when affected by different conditions in their environment

Design a series of learning experiences and assessment for supporting children’s interaction with the natural environment and living things connected to solving a local or global environmental problem

Examine the structure of science as a learning area in the Early Years and Primary curriculum to target physical, social, and intellectual development and characteristics of learners at different stages
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1a Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 1b Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 1c Admission into BEDPRBA-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Arts Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c))

title: The Developing Child (Professional Experience: Year 1B)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Enrich pre-service teachers' understanding of the theoretical perspectives of children’s physical, social, emotional, language and cognitive development, aged birth-8 Enable pre-service teachers to practise a variety of observation/assessment techniques to gain insight into the types of experiences, activities and ideas that engage young children and identify key developmental milestones Assist pre-service teachers to plan, implement and evaluate learning experiences that link to the curriculum, make a meaningful contribution to children’s learning, and extend their development Provide pre-service teachers with opportunities to work as a contributing member of the educational team, gathering evidence of developing professional knowledge, practice, and relationships

This topic will further develop pre-service teachers’ capacity to apply the methods used to observe, document, and assess children’s learning and development. Pre-service teachers will think critically and apply developmental and sociocultural theories as appropriate. Focusing on the concept of inclusion, pre-service teachers will plan for and justify their teaching approach, considering developmentally appropriate practice. This topic continues the professional experience placement from the previous placement topic, engaging pre-service teachers in a metropolitan early childhood setting over an extended period. Visiting the site for 1-day per week for 10-weeks, pre-service teachers track young children’s learning over time and develop an understanding of how a site changes through different seasons. Pre-service teachers begin to see how theory informs practice as they observe young children and make a plan for their learning, working with individual children, small groups and then the whole group. Through a focused inquiry project, pre-service teachers make a valuable contribution to children’s learning and development, combining theory with observations, planning, teaching, evaluation and documentation.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement and evaluate a series of experiences that are responsive to the observed needs and interests of young children
Examine historical and contemporary theories which underpin child observation, namely developmental and sociocultural theories and how these inform practice
Illustrate competency in observing children’s learning and development to make inferences about pedagogy, curriculum links and learning
Employ strategies for working inclusively as a pre-service teacher, including pedagogical approaches which support children from diverse backgrounds and those with specific needs

Show awareness of the broader aspects of early childhood learning, including an understanding of the environment as the third teacher, collegial learning and the importance of relationships with children and families
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1a Admission into BECEB-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education- Birth to 5 2 EDUC1221 2a ^ EDUC1239 Must satisfy: ((1 or 1a) and (2 and 2a)) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Understanding and Teaching Diverse Learners (Primary) and Professional Experience 1
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Inter‐connect theoretical and practical knowledge and understanding about diverse learners and their development, with implications for practice and reference to the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers Prepare preservice teachers for professional experience through an introduction to placement requirements and expectations Develop an appreciation of the ways in which educational psychology informs the teacher’s understanding of and provisions for diverse learners Cultivate opportunities to develop critical thinking, argument and authentic problem‐solving skills through written and verbal communication Develop a deep appreciation of the need for safe, inclusive and protective classrooms for the positive development of diverse learners, and the implications for how teachers might establish and manage a safe, inclusive and protective classroom Develop knowledge and experience of a professional and collaborative community of learners

Understanding students and their development through the theoretical lenses of Educational Psychology, while at the same time developing a professional identity and insight into teaching diverse students, are core and parallel aims of the topic. Effective teaching for student learning and well‐being requires an understanding of the diversity of learners ‐ their development, their contexts, their individual differences and the various factors which impact on their development, learning and well‐being. Educational Psychology theories which help to understand learners, and which underpin effective teaching practice, will be examined using critical analysis and reflection. Pre‐service teachers will work in small groups to complete a Problem‐Based Learning case study to investigate the ways in which teachers might design and maintain inclusive, safe and protective learning environments where diverse students can thrive. Learning in this topic will be linked to preparation for professional experience, providing the opportunity to make clear connections between theory and practice. Successful completion of this topic is an essential pre‐requisite for placement.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the many factors that will contribute to successful professional experience
Compose a sound and well‐reasoned argument in both written texts and oral presentations
Appraise the elements which contribute to effective collaboration within a community of learners
Apply research‐informed principles and practices to explain how a teacher might establish a supportive learning environment where diverse students can thrive
Analyse a developmental issue and explain how Educational Psychology theories inform teachers’ knowledge and understanding of diverse learners and their development
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 1a Admission into BISEP-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Primary) Must satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Communities of Practice: Enabling Learning
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to explore the beliefs, traditions, and values across and within cultures which affect relationships among and between children and young people, their families, and the educational setting. Pre-service teachers will engage with the application of pedagogy to effectively prepare, plan, and deliver engaging learning in the context of preschool and schooling with a core focus on establishing safe and inclusive classroom environments.

This topic examines the process of teaching and learning by bringing theory and practice together. It provides pre-service teachers with the opportunity to engage with educational literature that will inform the development of their pedagogical repertoire. Pre-service teachers will develop their understandings of what a supportive learning environment involves through their involvement in a community of practice. This will specifically include working with school students, fellow pre-service teachers, school staff and university lecturers.
learning_outcomes: Apply research-informed principles to establish supportive learning environments
Identify and communicate critical links between contemporary education theory and practice
Critically reflect on how educators can develop enabling conditions for learning
Appraise pre-service teacher learning within a community of practice

title: Partnerships, Parents and Participation
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Assist pre‐service teachers to develop an understanding of the social construction of families and childhoods Introduce pre‐service teachers to the concept of family‐centred, strengths‐based practice in early childhood settings Enable pre‐service teachers to critically analyse a wide variety of resources and approaches for working in partnership with families to enhance learning opportunities for young children, including those with special rights

This topic addresses the interface between early childhood education and care with the lives of children and families in diverse contexts. Through case studies of early childhood educators working effectively in partnership with diverse families and a range of agencies, the topic develops an understanding of the social constructions of families and childhoods, the social practices they adopt and the services in which they participate. Approaches to strengths‐based, family‐centred practice are also explored.
learning_outcomes: Explore a range of resources and approaches for effectively partnering with families to optimise learning opportunities for young children, considering diversity, inclusivity, and cultural responsiveness in educational practices
Articulate a family-centred, strengths-based approach to working in partnership with parents and other agencies in early childhood settings
Develop an understanding of the social construction of families and childhoods, including cultural, societal, and historical factors influencing perceptions and practices

title: The Expressive Arts in Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enhance pre-service teacher confidence, knowledge and skills in learning and teaching the Expressive Arts Enable pre-service teachers to generate and synthesise an inclusive and appropriate Expressive Arts program for children aged birth-5 or birth-8 years Enhance pre-service teachers’ personal approach to teaching the Expressive Arts based on their critical analysis of practical experience as well as in the light of a range of theoretical perspectives

Through an integrated teaching approach this topic introduces an understanding of the role of creative expression in society. Creative development is linked to theories of child development and to the importance of providing every child with the opportunity to practice and develop in creative expression. The themes of analysis, response and practice are explored in relation to the different forms of creative expression and in different cultural and vocational contexts. Students are introduced to a variety of appropriate teaching methodologies and resources, the importance of classroom organisation and materials management, the use of information and communication technologies and to necessary practical skills for teaching in the areas of the expressive arts. Current curriculum frameworks are used for planning for learning, and students address long-term planning for teaching encompassing rich, integrated learning, inclusive teaching practices, and the embedded use of information and computer technology.
learning_outcomes: Develop resources and a range of methodologies and skills for teaching the expressive arts
Demonstrate an ability to plan, analyse and critique an inclusive and developmentally appropriate and balanced expressive arts program for children aged birth-5 or birth-8
Foster children's curiosity and play as they investigate their social and physical worlds through the expressive arts

title: Health and Physical Education in Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Equip pre-service teachers with the skills and attitudes to be proactive in the implementation of the early learning strategy which aims to have all young children thriving and learning in childcare, preschool and school settings. Develop evidence-based foundational knowledge and competencies that ensure pre-service teachers can contribute to the monitoring of developmental milestones for diverse populations (including CALD and Indigenous children), plan and implement lessons and curricula and be responsive to a child’s point of need. Embed a mindset of self-care including strategies that create healthy boundaries, self-reflection and the challenging of assumptions to promote inclusive practices in everyday interactions with children, colleagues and families.

This topic aims to equip pre-service teachers with a mindset and tools that align with strength based early intervention principles. This topic embraces current evidence-based best practice that strives to build capacity in preschoolers, equipping them for the demands of school and beyond. Central to this goal are the frameworks provided by government policy which seek to reduce the percentage of developmentally vulnerable children at the time of starting school. Health and Physical Education encompass a broad range of wellbeing issues that are impactful in achieving this goal. From the joint perspectives of both education and public health, the holistic developmental needs of the child are at the forefront. Pre-service teachers will engage with early intervention models involving evidence-based screening tools and frameworks to determine point of need and to guide and inform inclusive practice and embrace diversity. A strengths-based approach will be promoted alongside play based pedagogies, wellbeing and physical activity as tools for the promotion of healthy habits for childhood and for life.
learning_outcomes: Apply evidence-based topic content and frameworks to case study scenarios using a problem-solving approach that is consistent with inclusive practices and supports the diverse needs of learners
Identify and analyse relevant issues concerning the implementation of proactive wellbeing and physical activity approaches to ensure the holistic growth of children to thriving
Select appropriate health and physical education programs for an Early Childhood setting and plan a lesson using a repertoire of inclusive, evidence informed content and teaching strategies
Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of educator self-reflection and self-care to model and maintain health and wellbeing for self and others

title: Literacy Across the Curriculum
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to ensure that pre-service teachers engage with evidence‐informed approaches to teaching literacies to develop understandings, knowledge and skills for supporting literacy learning across curriculum learning areas. Pre-service teachers will develop and enact strong personal literacy capabilities as they produce and critique a range of multimodal texts and explore their responsibilities to teach literacies within specific areas of the curriculum.

This topic supports pre-service teachers to develop a robust understanding of literacy, drawing from contemporary discussions, and engaging with the rapid pace of technological change, and the consequent implications for text production/ consumption. Pre-service teachers articulate the language and literacy demands associated with curriculum content in their learning area/s and are supported to develop appropriate metalanguage and other linguistic knowledge associated with expertise in their discipline area. PSTs develop their understanding of these disciplinary literacies as foundational to supporting students’ success throughout secondary education as the content knowledge becomes increasingly specialised with educational level. This topic supports pre-service teachers to develop confidence and competence in their personal literacy skills (oral, written, and digital), noting that these are integral to the inherent requirements of teaching.
learning_outcomes: Develop and use the metalanguage specific to the disciplinary literacies of a teaching area to design and discuss learning experiences that build students’ literacy capacity, including strategies to pre-assess and monitor literacy capabilities

Investigate and analyse the nature of literacies in contemporary society and schooling, and the consequent responsibility of teachers to demonstrate both proficient use of literacies, and life-long learning in relation to literacies
Establish a series of goals in relation to personal literacy skills (oral, written or digital), and engage in a structured learning plan to meet these goals

title: Foundations of Effective Teaching Practice: Understanding the Brain and Learning
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre-service teachers’ understanding of normative development across multiple domains (physical, social, emotional, cognitive) from infancy to early adulthood Enhance pre-service teachers’ understanding of neuroscientific principles to inform evidence-based instructional strategies that debunk prevalent neuromyths in education and optimise learning outcomes for students at various stages of development Begin to develop PST capacity to be responsive to diverse student needs (including Indigenous and CALD) through the application of evidence- based instructional practices, whole school frameworks, professional growth, self-reflection and self- care

This topic examines the foundational evidence-based cognitive principles that are foundational to effective contemporary teaching practice. Pre-service teachers will explore normative development across physical, social, emotional, and cognitive domains from infancy to early adulthood. Through a blend of theoretical insights and practical applications, pre-service teachers will explore novice brain progression toward mastery, understanding how expertise develops and its implications for teaching. Cognitive factors such as working memory and cognitive load theory will be presented. Common neuromyths prevalent in education will be examined and PST will learn how to discern evidence-based practices from misinformation. The topic equips future educators with the knowledge and critical thinking abilities essential for creating engaging and impactful learning experiences. Reflective practice will be explored as a conduit for responsive teaching of diverse learners and for self care.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the mechanisms through which the brain learns and retains information, including the transfer of knowledge from working memory to long-term memory and apply evidence-based teaching strategies to mitigate cognitive overload. Articulate the progression of knowledge to mastery in learners, adapting teaching practices accordingly to support students' transition from scaffolded to independent learning and problem-solving
Begin to develop the mindset and habits for responsiveness through professional self-reflection to enhance academic and wellbeing outcomes for self and learners

Examine physical, socio-emotional, and cognitive development in learners and assess how high-quality evidence-based classroom management and pedagogical practices support positive academic and wellbeing outcomes

Articulate an understanding of the MTSS (Multi-Tiered Systems of Support) framework and its application as a whole school approach to monitoring and managing the academic, emotional, and behavioural needs of diverse learners and their families
Develop awareness of and skills to critically examine the evidence base of contemporary pedagogical approaches against common neuromyths

title: Measurement and Geometry in Inclusive Classrooms
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Give students opportunities to develop their own understanding and competence with measurement concepts and geometric thinking Support students in exploring the conceptual foundations of measurement and geometry Enable students to identify and reflect upon children's emerging understanding, fluency, problem-solving and reasoning with measurement concepts and geometric thinking and share ways in which children's thinking and competence can be developed through effective pedagogies Build student capacity to ensure the engagement, participation and progress of all children through comprehensive knowledge of content and ways in which to differentiate and adjust learning

This topic seeks to teach students about how the study of foundational measurement concepts and geometric thinking are connected. Children's understanding of measurement and geometric thinking is significant for learning and progress in mathematics and will be explored through the use of the proficiency strands of the Australian Curriculum; understanding, fluency, problem-solving and reasoning. Children further develop their understanding of measurement and geometric thinking by exploring mathematical ideas. Students will study the Early Years Learning Framework, Australian Curriculum and Numeracy Progressions; and consider how children apply their developing knowledge. Students will be given opportunities to develop their own understanding and competence with measurement and geometry. Students will learn about effective pedagogies which promote the engagement and participation of children in mathematics in early childhood and school settings.
learning_outcomes: Review and critically analyse literature and discuss how children move from emergent to more proficient processes when working with measurement and geometry
Evidence their own working knowledge of measurement concepts and geometric thinking

Describe ways in which children's thinking and competence with measurement and geometry can be developed through effective pedagogies; and articulate ways to differentiate and adjust learning to ensure the engagement, participation and progress of all children
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education 1a Admission into BEDPRBSE-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Special Education 2 EDUC1231 - Number and Algebra in Inclusive Classrooms Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a) and 2)

title: Designing and Creating Digital Solutions
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre‐service teachers’ knowledge and understandings of the underlying concepts of information systems, data and the skills required to create digital solutions to problems and opportunities Provide pre-service teachers with an opportunity to experience effective digital technologies pedagogical practices Develop pre-service teachers' confidence to plan and assess learning activities, and identify resources to support the Australian Curriculum: Digital Technologies

This topic develops pre-service teachers' pedagogical content knowledge and confidence to plan, teach and assess the digital technologies curriculum across the primary years. Emphasis is placed on empowering pre-service teachers to design opportunities for children to become innovative creators of digital solutions, effective users of digital systems and critical consumers of information conveyed by digital systems. Pre-service teachers will design learning challenges which foster children's curiosity, confidence, persistence, innovation, creativity, respect and cooperation. The topic explores the underpinning content knowledge associated with the components of digital systems (hardware, software and networks) and how data are represented and structured symbolically for use by digital systems. The processes and production skills required to create digital solutions to problems and opportunities are also examined which include the skills in using digital systems; critical and creative thinking including systems, design and computational thinking.
learning_outcomes: Apply strategies to evidence, assess and enhance your impact on student learning in Digital Technologies

Critically evaluate resources to support teaching of the Digital Technologies subject considering their relevance, accessibility, teacher support, and suitability for diverse learners and instructional contexts
Discuss disciplinary knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge related to the Australian Curriculum: Digital Technologies
Plan a digital technologies lesson that integrates pedagogical reasoning and disciplinary knowledge, ensuring alignment with curriculum objectives, student needs, and effective teaching strategies
prerequisites: 9 units of EDUC topics

title: Respectful Teaching with Infants and Toddlers
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide pre-service teachers with an opportunity to question the purposes and possibilities of responsive and respectful teaching with very young children Support pre-service teachers to consider how to observe for, shape and implement a high-quality curriculum for infants and toddlers Enable pre-service teachers to critically examine the role of the teacher in the birth-3 learning space and connect this to their teaching philosophy Provide pre-service teachers with opportunities to apply their developing knowledge and understanding of infant-toddler curricula by planning, conducting and evaluating an inquiry

Focusing on the role that attachment and attunement play in early learning and development, this topic encourages pre-service teachers to explore contemporary and international perspectives on the foundational elements of high-quality curricula for very young children. Pre-service teachers will investigate approaches to responsive teaching and consider what very young children do as they relate to and seek to discover more about the people and the world around them. The reciprocal nature of the educator-child relationship will be of key consideration, using observation, reflection and planning techniques to question: what does it mean to teach infants and toddlers? Pre-service teachers will have the opportunity to study first-hand how to shape engaging and supportive educative care programs for very young children as they engage in Professional Experience Placement and implement an inquiry project.
learning_outcomes: Develop greater awareness of contemporary perspectives of high-quality curricula in birth-to-three learning environments noting parallels with responsive and respectful teaching practice
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the teachers’ role in very young children’s learning and development articulating personal teaching perspectives on this
Critically analyse and effectively respond to the socio-emotional, intellectual and physical needs, creativities and curiosities of infants and toddlers
Articulate professional learning needs to provide engaging and supportive educative care programs for very young children
Plan, implement, and reflect on an inquiry that is informed by children’s familial, cultural, and community contexts
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1221 and EDUC1242

title: Meaning Making Through Play and Development
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Plan opportunities for children to express themselves by designing and creating age-appropriate, multimodal opportunities using a range of resources Understand and value the knowledge that children bring to their educational context, valuing their funds of knowledge Explore pedagogical approaches to curriculum planning, evolving from children’s interests Experience a range of meaning making processes and how these would support children to make sense of the world

Children make sense of the world through play, development and meaning making practices. This topic focuses on how children learn, by valuing their competencies and building on their prior knowledge. Pre-service teachers will explore a range of approaches to develop and support creativity through different modalities, and how these resources can create opportunities for young children to communicate their knowledge and understanding as they make meaning of their world. Pre-service teachers will explore how to facilitate playful meaning making experiences that support children’s learning and development in the early years.
learning_outcomes: Examine how educators can support and encourage children’s multimodal creative expression through emergent teaching and learning
Assess how children represent their thinking and communicate their ideas, considering a diverse range of learners and culturally sensitive modes of communication
Plan opportunities for children to make sense of the world through a range of emergent meaning-making practices that support their play and development
Discuss how children develop their understanding of the world through meaning-making processes
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC1221, EDUC2321, EDUC1242, EDUC1246

title: Early Numeracy Birth-3 Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce contemporary theory on infant and toddler mathematical learning, including the role of language in developing mathematical concepts. Understand the role of early mathematical learning in the context of mathematical learning in later years, both prior to school and school. Introduce a range of resources and approaches to planning and designing learning environments that support infants and toddlers to access and develop fundamental concepts and ways of thinking mathematically.

This topic draws from contemporary research and examines infant and toddlers’ engagement with mathematics when exploring and making sense of their world. It introduces pre-service teachers to the mathematical capabilities of infants and toddlers, and the specific role language plays in infant and toddler’s development of fundamental concepts and ways of thinking that support later mathematical learning. Pre-service teachers will develop knowledge of how infant and toddlers learn, and the ways that this learning can be supported pedagogically, including planning for loose parts play.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate strategies, including analytical and observational skills, to assess and promote young children's mathematical growth, and articulate ways to further develop mathematical content knowledge through ongoing professional learning
Plan for a variety of opportunities that will support infants and toddlers to access and develop fundamental concepts and ways of thinking mathematically

Evaluate, investigate and apply contemporary research knowledge to knowing and understanding the purpose for developing infant and toddlers’ foundational mathematics concepts and ways of thinking mathematically, and the relationships between this and a child’s overall development
Demonstrate ways of reflecting on and communicating knowledge of infant and toddler mathematical learning and meaning-making and ways to support that learning to a wider audience
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1221, EDUC1242

title: Early Literacy Birth-3 Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Work with pre-service teachers to examine early literacy milestones from birth to three including motor, social, morphological, and phonological capacities in pre-language, language onset and language growth. Assist pre-service teachers to broaden knowledge and understanding of theoretical perspectives on play, cognition, and early literacy. Examine appropriate teaching and scaffolding skills that support early literacy milestones and behaviours. Advocate for young children as agents of their own learning to build interest and engagement in literacy activities as they transition to preschool with inquiry led, dialogic and interactive literacy learning. Explore and discuss the vital role that families and communities play in building successful literacy environments that link home and early childhood settings.

This topic invites pre-service teachers to explore and understand early literacy milestones and use that knowledge to consider and plan appropriate strategies that foster this development and afford young children rich language and literacy learning opportunities. Pre-service teachers will demonstrate understanding and application of evidence play- based learning in literacy development for babies, toddlers and young children and explore the profound significance that families make to foundational literacy within a range of sociocultural and cognitive contexts.
learning_outcomes: Identify how to empower family, peers, and other significant members and how they may contribute to young children's awareness and immersion in key literacy concepts
Design and develop physical and culturally appropriate environments for birth to 3 using knowledge of early literacy milestones
Apply an understanding of evidence based theoretical perspectives on play and cognition for early literacy development and experiences
Articulate an understanding of the educator's role in observing, planning, and assessing young children as agents of their own literacy learning and development
Respond to teaching and scaffolding skills that tune in to young children’s receptive and expressive language, movement, and motor skills to create quality literacy rich environments
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC1230, EDUC1221, EDUC1242

title: The Expressive Arts in Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
That pre-service teachers: Will develop an understanding of the role of creative expression in society Are introduced to a variety of relevant and innovative teaching methodologies and resources Recognise the importance of classroom organisation and materials management Demonstrate an ability to use inclusive teaching practices when planning for teaching and learning in the expressive arts

Through an integrated teaching approach this topic introduces an understanding of the role of creative expression in society. Creative development is linked to theories of child development and to the importance of providing every child with the opportunity to practice and develop in creative expression. The themes of analysis, response and practice are explored in relation to the different forms of creative expression and in different cultural and vocational contexts. Students are introduced to a variety of appropriate teaching methodologies and resources, the importance of classroom organisation and materials management, the use of information and communication technologies and to necessary practical skills for teaching in the areas of the expressive arts. Current curriculum frameworks are used for planning for learning, and students address long-term planning for teaching encompassing rich, integrated learning, inclusive teaching practices, and the embedded use of information and computer technology.
learning_outcomes: Developed resources and a range of methodologies and skills for teaching the expressive arts
Demonstrated an ability to use inclusive teaching practices when planning for teaching and learning in the expressive arts
Demonstrated an ability to plan for effective and developmentally appropriate teaching in the expressive arts
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into MTEC-Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) 1b Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1c Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education 1d Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1e Admission into BISEEC-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e))

title: Professional Experience: Year 2A (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Understand the complex work of the teacher Observe and learn from practising teachers how to effectively interact with children Undertake some of the tasks of the teacher under the supervision and direction of a practicing teacher

This topic helps to prepare students for entry into the teaching profession. Students will be placed for three one-week blocks or a minimum of 75 hours during their second year professional experiences. They will observe and work alongside registered teachers.
learning_outcomes: Interact with children as a beginning professional
Undertake some supportive tasks by working alongside a teacher at their direction
Describe the complex work and roles of the teacher by observing practising teachers at work
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1226 - Professional Experience: Year 1 (Primary) 2 EDUC1222 - Reading, Comprehending and Producing Multimodal Texts 2a EDUC1224 - Foundations of Special and Inclusive Education Must Satisfy: (1 and (2 or 2a))

title: Professional Experience: Year 2A (Early Childhood)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Make a meaningful contribution to childrens' learning and the placement settings curriculum priorities Test and use student theoretical knowledge, particularly in relation to the expressive arts and childrens literacy and numeracy learning and development Interact with individual children and small groups of children and as a contributing member of an educational team Use a variety of observation techniques and a modified version of the Leuven Involvement Scale to gain insight into the types of experiences, activities and ideas that engage young children Plan, implement and evaluate experiences/activities designed to extend childrens development in the arts and literacy and numeracy Reflect on the broader context of early childhood practice Gather evidence of their developing professional knowledge, professional practice and professional relationships

This topic helps to prepare students for entry into the teaching profession. The lectures develop students observation and planning skills. Students will be placed in an early childhood setting and they will observe and work alongside registered teachers.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of the factors that lead to high levels of involvement and engagement in curriculum experiences/activities
Become competent observers of childrens learning and development
Demonstrate the ability to plan, implement and evaluate experiences/activities that are responsive to the observed needs and interests of young children
Interact as a professional educator in an early childhood setting

Demonstrate awareness of the broader aspects of the early childhood learning environment, including an understanding of the environment as the third teacher, the importance of relationships, working with families and organizing for learning
Interact with individual children and groups of children as a pre-service teacher
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1225 - Professional Experience: Year 1 (Early Childhood) 2 EDUC1221 - Approaches to Play and Learning (Professional Experience: Year 1A) Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Professional Experience: Year 2A (Middle and Secondary Schooling)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide pre-service teachers with experiences that enable them to: Understand the complex roles and responsibilities of teachers Observe and learn how to effectively communicate, interact and work alongside school students and school staff Consider how staff/student relationships influence ways of student learning, being, engaging and participating at school Under supervision, assume some of the roles and responsibilities of classroom teachers Behave collaboratively and effectively with all members of the school community Make a valuable contribution to a recognised learning program within the school Evaluate their readiness and commitment for a career in teaching

During this professional experience pre-service teachers observe and experience some of the key roles of teachers. They engage with and contribute to supervised learning programs and, analyse, review and determine their commitment and preparedness for this career. Before, during and after placement students participate in a series of constructively aligned assessment tasks to plan personalised learning goals for future placements.
learning_outcomes: Implement a variety of teaching strategies and resources
Record, analyse, review and plan learning goals for future professional experiences
Define ways schools provide social, emotional and academic opportunities for school students to improve learning and engagement
Articulate how student characteristics may influence their learning
Assume some teaching responsibilities such as planning a lesson, facilitating group work and assisting individual students in recognised learning programs
Devise some effective ways of supporting engagement in learning
Understand how relational ways of being influence teachers' and students' capacity to learn, participate and belong
Articulate their understandings of the complex work and roles teachers and other school staff
Communicate effectively with all members of the school community
Determine whether this is a good career choice for them
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1227 - Professional Experience: Year 1 (Middle and Secondary Schooling) 2 EDUC1223 - Middle Schooling Philosophy and Pedagogy 2a EDUC1224 - Foundations of Special and Inclusive Education 3 18 units of study Must Satisfy: (1 and (2 or 2a) and 3)

title: Pedagogies of Belonging
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Provide pre-service teachers with opportunities to expand their knowledge and understanding of the cultures and social relationships within which infants, toddlers and young children live and learn Enable pre-service teachers to question dominant discourses of childhood (including common pedagogical strategies) to deepen their understanding of the particular social and emotional rights and needs of infants, toddlers, and young children.This includes understandings of ‘belonging’, ‘wellbeing’ and ‘social and emotional learning.’ Challenge pre-service teachers to become critically aware of their own social and cultural background, and how this will shape their role and actions as an educator Provide pre-service teachers with the skills and expertise to evaluate available resources and approaches designed to maximise children's engagement as learners, and to use this expertise to create responsive and effective teaching and learning environments

This topic presents a comprehensive picture of the lives of young children, and in particular how these lives are embedded within a social and emotional context. Pre- service teachers will be expected to become familiar with different constructions of the child, drawing on theoretical perspectives from sociology, psychology and childhood studies. Critically analysing this material, they will learn how to guide young children’s learning, from infancy through to middle childhood, and do so with sensitivity to the familial, cultural, and linguistic context which shapes such learning. Drawing on their own research and inquiry processes, pre-service teachers will develop a complex understanding of what motivates children’s learning, their rights, and needs, and their reactions to that learning, such as difficult behaviours. Based on this expertise, they will evaluate how best to plan, assess, and document children’s activities, and manage children’s behaviour with respect, compassion, and thoughtfulness.
learning_outcomes: Identify the many changes in children's most significant relationships (both within and beyond the family) during the early years, and how to creatively and appropriately respond to these changes in the planning and evaluation process

Determine your role, as an educator, in young children's social and emotional learning, including how best to respond to different needs and responses and articulating their own responses to children’s needs and behaviours

Articulate a complex account of children's engagement and motivation, using theoretical knowledge and understandings of class, gender and culture to explain the divergent dispositions and behaviours of young children

Reflect upon the historical and cultural construction of childhood, and develop a sophisticated understanding of how the theoretical and practical work of early childhood educators is shaped accordingly
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1a Admission into BISEEC-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) 1b Admission into BECEB-Bachelor of Early Childhood - Birth to 5 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b)

title: Planning and Assessment for Arts Media
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide pre‐service teachers with opportunities to explore a variety of visual arts media in their own artmaking Develop pre‐service teachers’ expertise to design Arts curriculum relevant to the Primary Years which explores a range of media Develop pre‐service teachers’ capacity to analyse the use of chosen media and explain the rationale for their approach

In this topic, pre‐service teachers will critically explore a range of traditional and contemporary visual arts media. They will develop the capacity to plan for and assess learning in a variety of media.
learning_outcomes: Appraise your arts intentions and choices of media
Develop creative works using a range of visual arts media
Plan learning and assessment activities in the Arts curriculum for the Primary Years which explores a range of media
prerequisites: 1 1 of VISA1401 2 1 of VISA1402, DRAM1002 Must Satisfy: (1) and (2)

title: Primary Mathematics Curriculum Studies 1
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Develop a philosophy of teaching and learning mathematics. Support pre-service teachers' in their understanding of how to develop children and young people’s understanding of number and algebra through investigation and problem-solving. Equip pre-service teachers with the knowledge of what to teach in number and algebra to ensure children and young people’s progression.

This topic seeks to teach pre-service teachers about how the study of number and algebra complement each other and how these core understandings support children’s investigation and problem-solving. Children and young people’s understanding of number and algebra is significant for learning and progress in mathematics and will be explored through the use of the proficiency strands of the Australian Curriculum, understanding, fluency, problem-solving and reasoning. Children and young people further develop their understanding of number through opportunities to explore mathematical ideas and apply number and algebra skills. Pre-service teachers will learn about effective pedagogies which promote the engagement and participation of children and young people in mathematics in educational settings.
learning_outcomes: Evidence their own working knowledge of number and algebra
Demonstrate a working knowledge of what to teach in number and algebra aligned with relevant curricula of primary educational settings
Articulate a philosophy of teaching and learning mathematics
Articulate an understanding of approaches which support children and young people’s capacity in applying their developing knowledge of number and algebra
prerequisites: 18 units of EDUC topics

title: Relational Pedagogies in Learning Spaces and Places of Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Examine the way the image of the child in Early Childhood Education has been constructed and reconstructed over time, toward a current view of the rights-bearing, capable child and children’s agency Explore the depth of relationships that are important to a child as a family member and a community participant and analyse the place of families and educators Enrich pre-service teachers’ understanding of learning and teaching in early childhood as relational and connected to the whole child, their social and emotional well-being, and their environment Enable pre-service teachers to recognise a variety of strategies and possible responses for building effective pedagogical practices and managing children’s behaviour Organise and construct programming and planning for effective teaching and learning during the Professional Experience placement, and summarise how to make an effective contribution to children’s learning through a curriculum inquiry

This topic explores effective pedagogical practices and appropriate classroom management approaches in early childhood, paying attention to the fact that children’s development, learning and well-being all emerge within a social context. The child as a capable individual, family member, and community participant is centred. Respectful pedagogies are developed that pay attention to children’s agency and rights as well as the need to connect. This topic includes professional experience placement, and pre-service teachers are familiarised with specific instructions and placement expectations by engaging with self-study learning modules online.
learning_outcomes: Examine learning and teaching through relationships to “place” and recognise a shared, legal and ethical responsibility for learning spaces, resources and community life
Plan, practice and document with a premise that a child is capable, agentic, and possesses rights, taking into consideration developmental and sociocultural perspectives
Demonstrate competency in planning for teaching and learning that is informed by effective pedagogical practices and classroom management
Understand the need for deep listening to children and families to develop pedagogical practice that is grounded in ethics, equity, and cultural competence
Evidence an array of assessment strategies used to plan, prepare and implement learning experiences for young children with support and guidance from the mentor teacher
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1221, EDUC1242

title: Science - Constructing a Future World
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enhance confidence, knowledge, and skills of pre‐service teachers in Physical and Chemical Sciences with a strong ICT perspective and supported by inter‐curriculum links where appropriate Promote skills of pre‐service teachers in using systems thinking for developing a series of learning experiences, units, and cross‐site/school plans and development for leading a site/school approach Develop the critical analysis skills of pre‐service teachers in evaluating case studies by peers and considering teaching construction (engineering) in a future world with various materials and exploring ways of moving

This topic provides a detailed look at how a design process of discovery can be purposefully integrated with scientific innovation and entrepreneurial thinking. Building on everyday science knowledge, play and inquiry processes are used to create solutions underpinned by scientific concepts that help to build a future world. Through a focused look at integrating Chemical and Physical Sciences curriculum content with the skills of inquiry and design, supported by General Capabilities including ICT; this topic looks at the strong links between environmental and manufactured objects and materials. Focusing on the processes and production skills of construction, this topic provides inter‐curricular teaching strategies for innovating and building a future world. This topic will highlight the ways children discover when thinking with real‐world problems seeking innovative solutions, both intentional and incidental. Supported by English and Technologies curricula, this topic will demonstrate methods commonly used in science can be analysed for enhancing opportunities across age groups and site/schools.
learning_outcomes: Plan for professional learning needs surrounding science learning and teaching practices, including leadership perspectives
Create and document prototype designs with everyday materials
Discuss how the movement of objects varies, can produce light, heat, and sound, and moves through forces and electrical energies
Explore the roles of resources and tools for building with a range of materials through constructive practices to demonstrate movement and force
Examine the range of age‐appropriate skills and curriculum General Capabilities relevant to science learning
Design a series of learning experiences which challenge children to solve real‐world problems and share with peers for feedback
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1240, EDUC1241

title: Teaching Communication for Learners with Communication Access Needs
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Investigate the characteristics of students with complex communication needs and explore considerations for assessment and instruction Prepare preservice teachers in the process of assessing functional communication Develop understanding of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) modes and innovative strategies for teaching and learning Facilitate knowledge and application of innovative communication technologies for diverse learners who have complex communication needs
