This topic is focussed on teaching to support the communication and learning of persons with complex communication needs who have intellectual and developmental disabilities. The topic explores assessment and approaches that can be conducted in educational settings and focuses on functional communication, naturalistic teaching, and implementing augmentative and alternative communication systems.
learning_outcomes: Develop an implementation plan to teach the use of an augmentative and alternative communication system
Identify the communication characteristics of learners with complex communication needs and their implications for teaching diverse learners
Analyse assessment data to identify communication goals for teaching
Implement targeted communication programs that reflect contemporary, research‐informed instructional strategies
Appraise modes of augmentative and alternative communication and systems including innovative technologies for inclusive education
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC1221, EDUC1223, EDUC1237

title: Teaching in and Through the Expressive Arts
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
That pre-service teachers will: develop an in-depth understanding of the role of the arts in education as a learning area in its own right, and an approach to explore and demonstrate broader understanding explore and apply current approaches to teaching and learning in and through the arts Develop the ability to use inclusive teaching practices, methodologies, and resources to plan for teaching and learning in the arts

Through an integrated approach this topic introduces the role of creative expression and arts-based pedagogy in education and society. The themes of making and responding through various viewpoints are explored in relation to different cultural and vocational contexts. Pre-service teachers (PSTs) apply and critique a variety of teaching methodologies and resources as they develop necessary practical skills for teaching in and through the five arts subjects; Dance, Drama, Music, Media Arts, and Visual Arts. This topic gives PSTs the opportunity to plan and prepare for teaching in and through the arts supported by artists and teachers.
learning_outcomes: Examine their own development through reflective practice to refine skills for teaching and learning in and through the arts to meet evolving educational needs
Implement embodied learning approaches within and beyond the expressive arts to foster holistic development and engagement in learning
Appraise and implement authentic arts resources to plan for learning in and through the arts
Apply recent developments in arts education to integrate arts-based pedagogy across disciplines, leveraging artistic practices to engage students and deepen understanding

title: Teaching Students with Learning Disabilities
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Explore the construct of learning disabilities and Multitiered Systems of Support in relation to effective planning and teaching for students with learning disabilities (SWLD) Introduce preservice teachers to complex connections between academic learning, behaviour, student‐teacher relationships and the educational environment Examine the role of disability legislation, inclusive policies, instructional practices and learning environments in promoting academic success and emotional wellbeing for students with learning disabilities Explore research informed perspectives related to high‐quality schooling for students with learning disabilities

This topic explores school frameworks, interventions and pedagogies aimed at providing inclusive and supportive education for students with learning disabilities. Preservice teachers examine the characteristics of learning disabilities and explore environmental and internal factors that influence learner success in education settings. Theories and practices that address effective school‐wide processes and supports are studied and applied to the Australian context. There is a focus on the promotion of equitable curriculum participation, academic learning and emotional wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Integrate knowledge of learning disabilities, educational supports, research‐informed teaching practices, and legislative requirements into a holistic understanding of high‐quality education for SWLD
Illustrate ways an individual’s academic, behaviour and emotional needs are considered in the design and implementation of a Multitiered Systems of Support framework
Appraise data to solve problems and make well‐reasoned judgments related to effective school processes and productive learning environments for students with learning disabilities
Prioritise with justification, instructional approaches, supports and services to ensure students with learning disabilities are appropriately challenged and supported
Discuss learning disabilities in the Australian education context with a focus on typical characteristics of learners with learning disabilities
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC1120, EDUC1221, EDUC1236

title: Evidence-Based Practices for Autism
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
Develop professional competence in teaching students on the autism spectrum using evidence-based practices (EBPs). Pre-service teacher will reflect on their learning to support autistic students.

This topic examines autism, elucidating characteristics, support needs and teaching implications. The use of evidence-based practices is a focus of this topic. The primary emphasis will be on effective and efficient classroom structure that promote comprehension for students on the spectrum. The importance of rules and routines, skill building plans and reinforcement will be taught so that pre-service teachers understand that environmental antecedents have a significant impact on learning for autistic students. Finally, the importance of evidence-based practices taught as instructional pedagogies that work effectively. The overarching framework for these instructional methods will be housed under a Tier 1 academic Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS).
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of evidence-based practices (EBPs) to develop instructional structures to teach autistic students

Create and enact instructional plans based on selected evidence-based practices (EBPs): Visual Supports (VS), Video Modelling (VM), Exercise (ECE) and incorporate supports plans with the use of Comprehensive Autism planning system (CAPS)
Analyse current research and legislative requirements to cultivate inclusive classrooms
Focus on structure, rules and routines, skill building, reinforcement and instructional plans for effective programming
Design classrooms based on principles of TEACCH Program

title: Critical Indigenous Pedagogy
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop An understanding of the diversity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander schooling experiences and Australian education from an Indigenous perspective A critical understanding of the issues in, and models of, contemporary Indigenous Australian education and policy An awareness of the power relations inherent in the historical constructions of ‘race’, racism, representation and identity and how this impacts on contemporary education policy A respect for the histories, cultures and perspectives of Indigenous communities Culturally sensitive and inclusive pedagogy demonstrating skills and knowledge in order for them to become an effective teacher of Indigenous students Students’ ability to research and communicate effectively to articulate their understanding of Indigenous issues and debates culture.

This topic examines the historical context of Indigenous Australian education to understand contemporary and diverse educational experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, families, and communities. Teachers who understand Indigenous perspectives on Australian history, the construction of 'Race' as an oppressive lens and education as a system of power that underpins Australian society are more equipped to meet all students' educational needs. The topic explores current theoretical frameworks and teaching practice in Australia, through inter-disciplinary and Indigenous knowledge systems. Students will develop a deeper understanding of the complexities Indigenous peoples experience in the Australian education system. The topic will assist students to make an ongoing commitment to becoming a critical, reflexive and more effective teacher of Indigenous students.
learning_outcomes: Identify, develop, and implement critical Indigenous pedagogical approaches supportive of Indigenous and non-Indigenous children and young people
Investigate and reflect on how race relations in Australia informs your own positioning and how these ideas shape knowledge of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Select, understand and critically analyse resources for implementation within relevant curriculum frameworks
Implement skills in working collaboratively
prerequisites: 18 units of EDUC topics

title: Literacy and Numeracy: Birth-4
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students with opportunities to broaden and deepen their knowledge and understanding of the ways infants, toddlers and young children engage with their worlds through play, moving and doing Help students to acquire questions, concepts, perspectives and strategies which will assist them in understanding and enhancing the literacy and numeracy learning of infants, toddlers and young children Support students to reflect upon contemporary discourse and research in order to consider their particular approach to providing literacy and numeracy learning opportunities in the early years

This topic enables students to examine the ways that infants and young children contribute to their social worlds as active participants in the interactions, language, ways of thinking, playing, and solving problems that form the basis of early literacy and numeracy competence. Through the inquiry processes used in this topic, student teachers explore the interrelationship between perceptual, sensory and language communicative capabilities of infants, toddlers and young children and examine the changes that occur as infants interact with others and develop complex communication skills. Students study the beginnings of abstract and symbolic thought in young children's play. The topic considers how families and educators and communities can identify and extend children's learning and development of key literacy & numeracy concepts. The topic draws from a multi-disciplinary knowledge base that includes child development, sociology and curriculum theory and research to consider how young children's acquisition of literacy and numeracy skills can be enhanced in early childhood professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Outline how family members, peers and other significant members in children's lives contribute to young children's awareness and immersion in key literacy & numeracy concepts
Explain how early literacy and numeracy concepts are socially situated
Demonstrate an understanding of the educator's role in observing and planning for young children's literacy and numeracy learning and development
Describe the influence of perceptual-sensorial, memory, representational-symbolic and communicative-linguistic thinking on young children's literary and numerical learning & development
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1120 - Teaching and Educational Contexts 1a EDUC1101 - Key Educational Ideas 1b Admission into MTEC-Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b))

title: Students with Literacy Difficulties
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
Through engaging in this topic participants will: Be aware of current literacy research focused on students with learning difficulties Understand how selection and interpretation of literacy assessments can inform program planning Develop knowledge and skills about how literacy intervention programs for students with learning difficulties may be implemented

This topic is designed to provide pre-service teachers with the opportunity to understand approaches to supporting students with literacy difficulties. There will be a focus on theories of literacy acquisition, factors that may influence literacy learning, and teaching and learning approaches.
learning_outcomes: Identify strategies to assess and plan for literacy improvement
Compare major theories of literacy acquisition
Explain the key skills and knowledge necessary for development of literacy in diverse learning areas
Plan lessons that meet the diverse literacy learning needs of students in different learning areas
Compare instructional approaches supported by evidence-informed research
prerequisites: EDUC1224 - Foundations of Special and Inclusive Education

title: Professional Experience: Year 2B (Early Childhood)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Make a meaningful contribution to childrens learning and the settings curriculum priorities Test and use their theoretical knowledge, particularly in relation to the expressive arts and childrens literacy and numeracy learning and development Interact with individual children and small groups of children and as a contributing member of an educational team Use a variety of observation techniques and a modified version of the Leuven Involvement Scale to gain insight into the types of experiences, activities and ideas that engage young children Plan, implement and evaluate experiences/activities designed to extend childrens development in the arts and literacy and numeracy Reflect on the broader context of early childhood practice Gather evidence of their developing professional knowledge, professional practice and professional relationships

This topic helps to prepare students for entry into the teaching profession. They will observe and work alongside registered teachers.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness of the factors that lead to high levels of involvement and engagement in curriculum experiences/activities

Demonstrate awareness of the broader aspects of the early childhood learning environment, including an understanding of the environment as the third teacher, the importance of relationships, working with families and organizing for learning
Demonstrate competent observing of childrens learning and development
Interact as a professional educator in an early childhood setting
Plan, implement and evaluate experiences/activities that are responsive to the observed needs and interests of young children
Interact with individual children and groups of children as a pre-service teacher
prerequisites: ^ EDUC2324 - Professional Experience: Year 2A (Early Childhood) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Professional Experience: Year 2B (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Understand the complex work of the teacher Observe and learn from practising teachers how to effectively interact with children Undertake some of the tasks of the teacher under the supervision and direction of a practicing teacher

This topic helps to prepare students for entry into the teaching profession. They will observe and work alongside registered teachers.
learning_outcomes: Describe the complex work and roles of the teacher by observing practising teachers at work
Undertake some supportive tasks by working alongside a teacher at their direction
Interact with children as a beginning professional
prerequisites: ^ EDUC2325 - Professional Experience: Year 2A (Primary) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Professional Experience: Year 2B (Middle and Secondary Schooling)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide pre-service teachers with experiences that enable them to : Understand the complex roles and responsibilities of teachers Observe and learn how to effectively communicate, interact and work alongside school students and school staff Consider how staff/student relationships influence ways of student learning, being, engaging and participating at school Under supervision, assume some of the roles and responsibilities of classroom teachers Behave collaboratively and effectively with all members of the school community Make a valuable contribution to a recognised learning program within the school Evaluate their readiness and commitment for a career in teaching

During this professional experience pre-service teachers observe and experience some of the key roles of teachers. They engage with and contribute to supervised learning programs and, analyse, review and determine their commitment and preparedness for this career. Before, during and after placement students participate in a series of constructively aligned assessment tasks to plan personalised learning goals for future placements.
learning_outcomes: Devise some effective ways of supporting engagement in learning
Assume some teaching responsibilities such as planning a lesson, facilitating group work and assisting individual students in recognised learning programs
Determine whether this is a good career choice for them
Record, analyse, review and plan learning goals for future professional experiences
Define ways schools provide social, emotional and academic opportunities for school students to improve learning and engagement
Understand how relational ways of being influence teachers' and students' capacity to learn, participate and belong
Articulate how student characteristics may influence their learning
Implement a variety of teaching strategies and resources
Communicate effectively with all members of the school community
Articulate their understandings of the complex work and roles teachers and other school staff
prerequisites: ^ EDUC2326 - Professional Experience: Year 2A (Middle and Secondary Schooling) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: HASS - Humanities and Social Sciences (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce students to the contestable nature of both History and Geography and its representations in the Australian Curriculum Explore the relationships of people with natural and built environments Engage with some key pedagogical approaches such as inquiry and problem based learning, that encourage school students to engage critically with information Collaboratively develop lesson plans drawing on Australian Curriculum content in History and Geography Develop an understanding of the different tools for assessing learning in History and Geography

This topic introduces students to the Australian Curriculum areas of History and Geography, commonly referred to as HASS. Students will reflect on the contested nature of history and geography from individual through to global perspectives. Inquiry and critical literacy skills of analysis, interpretation and evaluation will be fostered in developing personal stances and content knowledge for application in classroom settings. Pedagogical skills such as lesson planning, evaluation of resources, assessment tools and the embedded use of technology will be applied, and the inquiry-based approach of the International Baccalaureate will also be considered.
learning_outcomes: Analyse texts, resources and teaching strategies to explain and provide examples of the contestable nature of history and geography
Create relevant and engaging lesson plans for teaching a contemporary Historical or Geographical issue using the Australian Curriculum for guidance
Work collaboratively to achieve a common purpose through group discussions and presentations
Plan to assess and record student learning and use this data for exploring reporting strategies and approaches
Curate a range of resources and pedagogical strategies to effectively plan for teaching HASS in the primary years of schooling

title: Professional Experience 1: Relationships for Learning
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide pre-service teachers with the skills to personalise, adapt, and adjust materials and instructional variables in order to meet the needs of diverse children and young people.

This topic provides an overview of contemporary approaches to the development of positive learning environments. It clarifies the origins of behaviour and the diverse approaches to developing productive student behaviours. Positive approaches to behaviour prevention are articulated and examined alongside necessary behaviour interventions, each connected to overarching theory. The topic explores whole school approaches to behaviour, with positive teacher-student relationships as a foundational requirement. Critique is applied to the evidence base and application of approaches within diverse, contemporary Australian schooling contexts. Pre-service teachers apply learning from topic into a 15-day placement.
learning_outcomes: Develop knowledge of school policies and practices in relation to children and young peoples' diversity and inclusion, by considering intervention service delivery models (PBIS and SE-Rtl) within a multi-tiered systems of support framework
Develop awareness of how research on social emotional learning and behaviour underpins positive learning environments and effective teaching.
Learn to interact professionally with children and young people, staff and parents/caregivers and contribute to the class and educational setting.
Observe and evaluate how teachers interact with and support children and young people with diverse needs
prerequisites: 1 2 of EDUC1232, EDUC1224 2 1 of EDUC1244 or EDUC1243 Must satisfy: ((1 and 2))

title: Foundational Reading in the Early Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Assist pre-service teachers to understand the precursors for literacy success including oral language, vocabulary and phonological awareness whilst creating opportunities for children to use and develop emergent literacy for real-life purposes. Examine multiliteracies to define literacy and reading in the preschool and explore positive dispositions towards literacy learning to assist children with transitioning to formal school instruction. Support pre-service teachers in identifying and articulating reading pedagogies that support rich early literacy knowledge and recentre play as the child’s work. Enable pre-service teachers to apply the EYLF and Australian Curriculum to plan for and assess children’s early reading including oral language and vocabulary, phonemic awareness, and comprehension skills. Build advocacy skills for the importance of home literacy environments that engage with early literacy and language development and emphasise the value of the preschool years in developing foundational literacy skills.

Contemporary research continually emphasises the pivotal role that early literacy experiences have on later reading success. Drawing on previous knowledge, this topic invites pre-service teachers to explore multiliteracy acquisition and the foundational knowledge and understanding that underpin this process to define literacy and reading in preschool. Using contemporary evidence-based research into precursors of literacy success, such as oral language, phonological awareness and literature rich environments, preservice teachers will analyse and respond to effective pedagogies that nurture and value children’s cognitive development to support early code-related skills and comprehension. Pre-service teachers explore the significant link that home, community, and culture play in the development of preschool language and literacy learning to empower families to build on existing knowledge.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and understand multiliteracies that define literacy and reading to incorporate both skills-based instruction and meaning making to ensure a child centred focus and smooth transition into formal school learning
Demonstrate understanding of precursors for literacy success e.g oral language, vocabulary and phonological awareness and their relationship to real-life purposeful emergent literacy

Research and apply theories and practices related to home literacy environments and use data and research to explore how partnerships with families and community support children’s early literacy development

Apply evidence-based literacy principles and practices for 3- 5 years using the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum to plan and develop activities which engage children and build on their strengths and interests in both a skill based and meaning making environment

Articulate your own literacy knowledge and attitudes on reading pedagogies that focus on both teacher and child as interactive storytellers and readers within play based and agency based rich literature environments
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1230, EDUC2206

title: Mathematics 3-5 Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop knowledge of mathematics concepts and ways of thinking mathematically that are relevant for mathematics learning in prior-to-school settings. Develop knowledge of contemporary research and theories on the ways that children aged 3-5 years learn mathematics. Understand the relationship between mathematical learning in the dual contexts of prior-to-school and school. Introduce a range of resources and pedagogical approaches creating playful environments that provide multiple opportunities for mathematics learning. Develop an understanding of assessing young children's mathematical learning in the context of prior-to-school settings (3-5 years).

This topic will develop pre-service teachers’ knowledge of contemporary research on young children’s mathematics learning and practice in the prior-to-school context. It introduces pre-service teachers to the mathematical capabilities of children aged 3-5 years, and the ways that prior-to-school environments can plan provide rich and meaningful opportunities for children to engage in mathematical play, and how teachers can extend mathematics learning through and intentional teaching.
learning_outcomes: Articulate, evaluate and apply contemporary research and theories as to how young children (3-5 years) learn mathematics, and key mathematics concepts and ways of thinking mathematically for children aged 3-5 years

Investigate and plan for environments that provide a range of resources that will introduce, extend or enrich young children's mathematical development, and know and understand how to use the environment to support playful and intentional mathematics learning and assessment
Evaluate mathematics learning in the context of a continuum that overlays prior to school and school curriculum, and demonstrate ways of promoting young children's mathematical growth
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC1238, EDUC2207

title: Thinking and Working Scientifically in the Early Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Promote pre-service teachers’ confidence, knowledge and skills in science learning and teaching Enable pre-service teachers to develop an appropriate program in science for children Enhance pre-service teachers’ personal approach to science teaching based on their critical analysis of practical experiences in light of theoretical perspectives

This topic provides opportunities for pre-service teachers to consider the place of science in their own lives as well as in the daily lives of young children. Using inquiry learning processes, pre-service teachers are supported to identify the early signs of children developing concepts, skills and positive attitudes towards science. To build on these observations, pre-service teachers are supported to plan, implement, and evaluate programs of intentional teaching in science with considerations for integration across other areas. The topic develops pre-service teachers' development of scientific literacy and content knowledge through science in the areas with considerations for integration. Drawing from their knowledge of the curriculum documents in early childhood, strong inter-curricular links with other learning areas are made through examining the role of science in children’s everyday lives, including the media and the history of science as a field of study.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a high-level scientific process skills, literacy and knowledge through modelling intentional inquiry and play-based learning strategies for science education development
Identify techniques to support children's increasing awareness of safety procedures related to science investigatory play
Plan a balanced, sequential unit of inquiry in science by drawing on appropriate government documents and exploring existing ideas through published sample
Critically assess personal attitudes towards science, its applications and how an individual’s scientific identity has been shaped by family and culture
Discuss how science may be integrated across the curriculum in ways which encourage children's curiosity, interest and play as they investigate both natural and built environments and materials
prerequisites: 1 2 of EDUC1221, EDUC1242 2 ^ EDUC2207 2a EDUC1238 Must Satisfy (1 and (2 or 2a)) ^= May be enrolled concurrently

title: Supporting Children on the Autism Spectrum in Early Childhood Settings
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop an understanding of characteristics of autism in young children Address key behaviours to teach for best possible developmental prognosis Facilitate comprehension of key evidence-based intervention models in autism intervention for children Develop skills in specific evidence-based teaching strategy

This topic will introduce pre-service teachers to autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Specifically, it will address autism in young children in early childhood settings. The focus would be on understanding autism in early years and assessment of autistic children. Key areas of difficulty for autistic children, specifically, joint attention, symbolic play and emotional regulation will be addressed. It will also introduce evidence-based intervention strategies within a multi-tiered system of supports framework, in inclusive early childhood settings. Finally, intervention programs for autistic children such as JASPER, SCERTS and the Denver Model will be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate leading models in autism intervention
Explore diagnostic criteria and assessment of autism
Select appropriate knowledge of evidence-based practice to plan for teaching young children on the autism spectrum
Analyse the importance of joint attention, symbolic play and emotional regulation in young children on the autistic spectrum
Synthesise characteristics of autism in young children
prerequisites: 72 Units of study

title: Professional Experience: Final Assessment for Registration (Birth-5)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Make a meaningful contribution to children's learning and curriculum goals using contemporary Australian and international research. Deepen understanding of child development through praxis, integrating theoretical knowledge into practice. Use a variety of observation techniques to identify experiences, activities and ideas that engage young children. Document children's involvement and engagement in the curriculum, assess their learning over an extended period of time, and engage with families and other professionals to support children’s learning journeys.

This topic involves a 6-week full-time placement (total 30 days), spent in a metropolitan or country early childhood setting. Emphasis is placed on the planning, implementation, and evaluation of teaching programs. Close links are established between curriculum studies at Flinders and centre curricula, with PSTs designing, evaluating, implementing, analysing and theorising about their placement site’s curriculum inquiry focus in light of contemporary Australian and international Early Childhood research and practice. At the conclusion of this teaching experience, judgements are made about the pre-service teacher’s readiness to be registered to teach in the early childhood teaching profession.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement, and evaluate responsive activities based on children's needs and interests
Apply theoretically informed teaching strategies, reflect on the impact and effectiveness of approaches, document learning effectively, and collaborate to achieve shared educational goals
Take an increasing degree of responsibility for planning, implementing, and evaluating a curriculum that engages individual children and groups of children in deep and meaningful learning
Competently observe children's learning and development
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC2204, EDUC2206, EDUC2207

title: Playing on Country
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Equip pre-service teachers with the knowledge and skills to design and implement safe and culturally appropriate teaching practices rooted in Indigenous pedagogies, particularly in outdoor play settings Encourage pre-service teachers to critically reflect on their cultural assumptions and biases, fostering self-awareness and sensitivity to Indigenous perspectives in educational contexts Prepare graduates to create inclusive learning environments by integrating Indigenous perspectives, promoting cultural responsiveness, and honouring diverse ways of knowing and learning Develop an understanding of how to teach Indigenous perspectives, and literacy and numeracy concepts, through outdoor play experiences

The topic will engage preservice teachers in the critical analysis of effective pedagogical practices for all children learning about First Nations People. Pre-service teachers will build on their existing understanding of literacy and numeracy education and develop intercultural understandings, to promote reconciliation and build capacity to teach Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories and cultures through play; as well as being confident and competent in working sensitively and culturally appropriately with Indigenous Australian children. They will develop a critical understanding of contemporary Indigenous education practices and policies and apply this to outdoor play and learning. Pre-service teachers will engage their developing indigenous pedagogies as they participate in a series of Bush Kindergarten sessions with pre-school children in context. Carrying out an indigenous inquiry into children’s literacy and numeracy learning on Country.
learning_outcomes: Proficiently design, implement, and evaluate safe, play-based learning experiences that align with contemporary theories of child development, integrating indigenous perspectives on nature and environment
Critically analyse and articulate the principles and practices of indigenous pedagogies, including their historical and cultural contexts, and apply this understanding to educational settings
Apply approaches to teaching literacy and numeracy concepts through Indigenous pedagogies in outdoor environments

Demonstrate the ability to critically reflect on their own cultural assumptions and biases, integrating indigenous perspectives into their professional practice and fostering culturally responsive and inclusive learning environments
prerequisites: EDUC2420

title: Foundations of Effective Writing Instruction
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre-service teachers’ deep understanding of how to facilitate writing instruction that meets the diverse needs of learners Enhance pre-service teachers’ analytical skills to evaluate written text samples and identify strengths and areas for improvement in student writing Develop pre-service teachers’ ability to integrate writing instruction across learning areas, promoting interdisciplinary learning and student engagement

This topic equips pre-service teachers with the foundational knowledge and practical skills necessary to facilitate effective writing instruction in primary education settings. The topic will deepen pre-service teachers’ understanding of the interdependence between writing, reading, and learning and develop their capacity to design effective writing instruction for children and young people with a range of abilities and backgrounds. Through a blend of theoretical exploration and practical application, pre-service teachers will examine writing instruction across all sub-elements of writing in the Australian Curriculum (Handwriting & Keyboarding, Spelling, Punctuation, Grammar, and Creating Texts). They will explore the essential components of effective writing, including word choice, sentence structure, and overall text coherence, and critically evaluate written text samples at multiple levels and engage in moderated assessments to assess proficiency. With a focus on fostering growth and improvement, pre-service teachers will learn to justify their assessments using meta-talk, engaging in constructive feedback to guide learners towards enhanced writing skills. Pre-service teachers will explore the intersection of instructional design and writing instruction, learning to create texts, generate or adapt instructional goals, plans, and resources tailored to specific writing genres, linguistic features, and curriculum levels.
learning_outcomes: Generate or Adapt instructional goals, plans, resources and multi-modal texts tailored to specific writing genres or linguistic features to develop writing based on an assessment, content area and/or curriculum level
Critique theoretical frameworks and evidence-informed instructional approaches for primary writing
Evaluate written text samples at word, sentence and whole text levels using provided criteria and moderate assessments
Justify evaluation of written text samples at word, sentence, and whole text levels by using meta-talk (talking about how you write) to provide constructive feedback
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC1222, EDUC1230

title: Primary Mathematics Curriculum Studies 2
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Prepare pre-service teachers to develop their own and primary aged children and young peoples' understanding and competence with measurement, geometry, probability, and statistics Interrogate the relevant F-6 curricula in measurement, space/geometry, probability, and statistics Develop knowledge about children and young peoples' emerging understanding, fluency, problem-solving and reasoning with mathematics and share ways in which children and young people’s thinking and competence can be developed through effective pedagogies Develop pre-service teachers who have comprehensive knowledge and skill in teaching, differentiating and adjust learning in mathematics for all children and young people. Equip pre-service teachers with the necessary professional knowledge and requirements to undertake professional experience in their third year. Prepare pre-service teachers to design and plan effective teaching, learning and assessment in mathematics.

This topic teaches pre-service teachers about foundational measurement concepts, geometric thinking probability and statistics and the ways they are connected. Understanding these mathematical concepts is explored using the proficiency strands of the Australian Curriculum, understanding, fluency, problem-solving and reasoning. Pre-service teachers will develop their own understanding and competence with mathematics and learn about effective pedagogies and assessment in primary school settings. This topic will also prepare pre-service teachers for their first block of sustained teaching practice in professional experience.
learning_outcomes: Determine how children and young people move from emergent to more proficient processes when working with measurement, geometry, probability, and statistics

Design a unit of work in measurement, geometry, probability, or statistics and appraise ways to differentiate and adjust learning for the engagement, participation, and progress of all children and young people
Appraise ways to differentiate and adjust learning for the engagement, participation, and progress of all children
Critique children and young people’s thinking and competence with measurement, geometry, probability, and statistics can be developed through effective pedagogies
Critique your working knowledge of measurement concepts, geometric thinking, probability concepts and statistical reasoning
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC1231, EDUC2333, EDUC2422

title: Language, Literature and Literacies 4-8
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Support students to develop a research-based approach to: Language development Literacy practices of children in home and community prior to and during the early years of schooling Introduce students to a wide variety of texts, resources and approaches designed to enhance literacy learning opportunities for young children Guide students as they develop an understanding of planning for and evaluating multiliteracy learning across the 4-8 childhood years

This topic introduces students to research based theory and practice in literacy education for children aged between 4-8 years. This will involve critical analysis of language and literacy learning from contemporary perspectives. Literacy is defined broadly as communities using speaking, listening, viewing, reading and writing to communicate and shape ideas and values. The topic focuses on the acquisition of multiliteracies in preschool through early years of school contexts and the major theoretical frameworks which influence teaching practices. Modules in the topic include: the link between oral and written language; the elements in a balanced literacy program; catering for individual needs; planning and assessing literacy learning and creating a supportive learning environment. The topic emphasises the significance of interaction with experienced users of language in supporting the language development of young children.
learning_outcomes: Use an inquiry approach to examine literacy practices of children in home and community, prior to and during the early years of schooling
Utilise a wide variety of resources, approaches and strategies to enhance literacy learning opportunities for young children
Select appropriate planning and evaluation tools to sustain, enhance and monitor young children's literacy learning, including those at educational risk
Articulate their own evolving theory of literacy learning, based on their knowledge of theory and practical experiences
Demonstrate their knowledge of oral language development and its relationship to literacy learning
prerequisites: EDUC2321 - The Expressive Arts in Early Childhood

title: Pedagogies of Belonging
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students with opportunities to expand their knowledge and understanding of the history, cultures and social relationships within which infants, toddlers and young children live and learn Enable students to question dominant discourses of childhood (including common pedagogical strategies) in order to deepen their understanding of the particular social and emotional rights and needs of infants, toddlers and young children Challenge students to become critically aware of their own social and cultural background, and how this will shape their role and actions as an educator Provide students with the skills and expertise to evaluate available resources and approaches designed to maximise children's engagement as learners, and to use this expertise to create responsive and effective teaching and learning environments

This topic presents a comprehensive picture of the lives of young children, and in particular how these lives are embedded within a social and emotional context. Students will be expected to become familiar with different constructions of the child, drawing on theoretical perspectives from sociology, psychology and childhood studies. Critically analysing this material, they will learn how to guide young children's learning, from infancy through to middle childhood, and do so with sensitivity to the familial, cultural and linguistic context which shapes such learning. Drawing on their own research and inquiry processes, students will develop a complex understanding of what motivates children's learning, their rights and needs, and also their reactions to that learning, such as difficult behaviours. Based on this expertise, they will evaluate how best to plan, assess and document children's activities, and manage children's behaviour with respect, compassion and thoughtfulness.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a complex account of children's engagement and motivation, using theoretical knowledge and understandings of class, gender and culture to explain the divergent dispositions and behaviours of young children
Reflect upon the historical and cultural construction of childhood, and develop a sophisticated understanding of how this shapes the theoretical and practical work of early childhood educators

Identify the many changes in children's most significant relationships (both within and beyond the family) during the early years, and develop creative ways of responding to these changes in the planning and evaluation process
Analyse and justify their role, as educators, in young children's social and emotional learning, and evaluate how best to respond to the different needs and responses they encounter
prerequisites: 1 4.5 units of Level 2 EDUC topics 1a Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1b Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b))

title: Expressive Arts Curriculum Studies: Visual Art, Drama, Media, Music and Dance
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
That pre-service teachers: Will develop an understanding of the role of creative expression in society Are introduced to a variety of relevant and innovative teaching methodologies and resources Develop the ability to use inclusive teaching practices when planning for teaching and learning in the expressive arts

Through an integrated teaching approach this topic introduces an understanding of the role of creative expression in society. Creative development is linked to theories of child development and to the importance of providing every child with the opportunity to practise and develop in creative expression. The themes of analysis, response and practice are explored in relation to the different forms of creative expression and in different cultural and vocational contexts. Students are introduced to a variety of appropriate teaching methodologies and resources, the importance of organisation and materials management in the learning environment, the use of information and communication technologies and to necessary practical skills for teaching in the areas of the expressive arts. Current curriculum frameworks are used for planning for learning, and students address long-term planning for teaching encompassing rich, integrated learning, inclusive teaching practices, and the embedded use of information and computer technology.
learning_outcomes: Develope resources and a range of methodologies and skills for teaching the expressive arts
Demonstrate an ability to use inclusive teaching practices when planning for teaching and learning in the expressive arts
Demonstrate an ability to plan for effective and developmentally appropriate teaching in the expressive arts
prerequisites: 1 Admission into MTPR-Master of Teaching (Primary) 1a Admission into BEDSEOS-Bachelor of Education (Special Education) 1b Admission into BEDPRSEBDS-B Education (Primary R-7 & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1c Admission into BEDPRBGSC-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of General Science 1d Admission into BEDPRBSE-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Special Education 1e Admission into BEDSTBDS-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Disability Studies 2 4.5 Units in level 2 EDUC topics Must Satisfy: (((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e)) or (2))

title: Health and Physical Education Curriculum Studies
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
To give students the opportunity to: Introduce pre‐service teachers to relevant curriculum frameworks and curriculum development processes for Health and Physical Education Enhance pre‐service teachers’ ability to articulate the evidence supporting their practice in Health and Physical Education and the rationale for their approach Develop pre‐service teachers’ capacity to deliver meaningful learning experiences in Health and Physical Education Enable pre-service teachers to critically analyse pedagogical practices in Health and Physical education

This topic addresses the preparation for teaching Health and Physical Education in primary educational settings. It encompasses the nature, rationale, aims, content, teaching methodology and pedagogical practices appropriate for this learning area.
learning_outcomes: Apply and evaluate a range of pedagogical practices to learning design within health and physical education
Confidently navigate and interpret curriculum policy and documents, to ensure learning experiences are aligned with relevant curriculum
Translate and organise health and physical education theory, concepts and content into effective learning and teaching experiences in the primary educational context
prerequisites: 22.5 units of EDUC topics

title: Literacies Across the Curriculum in the Middle and Secondary Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Understand some of the factors that impinge on teachers' work as literacy teachers (policy, place, student needs) Develop understandings, knowledge and skills appropriate for beginning middle and secondary schooling literacy teachers Develop a positive disposition toward literacy Understand the responsibilities associated with teaching literacy in the middle and secondary years in content area classrooms

This topic supports pre-service teachers to think about their role as a literacy teacher. The topic begins with a focus on how socio-cultural background shapes students' textual practices. Preservice teachers will then consider place-based educational considerations and definitions of literacy. Against this background, pre-service teachers will examine their responsibility to teach literacy in their specialist teaching areas. Current frameworks for thinking about literacy will be introduced, and classroom strategies which support student learning will be explored.
learning_outcomes: Understand that a text is influenced by who wrote it; when, where and under what circumstances it was written; its intended audience and purpose: these are contextual understandings
Understand a range of currently held views about literacy learning and teaching and how they influence classroom decision making
Articulate an informed and defensible personal view of literacy so that they can interrogate their classroom practice for consistency with this view
Understand a range of teaching strategies that support students' literacy development and be able to use these strategies effectively
Embed literacy teaching in their teaching content areas
Develop their own language proficiency and literacy competence to the point where they can confidently teach students and use metalanguage that is clear and precise
Know the language structures and features of different text types, why they are significant, and ways of teaching them in classrooms
Build a familiarity with a range of written, oral and visual texts, be able to select appropriate texts and ways of dealing with texts for middle school students
prerequisites: 1 9 units of Level 2 EDUC topics 2 Admission into MTS-Master of Teaching (Secondary) 2a Admission into BSCMTS-Bachelor of Science, Master of Teaching (Secondary) 2b Admission into BAMTS-Bachelor of Arts, Master of Teaching (Secondary) Must Satisfy: ((1) or ((2 or 2a or 2b)))

title: Professional Experience: Year 3A (Early Childhood)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Ensure the students understand the legal and professional requirements of teachers and of them as pre-service teachers when they undertake professional experiences Help the students plan for effective learning while undertaking professional experiences over a sustained period of time (6 weeks) Ensure that the students understand how to make an effective contribution to children's' learning through a curriculum inquiry

This topic will prepare students for their first extended block of professional experience. Students will do 5 single day visits to work with their supervising teacher in preparation for a 6 -week block in semester two. The topic will prepare students for their third year professional experience in light of perspectives on contemporary Australian and international Early Childhood research and practice. It will introduce the legal, ethical and professional responsibilities students will be expected to execute on placement, as well as the communicative and technical research skills they will need to use when theorising and implementing their placement site's inquiry focus.
learning_outcomes: Plan for, prepare for and manage learning experiences for young children with the support and guidance of the mentor
Recognise the legal and ethical responsibilities they will assume as they enter the teaching profession
Develop a research inquiry that will effectively contribute to young children's learning over time
Demonstrate awareness of the relationships and skills that will contribute to successful professional experiences
Assume responsibility for working with and teaching groups of children within the early childhood setting and with the guidance of a registered teacher
prerequisites: 1 EDUC2421 2 EDUC2321 3 EDUC1221 4 18 units of EDUC topics 5 72 units of study Must Satisfy: (1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and 5)

title: Investigating Languages Pedagogy in the Integrated Curriculum (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce curriculum knowledge and pedagogical applications in modern languages Review and evaluate the methodological principles and strategies involved in a constructivist, integrated, task based, learner centred pedagogy Explore teaching for outcomes through education for sustainability in the languages classroom

This topic provides an introduction to curriculum and pedagogy in the field of languages with particular emphasis on its application in the primary school years. The topic also offers a specialised study of theory informed practice, in relation to languages in the primary classroom with a focus on cross cultural and cross curriculum contexts within recognised accountability frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Plan and design a range of assessment tasks and demonstrate competence in assessment of and for learning
Critique constructivist teaching principles and pedagogical models with the aim of implementing a learner centred pedagogy
Identify and critique issues in modern language pedagogy including literacy and integrated curriculum concerns
Plan and design lessons and units of work for the early, primary and middle years of languages learning
Evaluate lessons with a view to understanding the key features of successful constructivist languages pedagogy
Identify and critique key elements of policy documents in the languages area, including language education for a sustainable future in the integrated curriculum
Critique a variety of learning strategies and resources appropriate for use in the teaching of modern languages
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDPRBA-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into MTPR-Master of Teaching (Primary) 1b Admission into BEDJPBA-Bachelor of Education (Junior Primary/Primary), Bachelor of Arts 1c Admission into BA-Bachelor of Arts 1d Admission into BLANG-Bachelor of Languages 1e Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 1f Admission into BLITTTESOL-Bachelor of Letters (Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages) (TESOL) 1g Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g))

title: Professional Experience: Year 3A (Primary)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Ensure the students understand the legal and professional requirements of teachers and of them as pre-service teachers when they undertake professional experiences Help the students plan for effective learning about teaching while undertaking professional experiences over a sustained period of time (4 weeks) Ensure that the students understand the most significant aspects of their behaviours and performance in the classroom while practising the art of teaching

This topic will prepare students for their first block of sustained teaching practice in professional experience. Students will also observe in the classroom and work with their mentor teacher in preparation for the 4-week teaching block in semester two.
learning_outcomes: Interact appropriately with all members of a school community
Assume responsibility for working with and teaching groups of children within the classroom and with the guidance of a registered teacher
Plan for, prepare for and manage learning experiences for a whole class with the support and guidance of the class teacher
Practise assuming the role of the teacher with the guidance of a registered teacher
prerequisites: 1 EDUC2425 - Professional Experience: Year 2B (Primary) 2 18 units of EDUC topics 3 72 units of study Must Satisfy: (1 and 2 and 3)

title: Professional Experience: Year 3A (Middle and Secondary Schooling)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Ensure the pre-service teachers understand the legal and professional requirements of teachers and of them as pre-service teachers when they undertake professional experiences Ensure that the pre-service teachers understand the behaviours and performance in the classroom expected of them while undertaking teaching and associated duties and responsibilities

Through a series of 12 lectures and 5 lead-in teaching days at a school, this topic will prepare pre-service teachers for their first 'block' teaching experience to be undertaken in semester two through the topic EDUC3642 Professional Experience: Year 3B (Middle and Secondary Schooling). During these lead-in days pre-service teachers will observe classes, develop a teaching timetable and collaborate with mentors on forthcoming teaching responsibilities.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the professional role of a teacher
Undertake school professional experience in Semester 2
prerequisites: 1 EDUC2426 - Professional Experience: Year 2B (Middle and Secondary Schooling) 2 18 units of Education topics 3 72 units of study 4 EDUC2426 - Professional Experience: Year 2B (Middle and Secondary Schooling) 5 72 units of study 6 Admission into BAMTS-Bachelor of Arts, Master of Teaching (Secondary) 6a Admission into BLANGMTS-Bachelor of Languages, Master of Teaching (Secondary) 6b Admission into BDSMTSSE-Bachelor of Disability Studies, M Teaching (Secondary & Special Ed) 6c Admission into BSCMTS-Bachelor of Science, Master of Teaching (Secondary) Must Satisfy: ((1 and 2 and 3) or (4 and 5 and (6 or 6a or 6b or 6c)))

title: Discovering Technologies Thinking
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Extend pre-service teachers’ confidence, knowledge and skills in technologies thinking for learning and teaching design and digital technologies Enable pre-service teachers to develop an appropriate integrated program in technologies with design briefs for young children Enhance pre-service teachers’ personal approach to teaching with and through technologies, based on their critical analysis of research and practical experiences including Indigenous and cultural perspectives that have shaped civilisation’s technological endeavours.

This topic is designed to explore how technologies thinking is exhibited by children in their early years and can be recognised and developed through a child-centred, play-based approach to learning. Focusing on the Technologies as a curriculum learning component in the EYLF and ACARA, the topic will build on pre-service teachers’ understanding of a technological knowledge focusing on design, systems and computational thinking. Centred around design and constructive learning and teaching with both play-based and intentional teaching strategies, pre-service teachers will investigate strategies for implementing appropriate design and digital technologies with children to expand learning opportunities around how society and cultures design and utilise a range of technologies to solve solutions. Pre-service teachers will be expected to interpret the evolving body of research associated with the intersection between technologies and science (STEM) and to justify their pedagogical approach with children in the early years. Considerations for exploring opportunities to extend professional learning reinforce the notion of a continuous approach to learning about technologies in a professional teaching capacity.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and document your practice in response to an evolving body of research in technologies thinking using digital technologies to document and share learning experiences

Demonstrate an advanced capacity to plan, analyse and justify a range of approaches to using the design processes that are supportive of project-based learning and inclusive of suitable play-based strategies
Apply critical self-knowledge which will form the foundation for expert judgement when planning to teach technologies thinking and when using digital technologies with young children safely

Critique learning resources and synthesise understandings of the relationship between play, design, teaching, learning and assessment through multimodal digital documentation to generate effective learning for technologies thinking
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC2206, EDUC2207

title: Relationships for Learning
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop: Cultivate a research-informed understanding of the need for teachers to develop relational competencies in themselves and their students in order to create and maintain positive learning environments Prepare preservice teachers to build effective relationships among learners, educators, parents, and colleagues within schools, systems and outside agencies Equip preservice teachers with contemporary knowledge, understandings and skills related to fostering the social and emotional development of diverse young people Equip preservice teachers to foster self-awareness, personal resources, resilience and coping strategies for personal and relational wellbeing for diverse young people Enable critical appraisal of approaches to managing behaviour and learning environments Establish a clear articulation between teaching philosophies, theoretical beliefs, and specific teaching approaches related to creating and maintaining positive learning environments.

This topic focuses on effective interactions and developing the relational competencies teachers need, to develop positive relationships with young people, parents, and colleagues. Preservice teachers will encounter a range of theories and approaches to classroom management that are relevant to different educational contexts, considering school, family, community, and regional issues. They will reflect upon, critique and will consider situations of students who might be experiencing such issues as bullying, harassment, exclusion, isolation, socio economic disadvantage, disempowerment, trauma, withdrawal and family difficulties.
learning_outcomes: Formulate proactive, preventative and responsive ways to facilitate the agency, empowerment and social development of young people in educational settings
Apply developing relational competencies to plan for effective classroom management and positive learning environments
Evaluate a range of theories and approaches to behaviour and classroom management
Appraise universal frameworks for supporting positive behaviour and managing behavioural difficulties, inclusive of evidence-based primary prevention strategies
Synthesise research to explore the links between curriculum, engagement, motivation and behaviour
prerequisites: 9 units of Level 2 EDUC topics

title: Engaged Learners
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Encourage students to think critically about the concepts of the engaged and involved learner Challenge students understandings of children's behaviour Introduce students to a repertoire of resources and approaches designed to maximise children's involvement and engagement as learners

Drawing on contemporary theoretical perspectives on motivation, learning and behaviour, this topic uses an inquiry approach to examine the ways that early childhood educators can maximise young children's involvement and engagement as learners in early childhood settings. Attention is drawn to different constructions of the child and the impact of these constructions on early childhood curriculum practice. Modules in this topic include theories and research relating to children's involvement and engagement, planning and programming for individuals and groups of children, observation and documentation of children's learning and assessment of learning. Specific strategies designed to maximise children's positive behaviour will also be evaluated and discussed.
learning_outcomes: Develop programs to maximise the involvement and engagement of individuals and groups of children
Reflect on their own constructions of children as particular learners and the impact of these constructions on previous curriculum practice
Use a range of strategies that maximise children's positive behaviours
Articulate a complex understanding of engagement and involvement
Understand the theories related to involving and engaging children as learners
prerequisites: 1 4.5 units of Level 2 EDUC topics 1a EDUC1221 - Approaches to Play and Learning (Professional Experience: Year 1A) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Thinking and Working Mathematically
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Support pre-service teachers to examine the mathematical practices of children in home and community, prior to and during the early years of schooling Introduce pre-service teachers to a repertoire of resources and approaches designed to enhance mathematic learning opportunities for young children Guide pre-service teachers in developing an understanding of planning for mathematical learning and effective methods to assess young children's mathematical development in early childhood settings Invite pre-service teachers to reflect on their own mathematical knowledge and support them in considering professional learning needs and opportunities for ongoing growth

This topic uses an inquiry approach to examine theory and practice in mathematics in early childhood education. Stated simply, mathematics is the study of quantity, structure, space, and change. It includes ‘numeracy’ which can be thought of as the mathematics that we use in everyday living. The topic explores the question of how the powerful mathematical proficiencies exhibited by children in their early years, can be recognised and developed within a child-centred approach to learning. It also explores the mathematical competencies needed by early childhood educators to effectively sustain and enhance these proficiencies. Included in this topic are theories and research in children's learning of mathematics, mathematical concepts available to young children, challenging children to think mathematically, catering for individual learning, planning for, and assessing mathematical learning, and creating a supportive learning environment.
learning_outcomes: Identify appropriate mathematical concepts and skills for young children, and effectively plan and implement mathematical learning experiences in early childhood settings
Implement a variety of approaches to support and enhance young children's mathematical development
Articulate the foundational theories and research underpinning mathematical teaching and learning for young children.

Evaluate strategies, including analytical and observational skills, to assess and promote young children's mathematical growth, and articulate ways to further develop mathematical content knowledge through ongoing professional learning
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC2321, EDUC3102

title: Health and Physical Education in Early Childhood
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Analyse literature and curriculum frameworks (including Health Promoting and Active Schools) that inform the resourcing and practices of Health and Physical Education in Early Childhood Settings Develop an appreciation of the importance of fundamental movement skills as the basis of all other physical activities/sports Examine the relationship between play and physical, social and emotional health and wellbeing

Through the study of health and physical education, pre-service teachers develop an understanding of the interrelationship between social environment and health outcomes. The Health Promoting Schools model is analysed and developed in order to enhance health outcomes for young children and their families. The topic examines how physical education develops movement skills through active involvement in directed play and skill learning in a variety of contexts. The early years are a time of rapid physical, social, emotional and cognitive development and regular involvement in physical activity assists and facilitates this growth and development.
learning_outcomes: Identify and use teaching strategies which engage young children with the possibilities of taking social action
Assess children's fundamental movement (motor) skill development using established criteria and testing protocols
Develop a health and physical education curriculum for an Early Childhood setting using a repertoire of teaching strategies
Analyse relevant issues concerning the implementation of Health and Physical learning programs in Early Childhood settings
prerequisites: 9 units of Level 2 EDUC topics

title: Contemporary Issues in Middle Schooling
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Examine constructions and representations of adolescence Investigate the areas for action in bridging the gap between middle schooling philosophy and practice Consider the challenges of being a middle schooling teacher Examine middle schooling curriculum frameworks Consider self efficacy and the role of research in forming and informing the middle years educator and middle schooling

This topic explores contemporary issues in middle schooling. The areas examined include the developmental needs of adolescents, areas for action for middle schooling, the challenges of being a middle years educator, the role of middle schooling in a changing world and middle school curriculum frameworks. Students will also be provided with the opportunity to explore their role as a teacher-researcher in the area of middle schooling.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of unique needs of adolescent students
Reflect on the evidence as to whether middle schooling works in order to make considered judgements and take action on middle schooling
Demonstrate a clear understanding of the roles and challenges associated with being a middle schooling teacher
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDMSSBA-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Arts 1a Admission into BEDMSSBSC-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Science 1b Admission into BEDMSBA-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Arts 1c Admission into BEDMSBHS-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Health Sciences 1d Admission into BEDMSBSC-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Science 1e Admission into BEDSBA-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Arts 1f Admission into BEDSBHS-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Health Sciences 1g Admission into BEDSBSC-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Science 1h Admission into BEDMSSEBDS-B Education (Middle & Secondary/Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1i Admission into BEDSBSE-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Special Education 2 EDUC3628 2a EDUC2323 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g or 1h or 1i) and (2 or 2a))

title: Learning and Teaching Primary Science
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims for the students to: Develop pre-service teacher’s knowledge, skills, and confidence to become a creative, innovative, effective, and engaging teacher when planning, implementing, and evaluating science across the primary years. Explore the nature of scientific inquiry, scientific literacy, contemporary learning theories, ACARA curricula and assessment, best-practice pedagogies, issues, and practical considerations of science teaching, as they relate to learners in the primary years. Support science teachers to recognise their high values and positive dispositions to ensure children and young people become excited, active learners and critical thinkers with respect to science as a human endeavour. Promote pre-service teachers' professional development as science educators by aligning all learning aspects to AITSL standards and TfEL indicators.

This topic supports pre-service teachers to develop their knowledge, skills, and confidence to become an effective teacher in planning, implementing, and evaluating science across the primary years. They will explore the nature of scientific inquiry, scientific literacy, contemporary learning theories, ACARA curricula and assessment, best-practice pedagogies, issues, and practical considerations of science teaching, as they relate to learners in the primary years. They will clarify their own understandings, values, and dispositions about their role as a science teacher to ensure children and young people become active learners and critical thinkers with respect to science as a human endeavour. Pre-service teachers learn how to be creative and innovative when planning effective and engaging primary science learning programs. Professional development in science education will be modeled using the AITSL and TfEL standards for teachers.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate in-depth knowledge of current research related to what (Australian Curriculum), why (capabilities/values), and how (pedagogies) primary years children and young people learn in the contemporary science classroom
Apply the Scientific Method to show you understand how to think and work scientifically to guide primary classroom teaching and learning activities

Develop, analyse, and justify relevant unit/lesson plans and assessments (evidence of learning) in relation to theories and principles of learning and ensure growth-oriented feedback is prioritised for primary years science children and young people
Synthesise effective learning design processes, engaging teaching strategies, and practical classroom methodologies to explain how you will bring the primary years of science curriculum to life
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC2203, EDUC2333

title: Contemporary Issues in Secondary Schooling
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Investigate the key concepts associated with secondary schooling Consider the roles and challenges involved in being a secondary schooling teacher Examine secondary schooling models and curriculum frameworks, and post-compulsory secondary schooling options Consider self efficacy and the role of research in forming and informing the secondary years educator and secondary schooling

This topic explores contemporary issues in secondary schooling. The areas examined include models of secondary schooling, the role of secondary schooling a changing world, the transition of secondary students from adolescents to young adults, the post-compulsory secondary years. Students will also be provided with the opportunity to explore their role as a teacher-researcher in the area of secondary schooling.
learning_outcomes: Reflect upon and make considered judgements about the significance of secondary schooling in a changing world
Articulate an appreciation of the importance of schooling options for students in the post-compulsory years
Develop an understanding of unique needs of secondary students in their transition from adolescence to young adulthood
Demonstrate a clear understanding of the roles and challenges associated with being a secondary schooling teacher
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDMSSBA-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Arts 1a Admission into BEDMSBA-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Arts 1b Admission into BEDMSSBHS-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Health Sciences 1c Admission into BEDMSBHS-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Health Sciences 1d Admission into BEDMSSBSC-B Education (Middle & Secondary Schooling), B Science 1e Admission into BEDMSBSC-Bachelor of Education (Middle School), Bachelor of Science 1f Admission into BEDSBA-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Arts 1g Admission into BEDSBHS-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Health Sciences 1h Admission into BEDSBSC-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Science 2 EDUC3628 - Numeracy and ICT Across the Middle and Secondary Curriculum 3 Admission into BEDSBLANG-Bachelor of Education (Secondary), Bachelor of Languages Must Satisfy: (((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g or 1h) and 2) or (3))

title: Numeracy and ICT Across the Middle and Secondary Curriculum
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop a positive disposition toward numeracy and the use of ICTs Understand the responsibilities associated with teaching numeracy and the use of ICTs in the middle and secondary years in content area classrooms

This topic focusses on the concept of numeracy across the curriculum and the use of professional ICT in the design and delivery of pedagogical material.
