The key ideas addressed include: the nature of numeracy and critical numeracy; the professional numeracy and ICT demands in the teaching profession; the role of numeracy and applications of ICT within different curriculum areas; the inherent numeracy demands and opportunities within these curriculum areas for middle and secondary students; and the opportunities and limitations associated with the use of ICT in the design of integrated pedagogical materials.
learning_outcomes: Use ICT as a tool to enhance student learning outcomes and support students to become more aware of their needs as learners
Identify examples of numeracy in the community
Understand the power of and use of quantitative information to influence people's thinking
Make connections between their specialist teaching areas and numeracy
Understand the difference between mathematics and numeracy
prerequisites: 4.5 units of Level 2 EDUC topics

title: Students with Learning and Behavioural Difficulties
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to introduce students to the characteristics and identification issues associated with a range of learning difficulties and emotional and behavioural disorders. The topic will also develop students' understanding of the following broad special education principles: The experiences of individuals with diverse learning needs can impact the ability to learn, interact socially, and live as a fulfilled contributing member of the community Inclusive educational practices promote access to, participation in and achievement in relation to quality curriculum for all students The educational elements of curriculum, instruction, assessment, learning, engagement and behaviour are interdependent Professionals work collaboratively to promote transdisciplinary teaming as an integrated approach to teaching and learning

This topic introduces students to the characteristics and identification of a range of learning difficulties, specific learning disabilities and emotional and behavioural disorders and their implications for individual children and adolescents in educational settings. Students will explore relationships between individual and environmental factors that may influence developmental, behavioural and educational outcomes for children at risk of learning and behavioural difficulties, and consider how to manage learning environments to promote learning, positive behaviour and emotional wellbeing.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the implications for educational practice of alternative approaches to identification of specific learning disabilities

Describe characteristics and possible causes of a range of learning difficulties, specific learning disabilities, and emotional and behavioural disorders and their potential impact for individuals on learning, behaviour and wellbeing
Describe a continuum of practices that maximise task engagement and promote positive interaction and behaviour for students at risk of learning and behavioural difficulties

Identify policies and ethical principles of measurement and assessment related to referral, eligibility, program planning, instruction, and placement for individuals with learning and behavioural difficulties, including those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds
prerequisites: 1 9 units of EDUC topics 1a Admission into BEDSEOS-Bachelor of Education (Special Education) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a))

title: Professional Experience: Year 3 (Early Childhood)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enable pre-service teachers through research and inquiry, to continue to build upon their understanding of how children learn and develop by incorporating theoretical knowledge whilst making a meaningful contribution to the site and children's learning Provide pre-service teachers with Early Childhood contexts to use a variety of observation and assessment techniques to gain insight into the types of experiences, activities and ideas which engage young children Engage pre-service teachers in the work of planning, implementing, evaluating and documenting a curriculum which involves and engages children in deep and meaningful learning over a sustained period of time Provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to establish positive working relationships with colleagues, parents and families as a collaborative and collegiate team member Support pre-service teachers in documenting and organising evidence of developing professional knowledge, professional practice and professional relationships

This profesional experience comprises a full-time 6-week placement which immerses pre-service teachers in a metropolitan or country early childhood setting. Pre-service teachers practise planning, implementing and evaluating a progressive teaching program that demonstrates their understanding of how children learn. They make a meaningful contribution to children’s learning by creating and implementing an inquiry which supports children’s learning. Pre-service teachers practise developing relationships with parents, families and colleagues and begin to take responsibility for reflecting on and identifying their own learning needs. Successful completion of this topic prepares pre-service teachers for their final Professional Experience.
learning_outcomes: Plan, implement and evaluate meaningful curriculum-based experiences which use a range of resources and are responsive to the needs and interests of young children with support from the mentor teacher
Develop a repertoire of theoretically-informed pedagogical strategies through analysis and reflection upon teaching decisions and approaches
Practise and analyse an array of accurate, formal and informal methods of observation, assessment and documentation to inform teaching practice
Formulate an inquiry, based on relevant theory and observations of children’s experiences which sequentially supports and builds upon children’s learning
Develop ways of communicating effectively with families about children's learning and development
prerequisites: 1 2 of EDUC2206, EDUC2207, EDUC1221, EDUC1242, EDUC1225 2 72 units of study 3 2 of EDUC1221, EDUC1225, EDUC1242 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2 and 3)

title: Assessment and Planning for Students with Numeracy Difficulties
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to develop capacities in pre‐service teachers to: Evaluate current numeracy research focused on students with learning difficulties Appraise, and interpret numeracy assessment processes Explain how numeracy intervention programs for students with learning difficulties may be implemented

This topic is designed to provide preservice teachers with the opportunity to understand approaches to supporting students with numeracy difficulties. There will be a focus on perspectives about numeracy, factors that affect numeracy learning, and consideration given to issues around curriculum, planning, programming, and instruction. Students will be involved in analysing data, prioritising, and planning intervention programs to further develop school students’ knowledge, understanding and skills and will explore ways to further engage and involve them in their numeracy learning.
learning_outcomes: Prioritise and plan intervention programs by analysing assessment information
Determine how the educational elements of curriculum, assessment, instruction, and learning, are interdependent
Evaluate selection of instructional strategies based on evidence‐informed research
Discuss major theories and factors which may inhibit development of numeracy
Create resources that may be used to develop diverse students’ numeracy knowledge, understanding, and skills
Assess links between evidence‐based research and practical application in classrooms
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BISEEC-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) 1a Admission into BISEP-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Primary) 1b Admission into BISES-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Secondary) 1c Admission into BEDSTBDS Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Disability Studies 1d Admission into BEDSEOS Bachelor of Education (Special Education) 1e Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 1f Admission into BEDSEC - Bachelor of Education (Secondary) 1g Admission into BEDIE - Bachelor of Education (Inclusive Education) 2 18 units of topics Must satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d or 1e or 1f or 1g) and (2))

title: Inclusive Teaching Practices
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Demonstrate understanding of how students learn and how evidence-based instruction supports engagement and progression for all learners. Build knowledge of tiered intervention models and data-informed planning within a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS). Strengthen capacity to interpret and apply legislation, policy, and professional obligations that ensure inclusion and support for students with disability. Foster professional resilience, reflection, and collaboration to sustain ethical, inclusive, and high-expectation teaching practices

This topic develops pre-service teachers’ knowledge, understanding, and application of inclusive education and evidence-based teaching practices that support the learning and wellbeing of all children and young people. It explicitly teaches the legislation, regulations, policies, and obligations related to inclusion and support, including international agreements such as the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) and legal entitlements defined by the Commonwealth Disability Discrimination Act (1992) and the Disability Standards for Education (2005) . Pre-service teachers examine how these frameworks, together with professional codes of conduct and ethical responsibilities, guide inclusive and equitable practice in schools. They learn to design, implement, and evaluate teaching that reflects how children learn (Core Content 2.2 and 2.3) and to apply evidence-based instructional approaches (Core Content 2.6 and 3.2) including Universal Design for Learning (UDL), Explicit Instruction (EI) at Tier 1, Differentiated Instruction (DI) at Tiers 2 and 3, and Systematic Instruction (SI) at Tiers 2 and 3 within a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS). Through analysis of authentic classroom scenarios and school-based case studies, pre-service teachers develop the capacity to integrate legislative knowledge, ethical practice, and data-informed instruction to plan inclusive learning environments that uphold every learner’s right to access, participate, and progress.
learning_outcomes: Explain how students learn and how instruction adapts as learner familiarity and expertise increase, using modelling and scaffolding principles based on established educational theory
Implement multi-tiered academic and behaviour supports to address diverse learning and behavioural needs in classroom practice

Design inclusive learning experiences that apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL), Differentiated Instruction (DI), Explicit Instruction (EI), and Systematic Instruction (SI) as Tier 1-3 approaches within a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) framework to meet diverse student needs
Demonstrate understanding of ethical decision-making and professional conduct in inclusive practice, including teachers’ legal and moral responsibilities for equitable participation

Interpret the legislation, regulations, policies, and obligations that underpin inclusion and support in Australian schools, including the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989), the Disability Discrimination Act (1992), and the Disability Standards for Education (2005)
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1224 2 1 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322 Must satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Differentiating Learning Experiences in Diverse Classrooms
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Cultivate deep understanding of learner diversity and the implications for planning and teaching Prepare preservice teachers with contemporary understandings, knowledge and skills in inclusive curriculum design, assessment, and research‐informed teaching for academically diverse learners Prepare preservice teachers to establish and manage flexible, responsive, and inclusive classroom learning environments Encourage collaborative approaches to supporting young people with specialised educational needs in inclusive settings

Effective primary teachers are responsive to learner diversity as they facilitate inclusive learning environments that enable all students to access quality curriculum and experience academic growth. In this topic, preservice teachers will engage with key principles underlying differentiation for diverse learners and examine inclusive classroom practices. They will synthesise and build upon their understanding of learning, development, and effective teaching and assessment, and will apply this to design learning experiences suitable for the full range of learners in academically diverse classrooms. Preservice teachers will consider their roles and responsibilities in supporting students with specialised educational needs to thrive in inclusive classrooms.
learning_outcomes: Synthesise knowledge of learner diversity, inclusive practices, research‐informed teaching and legislative requirements into a holistic understanding of inclusion and differentiation
Incorporate appropriate technologies into a differentiated learning task to facilitate students' curriculum access and engagement
Design differentiated learning tasks suitable for the full range of students in academically diverse classrooms, in the context of one or more curriculum domains
Articulate key principles of effective differentiation and how these are reflected in a range of educational practices
Evaluate planning and teaching practices using a framework of key principles for inclusion
prerequisites: 45 units of EDUC topics

title: Implementing Tier 1 and 2 Schoolwide Positive Behaviour Intervention and Support
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Equip pre-service teachers to use research informed practices in SWPBIS. Cultivate understanding of educational implications for individuals with disabilities who exhibit behaviours of concern. Promote creative and reflective practice through design of ethical approaches to promoting positive behaviour.

This topic is designed to develop skills in developing universal (Tier 1) interventions and support in educational settings. Planning and implementation are based on the principles of Schoolwide Positive Behaviour Support (SWPBIS) of prevention and teaching prosocial behaviours. Pre-service teachers are required to develop a behaviour matrix and lesson plans for teaching prosocial skills.
learning_outcomes: Analyse classroom ecology and address prevention, teaching and responding to behaviour
Develop preventive practices that address diverse learning needs in inclusive and specialised settings
Discuss how the characteristics of diverse learners are considered in the design of a SWPBIS
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC2320, EDUC2336, DSRS2231

title: Digital Literacy and Numeracy in Education
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: • Develop pre-service teachers’ knowledge and understanding of the numeracy and information and communication technology (ICT) demands of the teaching profession. • Enhance pre-service teachers’ capacity to design and justify curriculum which fosters the development of numeracy and digital literacy capabilities of young learners within curriculum learning areas.

This topic examines the numeracy and information and communication technology (ICT) demands of the teaching profession. Pre‐service teachers will examine the relevant issues and strategies to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning and teaching. They will also justify their design of curriculum which fosters the development of young learners’ numeracy and digital literacy capabilities.
learning_outcomes: Explain the responsibilities, safety considerations and ethical issues associated with using information and communication technologies in learning and teaching
Justify the design of curriculum which effectively integrates evidence-based teaching strategies and ICT
Articulate a critical understanding of numeracy in the community and its application within a curriculum learning area
prerequisites: 18 units of EDUC topics

title: Partnerships, Parents and Participation
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Assist pre‐service teachers to develop an understanding of the social construction of families and childhoods Introduce pre‐service teachers to the concept of family‐centred, strengths‐based practice in early childhood settings Enable pre‐service teachers to critically analyse a wide variety of resources and approaches for working in partnership with families to enhance learning opportunities for young children, including those with special rights

This topic addresses the interface between early childhood education and care with the lives of children and families in diverse contexts. Through case studies of early childhood educators working effectively in partnership with diverse families and a range of agencies, the topic develops an understanding of the social constructions of families and childhoods, the social practices they adopt and the services in which they participate. Approaches to strengths‐based, family‐centred practice are also explored.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a family‐centred, strengths‐based approach to working in partnership with parents and other agencies in early childhood settings
Elaborate upon how educators gather, form and critique knowledge of families and childhoods
Discuss the contemporary issues affecting families and young children and the implications these have for early childhood educators working within an equity and social justice framework
prerequisites: 1 2 of EDUC1221, EDUC1225, EDUC1242 2 Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 2a Admission into BEDSEC-Bachelor of Education (Secondary) 2b Admission into BEDSHPE-Bachelor of Education (Secondary Health and Physical Education) 2c Admission into BEDPRBA-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Arts 2d Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 2e Admission into MTPR-Master of Teaching (Primary) 2f Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 2g Admission into BEDPRSEBDS-B Education (Primary R-7 & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 2h Admission into BEDPRBGSC-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of General Science 2i Admission into BEDSTBLANG-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Languages 2j Admission into BEDSTBHS-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Health Sciences 2k Admission into BEDSTBGSC-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of General Science 2l Admission into BEDSTBSC-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Science 2m Admission into BEDSTBA-Bachelor of Education Studies, Bachelor of Arts Must Satisfy: ((1) or (2 or 2a or 2b or 2c or 2d or 2e or 2f or 2g or 2h or 2i or 2j or 2k or 2l or 2m))

title: Readers, Reading and Literature in the Early Years (Professional Experience: Year 3A)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Inform pre‐service teachers about the foundational knowledge required for children to learn to read and how evidence‐based practice across the following elements are important in children’s early reading experience; phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension and oral language Support pre‐service teachers in identifying, articulating and reflecting upon reading pedagogies which are effective in supporting children’s early reading progress Inform and give opportunities to practise how to plan for and assess children’s early reading Give pre‐teachers the necessary tools to effectively assess children’s reading and respond to ensure the progress of children’s reading development Identify a range of assessment strategies and practise using them with young children Organise and construct a plan that allows for effective teaching and learning to be undertaken during the Professional Experience placement Summarise how to make an effective contribution to children’s’ learning through a curriculum inquiry

This topic invites pre‐service teachers to explore more deeply how young children learn to read and the foundational knowledge and understandings which underpin this process. The role of parents and community are considered in children’s early experience. Knowledge of evidence‐based practice around emergent reading is developed and pre‐service teachers apply intentional teaching for growing foundational knowledge; such as phonological awareness, oral language, vocabulary and conceptual knowledge, and the alphabetic principle. Pre‐service teachers use effective pedagogies and assessment methods to inform teaching and children’s progress as early readers. This topic will prepare pre‐service teachers for their first extended block of professional experience. Each pre‐service teacher completes 5 single day visits and work with a mentor teacher to establish plans for a 6‐week block‐placement in Semester 2. This topic focusses on the transition from theory to practice considering perspectives on contemporary Australian and international Early Childhood research and practice. The topic introduces the communicative and technical research skills which pre‐service teachers will use when theorising upon and implementing the inquiry focus of their placement sites.
learning_outcomes: Define reading and articulate how children derive meaning from text and how reading fluency may be promoted in young readers
Synthesise research literature and different perspectives to articulate an informed and evidence‐based approach to teaching reading
Demonstrate awareness of relationships, skills and legal and ethical responsibilities which will contribute to successful professional experience
Develop a research or curriculum inquiry that progressively and effectively contributes to young children’s learning over time
Utilise appropriate and highly effective pedagogies for teaching reading which acknowledge semantic, grammatical, graphophonic and visual knowledge
Evidence an array of assessment strategies used to plan, prepare and implement learning experiences for young children with support and guidance from the mentor teacher
Apply understanding of how phonics and other decoding skills are taught intentionally and build on children’s existing knowledge
Support children’s developing identity as readers and promote diverse experiences with quality literature and multimodal texts
Correctly assess children’s reading comprehension and articulate related proficiencies
prerequisites: 1 72 units of topics 2 4 of EDUC1238, EDUC1221, EDUC1242, EDUC1225, EDUC2321, EDUC2421 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Visual Arts, Media Arts, and Design and Technology
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre‐service teachers’ knowledge and confidence to critically analyse and creatively respond to art and design challenges Develop pre‐service teachers’ knowledge, understanding and skills involved in the design, development and use of technologies to enrich and transform societies Prepare preservice teachers to use research findings in a variety of relevant and innovative arts and design technologies teaching methodologies and resources Equip preservice teachers with the ability to use inclusive teaching practices in the arts and design technologies Cultivate ethical, creative and responsive designers when producing and using technologies

Through an integrated approach this topic introduces an understanding of the role of critical analysis and creativity in response to an increasingly technological and complex world. The themes of making and responding through various viewpoints are explored in relation to different cultural and vocational contexts. Pre‐service teachers apply and critique a variety of teaching methodologies and resources as they develop necessary practical skills for teaching in the Visual Arts, Media Arts and Design Technologies. This topic provides pre‐service teachers with the opportunity to plan and prepare for incorporating learning in these subjects in primary school settings.
learning_outcomes: Discuss ethical, legal, aesthetic and functional factors in your choice and use of technologies
Integrate cognitive, technical and creative skills in all arts subjects to plan for inclusive teaching in and through the Visual Arts and Media Arts and Design and Technologies
Critically analyse recent developments in Visual Arts and Media Arts, and Design and Technologies education
Combine the creative application of resources, methodology and skills for teaching the Visual Arts, Media Arts and Design and Technologies
Individually and collaboratively, plan effective learning experiences in Visual and Media arts and Design and Technologies for Primary Years students
prerequisites: 36 units of EDUC topics

title: Professional Experience 2: Assessment to Enhance Learning
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic enables pre-service teachers to apply an understanding of learning theories, curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment approaches to effectively design, manage, and assess learning of children and young people. The topic requires an applied approach to ensure that assessment is viewed as an opportunity to enhance learning by promoting knowledge, skills and attitudes to effectively assess learning and improve teaching practice.

The topic bridges theoretical understanding and practical application for students, enabling them to effectively design, manage, and assess learning in children and young people. Grounded in comprehensive learning theories, curriculum principles, pedagogical approaches, and diverse assessment approaches and strategies, the topic empowers students to embrace assessment as a measurement tool and a catalyst for enriched learning experiences. Through an applied and integrated approach, such as hands-on activities, case studies and practical simulations, students are equipped with the knowledge and skills to perceive assessment as a dynamic process intertwined with teaching practices. Students learn to harness assessment to gauge understanding, monitor progress, and tailor instructional strategies to meet individual learning needs. Students develop a holistic perspective on evaluation beyond traditional testing paradigms by fostering a deep understanding of various assessment methods and gaining proficiency in crafting authentic, equitable and inclusive assessments. By integrating assessment seamlessly into the teaching and learning cycle, students learn to leverage feedback as a tool for growth, encouraging iterative refinement of both teaching practice and student learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Examine own and others' approaches to teaching and assessment, utilising professional feedback, to identify strengths and challenges in professional practice
Critique and apply current teaching, learning, and assessment principles and processes to improve teaching practice
Critique current assessment policies, processes, and practices to evaluate their influence and impact on learning and learning environments
Evaluate and reflect on the design of inclusive and equitable assessments for children and young people as well as own assessment practices
prerequisites: 1 1 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322 2 EDUC3653 Must satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Mathematics Curriculum Specialisation: Developing Curriculum in Context in the Middle Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to analyse and synthesise the middle years' curriculum. It aims to enhance pre-service teacher confidence, knowledge and skills so that appropriate teaching and learning programs can be enacted for areas of subject specialisation.

This topic provides an introduction to, and critical analysis of, the nature and purposes of curriculum in education. It develops students' knowledge, skills and understandings in designing teaching and learning programs within contemporary understandings of curriculum and pedagogy, for a specific learning area. The focus is particularly on the middle years of schooling.
learning_outcomes: Apply curriculum frameworks to plan and implement coherent, developmentally appropriate learning sequences for the middle years
Apply educational research, theory, and concepts to design inclusive and engaging teaching and learning experiences using evidence-based pedagogical practices
Review and adapt teaching, learning, and assessment practices using evidence of student learning and reflective analysis
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1244 2 1 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320 Must satisfy: (1 and 2)

It develops students' knowledge, skills and understandings in designing teaching and learning programs within contemporary understandings of curriculum and pedagogy, for a specific learning area. The focus is particularly on the middle years of schooling.
learning_outcomes: Review and adapt teaching, learning, and assessment practices using evidence of student learning and reflective analysis
Apply educational research, theory, and concepts to design inclusive and engaging teaching and learning experiences using evidence-based pedagogical practices
Apply curriculum frameworks to plan and implement coherent, developmentally appropriate learning sequences for the middle years

title: Empowering Educators in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: • Familiarise pre-service teachers with the theoretical concepts and practical applications of artificial intelligence in educational contexts. • Equip pre-service teachers with the knowledge and skills necessary to critically evaluate and select appropriate AI tools for different educational purposes. • Empower pre-service teachers to design and implement AI-enhanced learning experiences that promote student engagement, personalization, and academic success.

This topic explores the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in educational settings, with a focus on preparing pre-service teachers to leverage AI tools effectively in their future classrooms. Pre-service teachers will examine the theoretical foundations of AI in education, explore various AI applications, and develop practical skills for incorporating AI technologies to enhance teaching and learning experiences.
learning_outcomes: Articulate the theoretical foundations of AI in education and its potential impact on teaching and learning
Reflect critically on the ethical considerations and implications of integrating AI technologies in educational settings
Design and implement AI-enhanced learning activities that cater to diverse child and young person needs and promote active engagement and collaboration
Evaluate and select appropriate AI tools and technologies based on pedagogical principles and learning objectives
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322

title: Leading Self and Others in Early Childhood Settings
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: assist pre-service teachers to bring their life experiences, educational and curriculum knowledge to bear on the investigation and review of contemporary educational and leadership issues. introduce pre-service teachers to procedures that can be used to critically analyse educational systems and selected contemporary educational and leadership issues. Analyse the roles and responsibilities of a leader within an Early Childhood setting. Reflect on their own knowledge and skill base and consider professional development priorities that will enable them to, as a future leader of an early childhood setting, play a critical role in that centre's provision of quality early childhood education for young children.

In the final semester of the program of study this topic is designed to provide pre-service teachers with the opportunity to reflect on the knowledge developed in this professional degree while drawing on the contexts of their personal life experiences and knowledge and understandings from their earlier studies. Pre-service teachers will be challenged to investigate significant contemporary educational and leadership issues and to use their educational and curriculum knowledge to explain and justify the positions they adopt in relation to these issues, and subsequently evidence their readiness to graduate. These understandings are applied in pre-service teachers' development and critical reflection on their role and responsibility as educational leaders in making research-informed quality improvements across all standards, and especially in pedagogical practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on educational research to extend understanding and knowledge, applying findings to continuously improve professional practices
Synthesise and critically evaluate relevant beliefs, knowledge, and skills to articulate a personal philosophy of teaching and education
Demonstrate how you have met graduate level focus-areas of the Australian Professional Standards for teaching by presenting evidence in a completed professional portfolio
Demonstrate an understanding of the ethical and professional leadership skills required for managing and leading early childhood settings, integrating foundational knowledge and skills
prerequisites: 1 EDUC4740 2 ^EDUC3104 Must satisfy: ((1 or 2)) ^= May be enrolled concurrently

title: Literacy in the Inclusive Classroom
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre-service teachers’ understanding of structured literacy practices and how they address equity in literacy education Equip pre-service teachers with the knowledge and skills necessary to design and implement evidence-informed literacy instruction that meets the diverse needs of learners Empower pre-service teachers to create literacy environments underpinned by the principles of cognitive science, to promote student voice, choice, and engagement in meaningful learning experiences To cultivate pre-service teachers’ capacity for action research, reflective practice, and ongoing professional growth in literacy instruction, ensuring decisions are informed by contemporary frameworks

This topic equips pre-service teachers with the knowledge and skills to foster inclusive and empowering literacy learning experiences for all children and young people. Pre-service teachers will explore evidence-informed teaching strategies and frameworks including high-quality well differentiated classroom instruction, assessment practices, progress monitoring, and decision-making processes for small-group interventions. By engaging with contemporary research, case studies, and best practices such as explicit-direct instruction, multi-tiered and system-wide approaches, pre-service teachers will gain a deep understanding of how to adapt and implement structured literacy instruction and interventions that meets the diverse needs of learners while nurturing their academic and personal growth.
learning_outcomes: Design and justify structured literacy instruction that incorporates the principles of universal design, explicit direct instruction, and multi-tiered systems of support and how they empower students as active participants in their literacy learning, fostering autonomy, ownership, and motivation, addresses diverse learners' needs and promotes equity in access and opportunity

Engage in action research, reflection, and plan professional development to refine your literacy instruction and improve children and young people's outcomes, ensuring decisions are informed by evidence-based practices and contemporary frameworks

Select and incorporate culturally relevant texts, materials, and experiences into literacy instruction to promote generalisation of learning, while also privileging children and young peoples' identities and backgrounds

Articulate an understanding of the principles of universal design, explicit direct instruction and multi-tiered systems of support, their application to literacy instruction and how they address the cognitive requirements of reading and writing
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC1222, EDUC1230, EDUC3106

title: Curriculum, Programming and Planning in the Junior Primary Classroom
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Explore how different curriculum frameworks can be integrated effectively to enhance learning in junior primary classrooms. Evaluate existing programming and planning practices to assess their effectiveness in addressing diverse learning needs and promoting active engagement and meaningful learning experiences. Examine planning methodologies that support differentiated instruction and personalised learning in junior primary settings. Engage in reflective practice to analyse teaching and learning experiences, gather evidence of learning, and meet graduate professional standards for teachers.

By synthesising theoretical knowledge gained from academic coursework with practical insights from professional placements, pre-service teachers will explore the skills and understanding necessary to effectively navigate the complexities of curriculum development, programming, and planning in junior primary education. Pre-service teachers will critically analyse evidence of their learning and performance across course topics and professional experience as a process for gathering evidence to meet the graduate professional standards for teachers and document this in teaching performance assessment activities.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply various curriculum frameworks to enhance learning in junior primary classrooms
Engage in reflective practice to analyse teaching and learning experiences, gather evidence of learning, and meet graduate professional standards for teachers
Evaluate and improve programming and planning practices to effectively address diverse learning needs and promote active engagement
Implement planning methodologies that support differentiated instruction and personalised learning in junior primary settings
prerequisites: 1 3 of EDUC3640, EDUC3618 and EDUC3622 2 ^ EDUC4740 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2) ^ = May be enrolled concurrently

title: Internship B
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
In this topic pre-service teachers will continue to explore their role as a teacher in educational settings with the support of their mentor to inform reflection and application of feedback. Pre-service teachers will have the opportunity to specifically explore components of their teaching they wish to enhance as they build a portfolio of evidence to support a deepening in understanding of their practice to further evidence their engagement with the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.

Internship A and B are designed to be taken concurrently to enable pre-service teachers to engage with learning directly connected with a school or pre-school setting. Internships are awarded via a competitive process with the locations and subject areas to be taught identified by the relevant employer (e.g. Department for Education). Students who are successful in gaining an internship will engage with this topic whilst employed in a fractional teaching contract with specific criteria stipulated for mentorship arrangements. The aims, outcomes and assessments outlined for the topic will be engaged with and completed as part of the daily duties required of the PST as in-service teacher. Identified workshops and online activities are designed to maintain connection and further mentorship from the university to support the PST to be successful in their role.
learning_outcomes: Produce records of learning to communicate achievement to children and young people and parents/caregivers through various methods.
Engage in reflective cycles with children and young people to demonstrate the provision of and acting on feedback.
Interpret individual and whole of class assessment data to reflect upon and adjust practice.
Evaluate the effectiveness of teaching and learning utilising data to inform reflection and future action
prerequisites: 1 3 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322, EDUC3661, EDUC3642, EDUC3641, EDUC4742, EDUC4741 2 ^ EDUC4102 ^ = May be enrolled concurrently Must satisfy: ((1 and 2))

title: Health Curriculum Specialisation: Middle Years 3
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop preservice teachers’ knowledge of the concepts, substance, structure and teaching strategies in a Middle Years teaching area Introduce preservice teachers to relevant curriculum policy and curriculum frameworks Extend preservice teachers’ understanding of learning design processes, including curriculum, pedagogical strategies and assessment Support preservice teachers in developing effective teaching and learning sequences

This topic provides an introduction to the nature and purposes of curriculum studies in teaching specialist areas. It develops preservice teachers’ (PSTs) knowledge, skills and understandings in designing teaching and learning programs within contemporary understandings of curriculum, pedagogy and assessment. The focus is particularly on the Middle Years of schooling.
learning_outcomes: Apply an emerging depth of knowledge of the concepts, substance, structure and teaching strategies in a teaching area, to learning design processes
Evaluate the role of a range of curriculum policies and approaches, in relation to learning design processes
Organise teaching area content into an effective learning and teaching sequence
Demonstrate understanding of Middle Schooling contexts in relation to learning design processes
Design teaching and learning sequences that cater for student diversity
Apply and evaluate a range of pedagogical strategies to learning design

school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work

In this topic, pre-service teachers will explore the transitional phase from pre-service teacher to early career teacher. The internship provides pre-service teachers with the opportunity to demonstrate an application of learning across their degree whilst purposefully engaging in formalised mentorship to inform ongoing reflective cycles.

Internship A and B are designed to be taken concurrently to enable pre-service teachers to engage with learning directly connected with a school or pre-school setting. learning_outcomes: Create engaging learning experiences that demonstrate contextual awareness
Plan for sequential learning and assessment that applies an understanding of pre-assessment, differentiated instruction and universal design for learning
Analyse strategies for communication and management by drawing upon a variety of feedback and critiquing links to evidence-informed approaches
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322, EDUC3661, EDUC3642, EDUC3641, EDUC4742, EDUC4741

title: Teaching How to Learn
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to Introduce students to how to promote self-regulate learning in the classroom Investigate the interactive, constructive, active, passive (ICAP) theoretical framework to promote effective student learning Enhance classroom practices through the application of self-regulated learning and ICAP theoretical framework.

This topic explores how learning environments can be created and adjusted to enhance the experience of learners. You will explore self-regulated learning and other ways of promoting student cognitive engagement to support achievement and learning. Theoretical concepts will be presented as an avenue to explore application of ideas into practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply evidence-informed strategies to improve classroom practices and learning environments that support student learning
Explain how self-regulated learning and the ICAP theoretical framework can inform effective classroom practice
Examine classroom practices to identify opportunities to promote student cognitive engagement

title: Critical Pedagogies for a Changing World
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
The topic aims to: Use critical pedagogical strategies to provide students with opportunities to broaden and deepen their knowledge and understanding of the ethical issues involved in early childhood education in a changing world Examine a repertoire of critical pedagogical approaches to social and environmental education, and how these can be mobilised effectively in early years settings Build skill-levels of students in planning and developing curriculum that promotes more just and inclusive educational environments Support students in analysing the ethical issues presented by a changing world, and developing their own critical and professional approach to these issues Strengthen students' communication and research skills, to help them become skilled practitioners, able to manage complex and sensitive ethical issues, and support children and families from a diversity of backgrounds

Critical pedagogies for a changing world explores the key concepts of critical and transformative education - social justice, equity, ecological/social sustainability, identity & values - within the context of the early years. The topic draws on Humanities and Social Sciences knowledge to examine the key theoretical ideas of place, space, time, continuity and change that underpin The Early Years Learning Framework and The Australian Curriculum documents and pedagogical practices. The topic develops a sense of professional autonomy in students, challenging them to find creative and novel ways to support young children in their participation in their social worlds, within and beyond the classroom. Using a social and critical pedagogies approach, it addresses practical dilemmas faced by teachers in the modern world, exploring the ethical questions underlying relevant issues. The topic enables students to develop a critical understanding of the social and environmental changes that are occurring in global society, and build a sense of expertise and competence in responding to these pedagogically.
learning_outcomes: Understand an educator's personal responsibility in evaluating difficult ethical issues, and the legal and professional frameworks which may guide and delimit this responsibility
Articulate and justify their pedagogical approach based on a critical analysis of theory and practical experiences
Apply creative and meaningful strategies in response to evolving ethical dilemmas within early years settings

Use a repertoire of theoretically-justifiable planning and evaluation tools which which draw on the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum to engage, enhance, and evaluate young children's learning in regard to social and environmental change
Understand the key theoretical concepts of this topic, and interpret them within the context of early years education in a global and diverse world
prerequisites: 1 2 of EDUC2324, EDUC2424 2 2 of EDUC3658, EDUC3640 Must Satisfy: ((1) or (2))

title: Investigating Early Years Curriculum and Pedagogy
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide students with a theoretical framework and a set of conceptual tools for thinking about and analysing early childhood curriculum and pedagogy Introduce students to the national and international policy context of early childhood curriculum and pedagogy Assist students in understanding the differences between curriculum and pedagogy across the different sectors of early childhood education Help students understand the interrelationship between discourses of curriculum and pedagogy, leadership, teacher identities and social justice and equity

This topic examines the historical, cultural and political discourses producing contemporary conceptions of early childhood leadership, curriculum and pedagogy. Differences between conceptions of curriculum and pedagogy across the different sectors of early childhood education are interrogated and the impact of these differences on early childhood teacher/leader identities is explored. Implications for the development of socially just and equitable early childhood education are investigated.
learning_outcomes: Compare international developments in early childhood curriculum and pedagogy
Recognise the ways in which their identities as early childhood educators and leaders are linked to particular discourses of curriculum and pedagogy
Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between discourses of curriculum and pedagogy, leadership, teacher identity and early childhood education that is socially just and equitable
Describe the context of early childhood curriculum policy in Australia
Identify the historical, political and cultural discourses producing contemporary conceptions of early childhood curriculum and pedagogy
prerequisites: 1 EDUC3640 - Professional Experience: Year 3 (Early Childhood) 1a EDUC3665 - Professional Teaching Practice 3E (Early Childhood) 1b Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1c Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c))

title: Thinking and Working Scientifically in the Early Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Enhance pre-service teachers' confidence, knowledge and skills in science learning and teaching Enable pre-service teachers to develop an appropriate program in science for children Enhance pre-service teachers' personal approach to science teaching based on their critical analysis of practical experiences in light of theoretical perspectives

This topic provides opportunities for pre-service teachers to consider the place of science in their own lives as well as in the daily lives of children 0-8 years. Using inquiry learning processes, pre-service teachers are supported to identify the early signs of children developing concepts, skills and positive attitudes towards science. To build on these observations, pre-service teachers are supported to plan, implement, and evaluate programs of intentional teaching in science with considerations for integration across other areas. The topic develops pre-service teachers' development of scientific literacy and content knowledge through experimental science in the areas of the Biological Sciences, Chemical Sciences, Earth and Space Sciences and the Physical Sciences. Drawing from their knowledge of the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum: Science, strong inter-curricular links with other learning areas are made through examining the role of Science in our children's everyday lives, including the media and the history of science as a field of study.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate high level scientific process skills, literacy and knowledge through experimental learning
Plan a balanced, sequential unit of work in science by drawing on The Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum: Science
Critically assess personal attitudes towards science, its applications and how their scientific identity has been shaped by family and culture both locally and globally
Identify techniques to support children's increasing awareness of safety procedures related to science investigatory play
Discuss how science may be integrated across the curriculum in ways which encourage children's curiosity and play as they investigate their natural and built environments
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1b Admission into BEDECBSE-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Special Education 1c Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1d Admission into BISEEC-Bachelor of Inclusive and Specialised Education (Early Childhood) Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c or 1d))

title: Approaches to Teaching English and Literacy
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide preservice teachers with the skills and understanding to manage the resources required for teaching a variety of genres and multimodal texts aligned with the Australian Curriculum: English Provide preservice teachers' opportunities to discern between the research‐based pedagogic practices to teach Australian English to students with a range of abilities and cultural backgrounds Develop preservice teachers' knowledge about when and how to use a range of assessment and moderation practices that guide the teaching and learning of literacy and English Encourage an enactment of socially just approaches to teaching English and literacy for primary students with a range of abilities and backgrounds, including ATSI students Create opportunities for planning to undertake research on ‘own’ teaching practice Deepen preservice teacher understandings of the key principles of unit planning in readiness for professional practice in a Primary Years classroom

This topic is designed to provide pre‐service teachers with the knowledge and skills to teach literary genres and multimodal texts to students in the Primary Years. In this topic, pre‐service teachers will create a sequence of lessons in preparation to teach, deliver, moderate and assess the English Curriculum during the final professional experience. The unit of work will reflect current curriculum frameworks, knowledge gained from research, and the engagement of students from diverse backgrounds including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students. This topic also provides preservice teachers the opportunity to prepare to undertake research on ‘own’ practice as teaching occurs in the final Professional Experience.
learning_outcomes: Select, prioritise and manage resources required for teaching a variety of genres and multimodal texts aligned with the Australian Curriculum: English
Plan for research on ‘own’ practice and evaluate how that impacted your professional learning and improved student outcomes while undertaking Professional Experience.
Propose and employ research‐based, socially‐just teaching strategies that cater for students with a range of abilities and backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students
Employ a range of assessment strategies, inclusive of moderation, for the purpose of providing feedback on literacy and English learning in a primary classroom

Interpret and discern the content and structures and the Standard/s of the Australian Curriculum: English ‐ and/or other authorised curriculum frameworks ‐ that support the sequencing of content for an English unit
Plan to enact the ongoing teaching of English and literacy in a primary classroom
prerequisites: EDUC3641 - Professional Experience: Year 3 (Primary)

title: Targeted Teaching for Students with Additional Support Needs
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Cultivate an advanced understanding of effective ways teachers design personalised curriculum for students with additional needs Examine general principles of learning, assessment and curriculum design for students with additional support learning needs

This topic will explore ways to create educational programs and lessons to support learning, communication and behaviour for learners with additional support needs. Preservice teachers will integrate theories of learning, assessments and effective teaching strategies in preparing well-designed programs and lessons for use in the classroom.
learning_outcomes: Formulate appropriate objectives, curriculum and research based teaching strategies to support the participation and progress of students with additional support needs
Evaluate data obtained from informal assessment to improve student learning outcomes
Appraise formal and informal assessment tools and strategies
Design an effective research-based learning program for students with additional support needs
Discuss theories of learning which ensure effective teaching and assessment strategies

title: Ecological Assessment and Instruction for Learners with Complex Needs
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop preservice teachers' understanding of the process of instructional programming Develop preservice teachers' understanding of outcomes based, individualised educational programming and planning Prepare preservice teachers for high quality curriculum planning and decision making in the classroom

This topic examines research in the area of curriculum development for individuals with complex learning needs and developmental disabilities. The topic presents literature with a focus on outcomes-based curriculum development from an ecological perspective and how this influences educational programming. Pre-service teachers will have the opportunity to design and develop personalised curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Design outcomes-based educational programming using an individualised functional curriculum for a student with developmental disabilities
Discuss how the characteristics of diverse learners are considered in the design of personalised curriculum development
Prioritise functional adaptive skills which can be embedded within the contextof the general curriculum for an individual student
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC3640, EDUC3641, EDUC3642, EDUC3661

title: Neurodiversity in the Classroom
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
Pre-service teachers will develop professional competence in teaching neurodivergent learners. They will synthesis learning from prior topics to reflect on their learning and translate these into practice, to support neurodivergent learners.

This topic will explore neurodiversity in the classroom. Neurodiversity is about understanding neurological differences among students, not limited to autism, and recognises cognitive variations including for example intellectual disability, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, and dyslexia, among others. Embracing neurodiversity involves creating inclusive environments for all learners to facilitate a strengths-based approach to appreciating neurodiverse learners and their needs.
learning_outcomes: Analyse current research and legislative requirements to cultivate inclusive classrooms
Develop an appreciation of neurodiversity to promote strengths and interest
Promote self-advocacy and advocacy to empower learners to seek a adjustments
Apply knowledge to create flexible teaching methods
prerequisites: 108 units of topics

title: Professional Experience: Year 4 Final Assessment for Registration (Early Childhood)
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Make a meaningful contribution to children's learning and the setting's curriculum goals and priorities that draws from contemporary Australian and international research and practice Evaluate a variety of observation and assessment techniques to gain insight into the types of experiences, activities and ideas that engage young children Analyse, plan, implement, evaluate, and document a curriculum that involves and engages children in deep and meaningful learning over an extended period of time Explore ways to connect with families and the community, and document evidence of developing professional knowledge, practice, and relationships aligned with Teaching Performance Assessments

Professional Experience (Early Childhood): Final Assessment occurs in the final year of the Bachelor of Early Childhood Education degree. 11 single-day visits and a full-time 6-week placement (total 41 days) immerse pre-service teachers in a metropolitan or country early childhood setting. Emphasis is placed on the pre-service teacher’s reflexivity and continuing professional practice. Sustained attention is given to the planning, implementation and evaluation of teaching programs which clearly demonstrate a sound understanding of the complexities of teaching young children. Informed by contemporary Australian and international Early Childhood research and practice. Teaching Performance Assessment tasks which evidence the pre-service teacher’s achievements of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at the Graduate level. At the conclusion of this teaching experience, judgements are made about the pre-service teacher’s readiness to become a registered teacher in the early childhood teaching profession.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate exemplary professional conduct to develop open and honest, collaborative working relationships with children, colleagues, parents, families, and the wider community
Analyse and reflect on teaching decisions and approaches to demonstrate a repertoire of pedagogical strategies built on reflective practice

Plan, implement and evaluate meaningful, innovative curriculum-based experiences that use a range of resources, engage children in deep and meaningful learning and are responsive to their needs and interests
Practice, analyse and moderate an array of accurate, formal, and informal methods of observation and assessment and consistently use these to inform teaching practice
prerequisites: 3 of EDUC3640, EDUC3618, EDUC3622

title: Professional Experience 3: Evidence Informed Practice
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic provides pre-service teachers with an opportunity to demonstrate that they have achieved the Graduate Standard of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers through their Teacher Performance Assessment and final placement report.

This 40-day placement topic is undertaken in a school setting and provides an opportunity for pre-service teachers to teach in their major subject area under the supervision of a mentor teacher/s, to assume an 80% teaching load and demonstrate their ability to undertake the roles and responsibilities of a teacher in an Australian school.
learning_outcomes: Use data and a wide range of evidence-based differentiated teaching, learning and assessment strategies to determine student learning progress
Create a positive, engaging and challenging learning environment for students over an extended time
Critically reflect on and gather evidence of teaching effectiveness against the APST Graduate Standard for all Focus Areas
prerequisites: 2 of EDUC2428, EDUC2320, EDUC2322, EDUC3661, EDUC3642, EDUC3641

title: Extended Rural Professional Experience
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims for pre-service teachers to demonstrate their ability to: Form effective relationships with both the school community and the local community of a regional, rural or remote area Plan appropriate curriculum and teaching materials and adapt their plans for the particular needs of students in a regional, rural or remote area Successfully integrate into the local community in which they are working as a professional Act in ways that show a clear understanding of the professional and ethical requirements of a teacher when they are living and working so closely within a small community

The Extended Rural Professional Experience occurs in the fourth year of the undergraduate degree program or the second year of the Master of Teaching program. It is undertaken con-currently with Professional Experience: Final Assessment for Registration. This combined and Extended Rural Professional Experience begins with the teacher preparation days for Term 1 and working in the school with their mentor teacher for a period of 10-12 days before returning to university for further academic studies. An extended teaching block of 10 weeks begins from Week 1 of Term 2. The pre-service teacher is expected to participate in the life of the rural community and to demonstrate the ability to combine working professionally with engaging personally in a rural community. Together with the required 40 days of teaching practice for the topic Professional Experience: Final Assessment for Registration, this combined professional experience constitutes an expected total of a minimum of 80 days.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate through behaviours a clear understanding of the professional and ethical requirements of a teacher when living and working so closely within a small community
Show your ability to adapt curriculum and teaching plans to the needs of the students of a school in a regional, rural or remote area
Develop effective working relationships with all members of your school community
Establish relationships or friendships within the local regional, rural or remote community
Describe living and working in a regional, rural or remote area for an extended period of time
prerequisites: 1 ^ EDUC4740 1a ^ EDUC4741 1b ^ EDUC4742 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b)) ^ = may be enrolled concurrently

title: Extended Urban Professional Experience
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims for pre-service teachers to demonstrate their ability to: Form and maintain effective working relationships with all members of a school community over an extended period of time Contribute to the extra-curricular activities of the class or school, and Act in ways that show a clear understanding of the professional and ethical requirements of a teacher working with different members of a school community

This topic occurs in the fourth year of the undergraduate degree program. It is undertaken concurrently with EDUC4740 / EDUC4741 / EDUC4742 Professional Experience: Final Assessment for Registration. Develop effective working relationships with all members of your school community and maintain these over an extended period of time

title: The Professional Educator
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to engage pre-service teachers in applied processes that enable the synthesis and evaluation of evidence to justify professional decision making and actions. Document evidence in a personal professional ePortfolio to meet the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers: Graduate Level and/or Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority's National Quality Standards.

The topic is a capstone experience allowing pre-service teachers to draw on learning from topics and professional experience placements, supporting the transition from pre-service teacher to the role of beginning professional educator. Engagement in Community of Practice (CoP) collaborative activities and the creation of an individual ePortfolio will contribute to the transition, clearly demonstrating how the pre-service teacher meets the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at the Graduate Teacher Level. The topic has specific links with the Teaching Performance Assessments (TPAs) 3, 4, and 5; completed during the final professional experience placement and formally assessed and moderated within this capstone topic.
learning_outcomes: Justify evidence of actions that demonstrate the achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers - Graduate Level
Articulate understanding and demonstrate a developing mastery of evidenced-based teaching and learning practices
Identify and evaluate the impact of relevant key issues on teachers, classrooms, teaching and learning
Describe and utilise key features of the process for entering the teaching profession

title: Mathematics Curriculum Specialisation: Developing Curriculum in Context in the Senior Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre-service teachers’ understanding of how senior secondary students learn and how evidence-based pedagogical approaches support conceptual progression and engagement. Build capacity to plan, implement, and evaluate balanced and sequential teaching and learning programs aligned with the curriculum frameworks such as the Australian Curriculum, SACE frameworks. Enable students to synthesise an appropriate teaching and learning program for a subject specialisation in the senior years informed by knowledge of a range of teaching approaches including explicit instruction, modelling, scaffolding, and feedback as key strategies for developing students’ disciplinary understanding and skill mastery. Foster professional confidence, critical reflection, and responsiveness to student diversity in curriculum planning and assessment practice.

This topic prepares pre-service teachers to design, implement, and evaluate evidence-based teaching and learning programs for the senior years of schooling. Drawing on current research into how students learn, pre-service teachers develop disciplinary and pedagogical content knowledge relevant to their subject specialisation. The topic explicitly teaches the use of explicit instruction, modelling, scaffolding, and feedback as core strategies for supporting progression in student understanding. Through engagement with the Australian Curriculum and relevant SACE frameworks, pre-service teachers apply inquiry and design processes to plan balanced and sequential programs that promote student engagement, critical thinking, and achievement in the senior years. They learn to integrate assessment for learning practices and use data to refine teaching and learning decisions. Workshops and collaborative design tasks provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to practise translating curriculum outcomes into meaningful learning experiences, connecting research-informed pedagogy with the diverse learning needs of senior secondary students.
learning_outcomes: Apply curriculum frameworks (Australian Curriculum and SACE) to plan balanced and sequential teaching, learning, and assessment programs that incorporate evidence-based strategies and respond to diverse learner needs
Reflect on professional learning and classroom practice to review teaching effectiveness and identify ways to support equitable outcomes for all learners in the senior years
Explain how senior secondary students learn and describe how evidence-based pedagogical approaches support progression in disciplinary knowledge and skills
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1244 2 1 of EDUC3661, EDUC3642 Must satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Exploring Literacies and Intercultural Contexts in Languages Pedagogy
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop awareness and understanding of the aims of intercultural language teaching and the pedagogical applications possible in modern languages studies for the Primary Years Introduce teaching strategies for encouraging intercultural competence in the languages classroom through the study of the connectedness of language and culture Develop pre-service teachers’ capacity to align curriculum, pedagogy and assessment in the learning area of Languages Develop pre-service teachers’ capacity to evidence their expert content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and plan highly effective classroom teaching and capacity to design an effective sequence of lessons and plan strategies to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of their teaching on student learning Enhance pre-service teachers’ understanding of the assessment, recording and reporting cycle in the Languages curriculum

This topic provides an introduction to the field of literacy in languages and related intercultural contexts, as well as a study of the role of ICT in languages pedagogy in the Primary Years. Pre-service teachers will explore the teaching of genre in the language classroom with a particular focus on contexts of culture and situation. The topic aims to prepare pre-service teachers for the Teaching Performance Assessment. Therefore, pre-service teachers will be expected to demonstrate expert content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and a capacity to design an effective sequence of lessons and plan strategies to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of their teaching on student learning. Pre-service teachers also consider how assessment and moderation is positioned within the languages curriculum in the Primary Years.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critique the key features of intercultural language teaching
Plan strategies to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of your teaching of the Languages curriculum on student learning
Plan for learning and assessment, recording and reporting in the learning area of Languages through well-developed pedagogical reasoning and disciplinary knowledge and skills
Assess, evaluate and report all elements of language teaching
Design and plan units, lessons and tasks incorporating relevant intercultural multimodal teaching and learning strategies
Evaluate lessons with a view to understanding the key features of successful learner centred, text type teaching in languages pedagogy

title: Researching with Young Children
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Introduce pre-service teachers to the concept of researching with young children as differentiated from research on young children Provide pre-service teachers with the skills necessary to conduct a small research project with young children that is of limited scope Examine the particular ethical issues of researching with young children

In Australia and beyond, there is interest in how young children can be included as active participants in research. This topic engages students with these issues by involving them in the design, implementation, analysis and discussion of a small scale research project involving young children. Particular attention is paid to the ethics of research with young children. Strategies for including young children's voice at each stage of the research process are evaluated and trialled.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret data collected using simple qualitative or quantitative methods, drawing appropriate conclusions
Present the findings of the research in an appropriate format
Identify a researchable issue, with a literature review, and design a small-scale research project with young children
Identify and respond to the ethical issues associated with researching with young children when implement a small-scale research project
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 2 EDUC3640 Must Satisfy: (1 and 2)

title: Myth, Magic and Mystery: Psychological Insights into the World of the Child
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Identify the essential elements of story and how the mediums of children's literature, film and story-telling make use of myth, magic and mystery Explore the appeal for children of myth, magic and mystery Develop an understanding of the psychological mechanisms underpinning myth, magic and mystery in everyday life Enhance students' personal growth, sensitivity and confidence in managing student learning, affect and well-being Extrapolate how teachers, clinicians and school counsellors can use myth, magic and mystery to enhance the development, learning and well-being of children

This topic explores the ways in which the mediums of children's literature, film and story-telling can access the psychological world of the child through imagination, affect and thought. Gaining insight into children's psyches, and understanding the power of story to both describe and transform experience, are empowering for the students in this topic. Students are encouraged to look beyond the written word to interpret the elements of story, including symbolism, character and mythology, and understand the mechanisms which can lead to a deeper understanding of the human condition, self-knowledge and transformation. Students will gain insights into how the teacher/ clinician/ counsellor may draw upon these mechanisms to enhance children's learning and development.
learning_outcomes: Use a topic vocabulary appropriately to describe elements of story, aspects of human development and psychology described in this topic
Explain how a critical issue in a child's life can impact on the human condition
Find an example of a quest story and explain its appeal for children
Critically evaluate how story can be used sensitively and therapeutically
Relate the quest motif to key aspects of the child's development

title: Promoting Positive Peer Relations and Wellbeing: Reducing Bullying Amongst Children and Young People
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Provide a basic understanding of friendships and peer relationships amongst children/adolescents Provide opportunities for students to examine their projected image and group participation Provide practical experience of group work procedures for working with children Explore ways in which adults can enhance social skill development Provide opportunities to critically examine social skills programs

The focus of this topic is children's and adolescents' peer group relations at school and intervention programs that can be used by the classroom teacher or school counsellor to understand peer group behaviour and enhance social and emotional development. The topic explores the significance of peer relations to personal development and academic achievement. Emphasis is given to identifying and evaluating practical programs available to reduce peer group problems and promote pro-social behaviour e.g. social skills programs.
learning_outcomes: Identify and present research which increases our understanding of students' peer relations
Enunciate the importance of peer relations for children's development in the classroom context
Critically evaluate a peer relations intervention programme
Use a topic vocabulary appropriately to describe aspects of peer relations, and program management
