title: Creating Calmer Classrooms: A Trauma Sensitive Approach
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to assist preservice teachers to increase their knowledge of trauma sensitive and inclusive pedagogies suitable for vulnerable students. It aims to provide evidence-based guidance from the field about practical ways teachers: Can create safe, welcoming and aesthetic spaces to support student wellbeing and engagement Get on the wavelength of vulnerable and sensitive students through developmentally appropriate expressive and relational activities Connect with families and caregivers Work collaboratively with colleagues Consider their own wellbeing and self-care

This topic offers a trauma-sensitive approach to support early years, primary, secondary and special education teachers to create positive learning environments to enhance the wellbeing of students with trauma backgrounds. Students will have the opportunity to learn about and experience a range of strengths based, solution focused and supportive environmental strategies and activities such as, empathic listening, movement, narrative, therapeutic story writing and telling, sand tray and other sensory, expressive, artistic and movement activities to reduce stress, build resilience and address obstacles to learning, engagement and participation for this group of students. Students will be provided with case study examples to demonstrate how these activities can be supported through creating area of sanctuary, from rooms, to classroom corners in early years, primary, secondary and special education settings.
learning_outcomes: Develop understandings about the challenges faced by vulnerable students, and their parent-caregivers
Apply a chosen approach (for example therapeutic story writing, expressive arts, sandtray, movement) to a case study student relating to current or future setting
Develop awareness of the developmental needs of vulnerable children and young people and their carers or family
Identify a range of strengths based, creative, expressive and non-verbal approaches that can assist young people to communicate and express their feelings safely and appropriately
Develop an understanding of a range of self-care strategies to support the wellbeing of self and colleagues working with vulnerable young people
Identify effective ways to provide calm and welcoming learning and supportive environments in which vulnerable young people can experience safety, belonging, consistency and predictability

title: ICT and Numeracy
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre‐service teachers’ understandings of the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning and teaching Enhance pre‐service teachers’ capacity to integrate ICT and numeracy to expand curriculum learning opportunities for students

This topic is designed to enhance pre‐service teachers’ capacity to effectively integrate information communication technology (ICT) and numeracy across the Australian Curriculum. Pre‐service teachers will be introduced to the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning and teaching. The topic examines numeracy as a fundamental component of learning, how it is related to the broader field of mathematics, and the importance of linking classroom learning to real-world applications. Pre‐service teachers will design curriculum which fosters the development of students' numeracy and digital literacy capabilities.
learning_outcomes: Justify the design of curriculum which effectively integrates numeracy, digital literacy and evidence-based teaching strategies
Explain the relevant issues and the strategies available to support the safe, responsible and ethical use of ICT in learning and teaching
Articulate a critical understanding of numeracy in the community and its application within a curriculum learning area
prerequisites: 1 EDUC2422 2 2 of EDUC2333, EDUC3641 Must Satisfy: ((1) or (2))

title: Numeracy, Assessment and Reporting in the Secondary Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Prepare preservice teachers with contemporary understanding of numeracy and its application in teaching areas Investigate strategies to effectively teach numeracy in secondary schools Critique the purpose and impact of high stakes assessment both in Australia and internationally Interrogate student assessment data and modify teaching to support learning Explore a range of strategies for reporting to students and parents/caregivers Promote the importance of keeping accurate and reliable records of student achievement and develop strategies for clear and ongoing communication with parents/caregivers

This topic will prepare preservice teachers to apply contemporary understanding of numeracy in their teaching. Preservice teachers will critically engage with statistical data and be able to analyze purposes and effects of high stakes assessment. They will learn how to interpret student assessment data and to effectively communicate with students and parents/caregivers.
learning_outcomes: Develop effective strategies for keeping accurate and reliable records of student achievement and to communicate effectively with parents/caregivers
Create effective learning experiences that incorporate numeracy in a learning area
Synthesise research about contemporary numeracy issues in secondary schooling
Critically engage with statistical data and analyse purposes and effects of high stakes assessment
Interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and modify teaching practice.
Formulate a range of strategies for reporting to students and parents/caregivers
prerequisites: 49.5 units of EDUC topics

title: Pedagogies for Writing with Young Children in the Early Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop preservice teachers’ understanding around the complexity of the writing process including milestones in early writing development and the authoring process Promote the importance of pre‐service teachers acknowledging and valuing children’s early writing attempts. Inform and provide opportunities to practise assessing children’s emergent and early writing Support pre‐service teachers to plan for logical, supportive and engaging writing experiences which differentiate by the needs and interests of children Invite pre‐service teachers to evidence their understanding of how to develop children’s voice as writers and their ability to write for purpose and audience

Drawing on from previous early literacy topics, pre‐service teachers are invited to reflect upon the developmental progression of emergent and early writers as they consider how children develop from mark making, scribbling, drawing to conventional writing and print knowledge. Pre-service teachers explore pedagogies that promote children’s voice as writers, authors, the steps involved and the phases that depict this growth. Exploring key theoretical perspectives, practices and experiences important to young children’s writing development, preservice teachers will critically analyse their effectiveness and plan teaching and learning sequences that meet the needs of diverse cohorts. Interpreting datasets such as the AEDC, preservice teachers are asked to consider the importance of home, community and other early childhood settings that enrich and promote purposeful age-appropriate writing experiences.
learning_outcomes: Determine ways to engage with parents, families, colleagues and professional teaching networks
Critically reflect upon writing pedagogies and consider how they may be effective in developing children’s competence and confidence as writers.
Map samples of children’s writing to writing stages of development
Plan teaching and learning sequences which demonstrate deep understanding of the writing and authoring process
Discuss how to support emergent and early writers to craft simple texts
Articulate ways in which children’s writing development may be documented and assessed
prerequisites: 1 of EDUC3658, EDUC3100

title: Pedagogies of Inquiry, Curricula and Children’s Worlds
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Give pre-service teachers the opportunity to evidence their expert content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and highly effective classroom teaching and capacity to impact children’s learning Guide pre-service teachers in how to incorporate documentation and assessment to inform their plan for children’s learning in the area of curriculum specialisation Critically reflect on techniques to differentiate teaching and learning to ensure the engagement and participation of all children Prepare pre-service teachers for the final Professional Experience where they will evidence how they make their expertise as curriculum specialists available to the site through teaching and learning and related professional activities

This topic draws together pre-service teachers’ knowledge of inquiry, curricula and pedagogies in the area of their chosen curriculum specialisation in the Early and Primary Years. They demonstrate expert content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and highly effective classroom teaching and capacity to impact children’s learning through planning effective teaching and learning sequences with children in mind. Pre-service teachers carefully consider how assessment and moderation is positioned within teaching and learning in their curriculum specialisation and explore different ways to capture and document children’s thinking, including the use of digital technologies.
learning_outcomes: Explain reasons for using chosen teaching and learning techniques to effectively differentiate to ensure the engagement and participation of all children in the curriculum

Demonstrate expert knowledge in your curriculum specialisation through planning a progressive sequence of teaching and learning experiences which incorporate deep knowledge of content, discipline specific pedagogy and specialist teaching and learning
Determine areas of further professional growth in the area of curriculum specialisation and how this may be achieved
Justify your choice of assessment methods in the learning process; assessment for learning, assessment as learning and assessment of learning
prerequisites: 1 3 of EDUC1233, EDUC1234, EDUC2328 2 3 of EDUC1240, EDUC1241, EDUC2335 Must Satisfy: ((1) or (2))

title: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Education
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre‐service teachers’ understanding of the conceptual connections within and between the Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines Develop pre‐service teachers’ capacity to contribute to the design and provision of high‐quality STEM education Prepare pre‐service teachers to demonstrate highly effective classroom teaching of STEM education and understand, evaluate and improve their impact on student learning

This topic develops pre‐service teachers’ capacity to contribute to the design and provision of high‐quality Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education in the Primary Years of schooling. Pre‐service teachers examine the knowledge and skills that the different STEM disciplines bring and work across disciplinary boundaries to actively create cross‐curriculum links. Emphasis is placed on designing learning opportunities for primary school children and young people which builds their knowledge and curiosity about STEM concepts and their capacity to solve problems through harnessing and manipulating the world around them. This topic is designed to prepare pre‐service teachers to demonstrate highly effective classroom teaching of STEM education and understand, evaluate and improve their impact on children and young people's learning.
learning_outcomes: Explain the rationale underpinning your approach to STEM education

Plan a STEM learning curriculum integrating interdisciplinary concepts, real-world applications, inquiry-based methods, evidence-based teaching strategies, collaborative learning, and ongoing assessment strategies to ensure student engagement and achievement
Plan strategies to evidence, assess and enhance the impact of your teaching of STEM curriculum on primary school children and young people.

Identify pedagogical strategies that promote quality engagement and retention appropriate to specific groups of learners who are currently less likely to engage in STEM education and are at higher risk of not developing high capabilities in STEM‐related skills
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDPRBA-Bachelor of Education (Primary), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into BAMTPR-Bachelor of Arts, Master of Teaching (Primary) 1b Admission into BAMTSP-Bachelor of Arts conditional entry to Master of Teaching (Primary) 1c Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 2 1 of NMCY1001, NMCY1201, INNO1001, INNO1201 3 2 of EDUC2203, EDUC3624 4 Admission into BEDSHPE-Bachelor of Education (Secondary Health and Physical Education) 5 2 of BIOL1101, CHEM1010 6 1 of EASC1101, PHYS1101, PHYS1701 Must Satisfy: (((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c) and 2 and 3) or (4 and 5 and 6))

title: Teaching and Learning through Arts Based Pedagogies
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre‐service teachers’ capacity to align curriculum, pedagogy and assessment in Expressive Arts Develop pre‐service teachers’ capacity to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of their teaching on student learning in the Expressive Arts Enhance pre‐service teachers’ understanding of the assessment, recording and reporting cycle in the Expressive Arts curriculum Enhance pre‐service teachers’ understanding of assessment moderation and its application to support consistent and comparable judgements of student learnings relevant to the Expressive Arts curriculum

This prepares pre‐service teachers for the Teaching Performance Assessment focused on the Expressive Arts. By completing this topic pre‐service teachers gain expert content knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge and a capacity to design an effective sequence of lessons and plan strategies to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of their teaching on student learning. The topic also introduces pre‐service teachers to ways in which assessment and moderation is positioned within the Expressive Arts curriculum in the Primary Years.
learning_outcomes: Justify strategies to providing timely and appropriate feedback to students about their learning in the Expressive Arts
Plan strategies to evidence, evaluate and improve the impact of your teaching of the Expressive Arts on student learning
Justify the use of teaching and learning techniques to effectively differentiate the Expressive Arts curriculum to ensure the engagement and participation of all students
Evaluate your professional learning needs and identify appropriate sources of professional learning relevant to the Expressive Arts
Plan for learning and assessment, recording and reporting in the Expressive Arts supported by well‐developed pedagogical reasoning and disciplinary knowledge and skills
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDPR-Bachelor of Education (Primary) 1a Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 1 b Admission into BEDSEC Bachelor of Education (Secondary) 2 2 of EDUC2332, VISA1401 3 1 of DRAM1002, VISA1402 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b) and 2 and 3)

title: Working with Families and Professionals
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Explore the concept of family, the application of a systems theory approach and the value of a social ecological model in relation to families with a child living with a disability Examine the impact of having a child living with a disability on family members, family functioning, and life‐stage transitions Examine the Indigenous and multicultural variables associated with parenting a child living with a disability Examine the family support needs and the role of professionals in meeting these needs, within the context of a developing professional partnership Explore evidence‐informed research on high‐quality family and professional partnerships

This topic engages preservice teachers in developing their knowledge of family functioning, developmental stages of families and the issues of influence on families with a child living with a disability. Issues including grief, empowerment, transition across different life stages, cultural diversity and working with professionals will be addressed. Preservice teachers are supported to develop skills to effectively engage with and support families as they transition across stages in parenting a child living with a disability. Preservice teachers will also develop understanding of roles of professionals in working with families with a child living with a disability and in working within interdisciplinary professional teams.
learning_outcomes: Formulate approaches to engage with other professionals and professional networks to ensure access to relevant support services and resources for self and families with a child living with a disability

Appraise ethical and legal issues associated with working in partnership with families, in particular indigenous and/or culturally diverse families to develop personal principles for professional practice

Integrate the principles of effective professional partnerships in working with families with a child living with a disability and other professionals to effectively engage parents in a site‐based education program
Critically evaluate evidence‐informed research to support effective transition planning for families with a child living with a disability
Apply a systems theory approach in designing a family/professional partnership plan designed to support enhanced outcomes for a child or young person living with a disability
prerequisites: 72 units of EDUC topics

title: Respectful Teaching With Infants And Toddlers
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Stimulate students to question the purposes and possibilities of respectful teaching approaches with very young children Support students to consider how to observe for, shape & implement a high quality curriculum for infants and toddlers Provide students with opportunities to apply their developing knowledge and understanding of infant/toddler curricula

Respectful teaching involves the careful consideration of what very young children do as they relate to and seek to discover more about the people and the world around them. Focusing on the role that attachment and attunement play in early learning and development, this topic encourages pre-service teachers to explore contemporary and international perspectives on the foundational elements of high-quality curricula for very young children. The reciprocal nature of the educator-child relationship will be of key consideration, using observation, reflection and planning techniques to question: what does it mean to teach infants and toddlers? Pre-service teachers will have the opportunity to study first-hand how to shape engaging and supportive educative care programs for very young children through 16-days of professional experience in a birth-2 setting. This elective topic involves placement visits Monday-Thursday, and a workshop on Friday, for 4-weeks. This supports pre-service teachers to complete the ACECQA accreditation requirement of a minimum of 10-days placement in Birth-2.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and effectively support the socio-emotional, intellectual and physical needs, creativities and curiosities of infants and toddlers, in light of their familial, cultural and community contexts
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the role that the educator-child relationship plays in very young childrens learning and development
Rationalise how curriculum for very young children is distinct from curricula for children over 3 years, noting parallels with the students own teaching philosophy and that of the early years sectors
prerequisites: 1 Admission into BEDECBA-Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood), Bachelor of Arts 1a Admission into BEDECSEBDS-B Education (Early Childhood & Special Ed), B Disability Studies 1b Admission into MTEC-Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) 1c Admission into BECE-Bachelor of Early Childhood Education - Birth to 8 2 1 of EDUC1221, EDUC9222 3 1 of EDUC1238, EDUC2421 Must Satisfy: ((1 or 1a or 1b or 1c) and 2) and (3)

title: Business Curriculum Specialisation: Developing Curriculum in Context in the Senior Years
school: College of Education, Psychology and Social Work
syllabus_overview:
This topic aims to: Develop pre-service teachers’ understanding of how senior secondary students learn and how evidence-based pedagogical approaches support conceptual progression and engagement. Build capacity to plan, implement, and evaluate balanced and sequential teaching and learning programs aligned with the curriculum frameworks such as the Australian Curriculum, SACE frameworks. Enable students to synthesise an appropriate teaching and learning program for a subject specialisation in the senior years informed by knowledge of a range of teaching approaches including explicit instruction, modelling, scaffolding, and feedback as key strategies for developing students’ disciplinary understanding and skill mastery. Foster professional confidence, critical reflection, and responsiveness to student diversity in curriculum planning and assessment practice.

This topic prepares pre-service teachers to design, implement, and evaluate evidence-based teaching and learning programs for the senior years of schooling. Drawing on current research into how students learn, pre-service teachers develop disciplinary and pedagogical content knowledge relevant to their subject specialisation. The topic explicitly teaches the use of explicit instruction, modelling, scaffolding, and feedback as core strategies for supporting progression in student understanding. Through engagement with the Australian Curriculum and relevant SACE frameworks, pre-service teachers apply inquiry and design processes to plan balanced and sequential programs that promote student engagement, critical thinking, and achievement in the senior years. They learn to integrate assessment for learning practices and use data to refine teaching and learning decisions. Workshops and collaborative design tasks provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to practise translating curriculum outcomes into meaningful learning experiences, connecting research-informed pedagogy with the diverse learning needs of senior secondary students.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on professional learning and classroom practice to review teaching effectiveness and identify ways to support equitable outcomes for all learners in the senior years
Explain how senior secondary students learn and describe how evidence-based pedagogical approaches support progression in disciplinary knowledge and skills

Apply curriculum frameworks (Australian Curriculum and SACE) to plan balanced and sequential teaching, learning, and assessment programs that incorporate evidence-based strategies and respond to diverse learner needs
prerequisites: 1 EDUC1244 2 1 of EDUC3661, EDUC3642 Must satisfy: (1 and 2)
